structure.background:
### Early Life

Cithria was born in the village of [Cloudfield](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Cloudfield "Universe:Cloudfield"). A dedicated and honest girl, she often played [tellstones](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tellstones "Universe:Tellstones") with her father, eventually surpassing his skill.[[2]](#cite_note-KingsGambit-2) During her younger years she took part in the Yellow Spring Festival of Cloudfield as a flower bearer.[[3]](#cite_note-Weight-3)

When Cithria was young, her mother told her stories of the Demacia's greatest heroes, and felt a personal calling to protect the country. Once she was old enough, she set off to start her own adventure, traveling to the [Great City of Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia") to enlist and hopefully join the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard").[[5]](#cite_note-LorCloudfield-5)

In her first year as a recruit, Cithria proved herself to be a capable soldier, and she was stationed at the East Wall under the Ninth Battalion of Captain Eldran.[[3]](#cite_note-Weight-3) She would experience things most of her squadmates could not stomach, things that would harden her resolve to protect Demacia and her people as best as she could.[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4)

### Crisis in Meltridge

:   *Main article: [Turmoil](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Turmoil "Universe:Turmoil")*

One month after the escape of  [Sylas](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sylas "Universe:Sylas") and the death of  [King Jarvan III](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_III "Universe:Jarvan III"), and just one year after she had been recruited, Cithria and a detachment from her battalion were sent to the [Graygate](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Graygate "Universe:The Graygate") on the far eastern border of  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"). Many of her comrades, including a man named Bakker, believed they should be in the [capital](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia") fighting the [Great Mage Rebellion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Great_Mage_Rebellion "Universe:Great Mage Rebellion"). Although Cithria had been raised to fear [magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic"), and to an extent agreed that they should be fighting Sylas, she was also unnerved by Bakker's hatred for all mages, which he expressed vocally to the others. Shield-Sergeant Gunthar informed his soldiers they were to escort an important envoy from the [Arbormark](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Arbormark "Universe:Arbormark") to the Demacian capital. The diplomat, a massive and jovial man named Arjen, was a mage, and in accordance with the Laws of Stone he was allowed within Demacian borders so long as he did not use any magic. A pair of  [mageseekers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mageseekers "Universe:Mageseekers")—Senior Adept Cadstone and his associate Arno—were tasked with accompanying Arjen at all times to hold him to his word.[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4)

During the three-hour march to [Meltridge](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Meltridge "Universe:Meltridge"), Cithria grew fond of Arjen's affable nature, despite her instincts telling her he might be dangerous. Eventually, her curiosity got the better of her and she asked him why the Arbormark would send a mage to Demacia, at a time when tensions were high and mages were in open rebellion. Arjen replied that as chief advisor to the Lord of the Arbormark, and as a mage himself, he was here to offer a unique perspective that could aid Demacia given the challenges it currently faced.[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4)

When the escort reached Meltridge, Cithria quickly sensed a tense atmosphere, as the townspeople were giving them dirty looks, spitting and throwing rocks at them. The soldiers assumed this was because the man they were escorting was a mage, and they tightened ranks to ensure he and the mageseekers could get through the town safely. The situation escalated quickly as the townspeople barricaded the street with wagons, blocking their path. Not wanting to harm the civilians, but also unwilling to hand over the envoy, Cithria suggested that Arjen and the mageseekers escape through a barred-up storefront. Gunthar held the line with a shieldwall, and Cithria broke the door open with the help of Bakker, who believed it would be better to just hand the mage over.[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4)

As they exited the candle shop's back door, they found the alleyway blocked by a visibly distraught woman named Rosalyn, who was armed with a crossbow. Under threat of being shot, Cithria reasoned that she could not allow an allied envoy to be killed on Demacian soil. But Rosalyn declared the man she wanted to kill was not Arjen, but Seeker Cadstone, who had arrested her young daughter Kyra after she had stepped forward and registered herself as a mage to the authorities. Although Kyra's abilities were benign, Cadstone said he had no choice but to arrest Kyra after the law was amended, which ordered the arrest of all the kingdom's mages. Cithria sympathized with Rosalyn and diffused the standoff by comforting her, saying that if Kyra returned home, she would need her mother to be there, and becoming a murderer would prevent any possible reunion. Cithria promised to help find Rosalyn's daughter, and she finally lowered the crossbow. The weapon misfired, and the bolt would have killed Bakker had Arjen not intervened with a small magical shield. The mageseekers did not notice what Arjen had done, and Cithria and Bakker did not report him. Cadstone also did not arrest Rosalyn, claiming as there was no magic performed, the matter fell outside their jurisdiction.[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4)

Upon returning to the main road, Rosalyn urged her fellow townspeople to stand down, saying it was not what Kyra would have wanted. The mob dispersed, and the people went home. Sergeant Gunthar was not sure what Cithria had done, but recognized it was her action that ended the crisis. Cithria did not feel a sense of victory though, having learned how easy it was for well-intentioned Demacians to turn against one another, and having gained a new perspective on the difficult time her homeland now found itself in.[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4)

### Dauntless Vanguard Trials

:   *Main article: [The Weight of Expectations](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Weight_of_Expectations "Universe:The Weight of Expectations")*

At some point after returning to the [capital](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia") from the East Wall, Cithria earned recognition as an outstanding soldier, and after receiving a letter of invitation from Sword-Captain  [Garen Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen"),[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1) she was allowed to undergo the necessary trials to join the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard"). Her Testing was overseen by Proctor-Corporal Pell, and it was a grueling process. On the Testing Grounds, Cithria was made to do training exercises while carrying a backpack of stones equal to half her own weight, each one signed by one of her comrades in the Ninth Battalion. The weight of these stones exhausted Cithria, but knowing they each represented a friend of hers gave Cithria the strength not to lose a single one.[[3]](#cite_note-Weight-3)

Two weeks after the Testing began, Corporal Pell allowed Cithria a meal break, after she had spent several hours of manual labor digging a trench. As Cithria got food at the messfield, she saw a crowd of Vanguard soldiers gathered for a [tellstones](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tellstones "Universe:Tellstones") tournament. A 2 [war chef](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:War_Chefs "LoR:War Chefs") beat a young 4 [raptor-scout](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Silverwing_Diver "LoR:Silverwing Diver"), after which a woman with a scar on her cheek played against a soldier named Bunder. Cithria quickly realized the tellstones they were playing was not the version she was used to; it was faster, and no words were exchanged between opponents as they were making their moves. As she was still trying to decipher what they were doing, the woman knocked on the stump they were playing on. Bunder appeared angry for a moment, then abruptly conceded the match without a word.[[3]](#cite_note-Weight-3)

After the match had finished, Proctor-Corporal Pell instructed Cithria that as part of her Testing, she should play a game as well. Her opponent was  [Shield-Sergeant Merrek](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Merrek "Universe:Merrek"), the long-time mentor and second-in-command of Garen. Cithria, having heard of Merrek's feats and reputation, felt out of her element against her opponent, but was determined not to fail in front of him. Before the match, Merrek led her through the rules of "Silent Stones," the version of the game played by the Vanguard. Gradually Cithria familiarized herself with the rules and also became more comfortable with Merrek, who made conversation about her background and her hometown of [Cloudfield](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Cloudfield "Universe:Cloudfield").[[3]](#cite_note-Weight-3)

Right before they began, Merrek promised not to go easy on Cithria, as he knew she was the four-time tellstones champion of the Ninth Battalion. Cithria played well, and many among the crowd of onlookers began to root for her, attempting to distract Merrek with various questions, reports, and nonsensical strings of words. As they reached their final moves, Cithria mustered the courage to respond to Merrek's boast. She correctly named five of the seven face-down stones, but ended up losing a 50-50 when guessing the order of the final two. Cithria was crestfallen at having lost their match, but learned a great deal about tactics, strategy, and what it meant to be a Vanguard. Merrek was very impressed by Cithria's courage, and said he looked forward to their next game.[[3]](#cite_note-Weight-3)

### Cithria, Vanguard Squire

At some point in her military career, Cithria *may* have served as a squire to a member of the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard").[[6]](#cite_note-Canonicity-6) She may have also been part of a Demacian [expedition](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Future_Events#Demacian_Shadow_Isles_Expedition "Universe:Future Events") to the  [Shadow Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shadow_Isles "Universe:Shadow Isles").

### Expedition to the Nockmirch

:   *Main article: [Garen: First Shield](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen:_First_Shield "Universe:Garen: First Shield")*

Due to the death of Helmar of the First Shield, Cithria was recruited straight into the First Shield of the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard") from the Testing Grounds, where she would serve directly under  [Merrek's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Merrek "Universe:Merrek") command. Her test scores were as high as those of  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen") himself, and very soon she was brought to meet the famed sword-captain. Garen had heard of Cithria's [action](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Turmoil "Universe:Turmoil") in [Meltridge](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Meltridge "Universe:Meltridge") and remarked that he was impressed. Cithria was awestruck to have received a compliment from him.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

Among the First Shield, Cithria's comrades were Sergeant Merrek, the Stonehorn [minotaur](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Minotaur "Universe:Minotaur") Kriel, master swordswoman Alys Morn, the affable Aiguo, the surly Eben Hess, and the twins Saskya and Rurik Vos. Each member of the Dauntless Vanguard was a hero in their own right, and as their newest and youngest member, Cithria struggled to feel like she belonged. For her first mission, Cithria accompanied Garen and the First, Fourth, and Eighth Shields on a diplomatic expedition to the [Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Nockmirch "Universe:Nockmirch"), an allied nation in central  [Valoran](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Valoran "Universe:Valoran"), where they were to meet with the  [Demacian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") ambassador, Hargold Crownguard. They took a falcon-ship caled the *Stormbright* south along the [Ironfork River](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ironfork_River "Universe:Ironfork River"), into the [Bay of Sentinels](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Bay_of_Sentinels "Universe:Bay of Sentinels"), and finally eastward along the [Silverrun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Silverrun_River "Universe:Silverrun River"), taking shifts rowing for a few days until they reached the Demacian border at the [Custodian Wall](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Custodian_Wall "Universe:Custodian Wall").[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

Along the journey, the *Stormbright* passed [Everpeak](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Everpeak "Universe:Everpeak"), and Cithria was amazed as she saw the citadel and its 4 [raptor-knights](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Silverwing_Vanguard "LoR:Silverwing Vanguard") upon [silverwings](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Silverwing "Universe:Silverwing"), which were far more majestic than she had imagined from her father's stories. As she stared at the Everpeak, Kriel told her the history of its construction under King Argostan, and how it had been built by the master stonemasons of the minotaurs. Shortly after this, their expedition was joined by  [ranger-knight](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacian_Rangers "Universe:Demacian Rangers")  [Quinn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Quinn "Universe:Quinn"), [sent](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shield_of_Remembrance "Universe:Shield of Remembrance") by  [Tianna Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tianna "Universe:Tianna") to join them. Upon leaving Demacian borders, Quinn's knowledge would be relied on for traveling through the border countries to [Alderburg](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Alderburg "Universe:Alderburg"), and they eventually disembarked and made camp to plan their route.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

When she was trying to sleep that night, Cithria overheard Merrek and Alys Morn speaking about her. Alys Morn, whom Cithria idolized as a personal hero, believed their new recruit would be unable to fill the shoes of a veteran like Helmar. Cithria was completely heartbroken to hear this, and even though Merrek told Morn that Cithria would surpass her expectations, she was unable to fall back asleep for the rest of that night.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

When the Vanguard reached the ravine between the [Rijenland](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rijenland "Universe:Rijenland"), they were all surprised to see an enormous bridge had been built—one which had not been mentioned at all by the Demacian ambassador to the region. Wary of its recent construction, but still formally allies with the Nockmirch, the Vanguard crossed the bridge and was allowed to enter by the Warden Vigrid, who invited the Vanguard's senior members to a banquet of welcome on behalf of Lord Castellan Eldwyn. Cithria, Eben Hess, and the Vos twins were sent to the barracks. A young Nockmirch soldier came to provide them refreshments, but Hess, feeling irritable and on edge as usual, threatened him, causing him to drop everything. Cithria attempted to help the Nockmircher clean up, but he ran away, still startled by Hess.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

Later, Cithria and the other Vanguard were alerted by bells—a battle had begun, with the Nockmirchers attacking the Demacians and a  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") warhost marching on the city. The Lord of the Nockmirch had betrayed his alliance with Demacia and instead aligned himself with Noxus. Cithria rushed to regroup with the First Shield and slew a Nockmirch soldier, whom she recognized as the boy from the barracks. The Vanguard made to escape the city across the Nockmirch bridge, with Quinn and her [azurite eagle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Azurite_Eagle "Universe:Azurite Eagle")  [Valor](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Valor "Universe:Valor") going ahead of them to open the gatehouse and send word back to Demacia. The Vanguard saw Valor flying west, but the portcullis closed shut before they could cross, trapping them on the bridge.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

With no route of escape, the Vanguard resolved to make a last stand on the bridge so as to buy Quinn enough time to get back to Demacia and prevent a Noxian invasion. Warden Vigrid, who had secretly been a Noxian, sent wave after wave of his warriors to break their formation, each one stronger than the last. Under the cover of night, the Vigrid's archers launched a surprise volley of arrows at the Demacians. Cithria noticed the attack and warned her comrades, saving a majority of them. Cithria lost several comrades during this battle, including Rurik Vos and Aiguo. The wave after this was led by a chieftain riding a [basilisk](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Basilisk "Universe:Basilisk"), a massive and monstrous creature which moved at alarming speed. As it charged forward, Cithria froze and had to be saved by Eben Hess, who took the blow for her.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

After the basilisk and its rider had fallen, Cithria and her comrades went to treat the wounded. Hess's ribs had been broken, and despite hating him, she felt guilty for letting him down. Luckily, Hess's life being saved by a large amount of gold he had taken from Nockmirchers while playing [tellstones](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tellstones "Universe:Tellstones"). Alys Morn, irritated by Hess, took the gold and split it between herself and Cithria, calling it a medical fee. Cithria and Morn also saw that Quinn had not made it out safely after all, having been gravely wounded by an arrow on top of the gate tower. She assisted Morn by cutting her cloak into bandages for the ranger-knight, and was subsequently sent by Merrek to scout out the enemy formation.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

Just before dawn, Cithria returned to Merrek and Garen and delivered the intelligence: the  [elite soldiers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Trifarian_Legion "Universe:Trifarian Legion") of Noxus were gathering to launch a final offensive against the Demacians at sunrise. Vigrid had also left his tower and was arguing with his commanders, believing it would be better to attack right away. After hearing this, Garen declared that with Vigrid out in the open, the Demacians would launch their counteroffensive and kill the enemy leader once and for all. The Vanguard charged through the fog, with Cithria feeling elated and fearless now that they were finally striking back. As they met the Noxians, Cithria's reflexes and speed with her blade surprised even Garen. After Vigrid had been slain by Garen, Valor returned with Demacian 4 [raptor-knights](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Silverwing_Vanguard "LoR:Silverwing Vanguard") as reinforcements, who finally forced the remaining Noxians to retreat.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

With the battle finally over, Cithria mourned for a slain silverwing raptor, taking a feather to remember it by. The Nockmirchers, including Lord Eldwyn and his daughter Odelyn, had all surrendered after the Noxians left. Garen was to decide their fate, and though much of the blame rested on a  [sorcerer](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:LeBlanc "Universe:LeBlanc") who had impersonated Ambassador Hargold and prevented communication between the two allies, Eldwyn had knowingly broken his alliance with Demacia. Odelyn pleaded that he spare the soldiers, as they did not share her father's guilt as the one responsible for the bloodshed. Garen prepared to execute Eldwyn, but after consulting Cithria, he decided on mercy so as not to destroy how Demacia's other allies viewed them. Eldwyn would have to abdicate his position to his daughter, and Demacia would promise to strengthen the Nockmirch against any threat of Noxian invasion. As they were leaving, Eben Hess confronted Cithria, demanding she return his gold. Alys Morn stood up for her, then acknowledged that she may have misjudged Cithria in thinking she was not ready.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

When the Vanguard returned to the Great City, Cithria was greeted with a heroes' welcome, but felt no comfort in the parade after witnessing so much pain and death on the expedition. She spoke with Sergeant Merrek on the same training ground where she had first met Garen, sharpening her sword with a whetstone. Merrek had delivered Cithria a gift from Kriel: a small wooden carving of a silverwing raptor. Cithria loved the raptor and promised to treasure it, but was still bothered by when she had frozen against the basilisk and had to be saved by Hess. After Merrek complimented her, she confessed everything to her sergeant, expecting him to be disappointed. Instead, Merrek said that as a Vanguard, it was only right that Cithria and her comrades protect one another, and that as one of them, she was unlikely to make the same mistake twice. Merrek's words lifted Cithria's spirits and helped convince her that the First Shield was where she truly belonged.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

### Cithria the Bold

In the future, Cithria *may* prove herself in the Dauntless Vanguard until she earns the title **Cithria the Bold**.[[6]](#cite_note-Canonicity-6)

### Cithria, Lady of Clouds

In another timeline, Cithria has become a legendary warmaster in Demacia, leading her Silverwings to the rescue of Prince  [Jarvan IV](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_IV "Universe:Jarvan IV").
structure.appearance:
Cithria has pale skin and dark brown hair, tied into a long ponytail. She wears a brown tunic and pants, and carries with her a sword with a Silverwing feather.

As one of the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard"), Cithria wore the typical armored uniform of the  [Demacian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") army, silver with the Vanguard's signature blue cloak, and a significantly longer, braided ponytail. During the [expedition to the Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen:_First_Shield "Universe:Garen: First Shield"), Cithria received a large cut across her left cheek from their battle against  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"). As a veteran soldier, she would acquire several more battle scars, with at least three of them running in parallel across the left side of her face.

As a Warmaster and silverwing rider, Cithria appeared with more embellished armor with gold accents resembling feathers or scales.
structure.personality:
Cithria has a plucky and strong-willed personality, reflecting her personality as a new recruit for the Demacian army. She can be a bit timid at times, especially when encountering figures she idolizes, such as Garen and Jarvan IV, or when encountering dangerous scenarios. However, her personality is ultimately courageous, ready to face encounters that come her way.

In later renditions, Cithria may become more confident in her roles as a soldier; her personality may become more confident and bold, fitting her evolution as she experiences accumulate.
structure.abilities:
- **Soldier:** Since her early days as a recruit, Cithria has proven herself to be a capable soldier, resilient on the battlefield and committed to protecting  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") and its people.[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4) Her role in quelling the [turmoil](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Turmoil "Universe:Turmoil") in [Meltridge](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Meltridge "Universe:Meltridge") did not go unnoticed by  [Garen Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen"), and within a few months she earned a spot in the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard"). Cithria's notable skills on the battlefield are her swordsmanship and her speed, which impressed the sword-captain. Her awareness of and quick reactions to incoming strikes and projectiles has saved multiple lives, including Garen and the other Vanguard,[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1) and the envoy from the [Arbormark](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Arbormark "Universe:Arbormark").[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4)
- **Diplomacy:** Although she is not officially a diplomat, Cithria has a keen awareness of interpersonal relationships which has diffused multiple brewing conflicts facing  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"). Her negotiation with Rosalyn and understanding of her plight ended the crisis in [Meltridge](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Meltridge "Universe:Meltridge"),[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4) and her counsel to  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen") when deciding Lord Eldwyn's punishment was deemed wise foresight to preserve Demacia's image among their allies.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)
- **[Tellstones](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tellstones "Universe:Tellstones"):** When she was a child, Cithria would play games of King's Gambit against her father, who taught her it was not a game of memorization, but of knowing one's opponent and their weaknesses.[[2]](#cite_note-KingsGambit-2) After practicing in countless games, Cithria surpassed her father's skill in the game, and after she became a soldier, she won the championships of four tellstones tournaments among the Ninth Battalion.[[3]](#cite_note-Weight-3)

relations.relationship_description:
Some time after Cithria's [action](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Turmoil "Universe:Turmoil") in [Meltridge](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Meltridge "Universe:Meltridge"), in which she prevented an uprising in the city during the [Great Mage Rebellion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Great_Mage_Rebellion "Universe:Great Mage Rebellion"), Garen recognized her potential and wrote a letter inviting her to undertake the Testing, a grueling month-long evaluation which would allow her to join the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard"). He kept a close eye on Cithria's progress, and she ended up passing the examination with scores comparable to Garen's own. As part of the Vanguard, Cithria agreed with the common consensus that Garen was an excellent commander, who put the lives of his subordinates and his countrymen above upholding tradition or appeasing his superiors.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

Cithria and Garen's first mission together was the [expedition to the Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen:_First_Shield "Universe:Garen: First Shield"), in which they and the other soldiers held the line at [Alderburg](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Alderburg "Universe:Alderburg") against forces of  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"). During this time, Cithria came to understand the human side of Garen, recognizing loneliness and vulnerability behind the mask of the legendary sword-captain. Garen was impressed with Cithria's fearlessness and speed during the battle, and when making his decision whether or not to execute Lord Eldwyn, it was her counsel he requested and heeded on how to best administer justice for all the lives lost.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

Cithria met Quinn during the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard")'s [expedition to the Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen:_First_Shield "Universe:Garen: First Shield"), where the  [ranger-knight](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacian_Rangers "Universe:Demacian Rangers") was to serve as their navigator through the border nations of central  [Valoran](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Valoran "Universe:Valoran"). Later on, after they learned the [Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Nockmirch "Universe:Nockmirch") had betrayed  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"), Cithria and the other Vanguard held the line on the Nockmirch bridge to buy Quinn enough time to escape and get word back to Demacia. They would learn hours later that Quinn had been severely wounded by a crossbow on top of the gatehouse, and Cithria helped Alys Morn give medical assistance to Quinn by making bandages from her cloak. After the battle was won, they brought Quinn back safely to the [capital](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia"), where she immediately left as soon as she was strong enough to move on her own.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

Cithria met Sergeant Merrek on the Testing Grounds, where he evaluated her character and sense of courage during a game of [King's Gambit](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tellstones "Universe:Tellstones"). Cithria had never played "Silent Stones" before, and as they were playing, Merrek asked her many questions about the game, its unique rules, and why she thought the Vanguard played that way. Cithria was intimidated by Merrek's reputation, but was also determined not to lose against him, which made her eventual loss all the more upsetting. Despite this, Merrek had gotten to know Cithria very well from their conversation and believed she would be a fine addition to the Dauntless Vanguard's ranks.[[3]](#cite_note-Weight-3)

Due to the death of Helmar of First Shield, Cithria was brought directly under Merrek's command for the [expedition to the Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen:_First_Shield "Universe:Garen: First Shield"). On the journey, Cithria overheard a conversation between Merrek and Alys Morn, where the latter believed Cithria was too inexperienced to fill Helmar's shoes. Merrek, however, had no such doubts about Cithria and believed she would surprise Morn. During the battle at [Alderburg](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Alderburg "Universe:Alderburg"), Merrek trusted Cithria with tasks such as reconnaissance, where she gathered intelligence on the  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") formation before they made their last stand. Merrek and Cithria both made it back to the [Great City of Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia") after the battle was won. They spoke together on the training grounds after Merrek delivered Kriel's gift to her, and though Cithria believed she had failed her comrades at Alderburg by freezing against a [basilisk](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Basilisk "Universe:Basilisk"), Merrek reassured her that there was no shame in having her life saved, and that the Vanguard was lucky to have her. Merrek's stubborn belief in Cithria, along with her unwillingness to argue with her superior officer, helped convince her that she truly belonged among the Dauntless Vanguard.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

As a child, Cithria heard stories of the Dauntless Vanguard and had always dreamed to join their ranks as a hero of  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"), where she could wear their signature blue cloak and protect the kingdom's people. She respected and even idolized several of their members, including  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen"),  [Merrek](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Merrek "Universe:Merrek"), and Alys Morn. Upon joining their ranks, Cithria befriended Kriel, a [minotaur](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Minotaur "Universe:Minotaur") of the Stonehorn clan who taught her the history of the [Everpeak](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Everpeak "Universe:Everpeak"), a citadel renowned for its [silverwing](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Silverwing "Universe:Silverwing") riders, and after seeing her admiration for them he carved a small wooden raptor for her as a gift. She got to know many of them as individuals, seeking to prove herself to veterans like Alys Morn, and forming a distaste for Eben Hess, a skilled soldier with an irritable nature. Cithria also lost several new comrades in the battle, including Aiguo, who was killed by a stray arrow. Upon returning from [Alderburg](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Alderburg "Universe:Alderburg"), Cithria earned the respect of Alys Morn, who had initially believed Cithria was not ready. Cithria also felt she had gained a new perspective on the group she had once idolized, now seeing glory and parades as empty compared to the sacrifices of the fallen and their sworn duty to the kingdom.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

Cithria's first encounter against Noxus was during the battle at [Alderburg](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Alderburg "Universe:Alderburg"), after the [Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Nockmirch "Universe:Nockmirch") had secretly allied themselves with the empire and trapped them on the bridge over the [ravine](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Gray_Claws "Universe:Gray Claws"). She regarded the disorganized ranks of warriors as fearsome and barbaric, and believed they were disrespectful to their own dead in tossing the corpses unceremoniously off a cliff.[[1]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-1)

In her first year as a recruit for the  [Demacian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") army, Cithria was part of a detachment tasked with escorting an envoy from the [Arbormark](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Arbormark "Universe:Arbormark"). This envoy, a massive and jovial man named Arjen, happened to be a mage. The other soldiers and  [mageseekers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mageseekers "Universe:Mageseekers") in their escort regarded Arjen with suspicion, but Cithria's doubts about him were gradually assuaged by the stories and jokes he told along the journey. She was eventually brave enough to make conversation with Arjen, and at [Meltridge](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Meltridge "Universe:Meltridge"), Cithria saved his life from the chaos of the riot and tried to help him escape. To save one of Cithria's comrades, Arjen was forced to use his magic, even though this was forbidden by Demacian law. The mageseekers did not notice what he had done, and Cithria kept quiet so he would not be arrested.[[4]](#cite_note-Turmoil-4)

structure.name: Kindred
structure.quote: *"Tell me again, little  Lamb, which things are ours to take?"*
structure.background:
### Origin

:   *Main article: [Listen to Their Tale](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Listen_to_Their_Tale "Universe:Listen to Their Tale")*

Tales of the [spirit god](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Spirit_God "Universe:Spirit God") known as the Kindred go back millennia, making it difficult to determine their true origin. Some of the earliest legends tell the story of 'a pale man with dark hair' who was very lonely, as all things would have to meet this man at the hour of their death. For this the people shunned him, so the lonely man took an axe and split himself in two so he 'would always have a friend'. According to the legend, these two halves became the  Lamb and the  Wolf, the eternal companions who would stalk the continent and hunt all things. Forever separate, yet together always, they worked as one to shepherd the souls of  [Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Runeterra "Universe:Runeterra") into the [afterlife](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Spirit_Realm "Universe:Spirit Realm").

### Legends and Folklore

At some point in early history, a pair of masks were found carved into the remains of ancient gravesites. These masks helped spread the earliest stories of the Kindred across all of Runeterra, with every major nation having some variation or interpretation of the Kindred myth. Some, like  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"), revered the Lamb's swift and true arrows, while  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") strove for fierce and violent battles to escape the Wolf. The  [Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord") was known to honor the Wolf's chase by watering the battlefield in their enemies' blood, while in  [Bilgewater](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Bilgewater "Universe:Bilgewater"), people would throw festivals to honor the people granted a 'true death', rather than being claimed by the [Harrowing](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Harrowing "Harrowing"). Even on the  [Shadow Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shadow_Isles "Universe:Shadow Isles"), a perverse expanse where every undead soul is trapped in a waking nightmare, there are none who can escape the Kindred, as they are certain to outlast the Isles' curse.

As these many versions of the tale spread, so too did reenactments, with people wearing masks as they imitated the calm grace of the Lamb and the playful savagery of the Wolf.[[1]](#cite_note-A_Good_Death-1) One of the great bards of  [Valoran](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Valoran "Universe:Valoran"), Soates, wrote the Kindred Fables on her deathbed as she descended into madness. Her final narrative, *Lambs in the Orchard*, famously went unfinished before she died. During the reign of King Jarvan II, a playwright named Tarnold was hired by a noblewoman to write and direct an ending to Soates' incomplete work. He and his troupe were able to finish Soates' masterpiece after they all wore masks to channel the spirits of death, including Lamb, Wolf, a 6 [Vulture](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:The_Etherfiend "LoR:The Etherfiend"), and a 2 [maskmaker](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Mask_Mother "LoR:Mask Mother"). When it came time to perform, however, the actors stood lifeless, as the ending was meant only for those who wore masks.[[2]](#cite_note-Soates-2)

### Recent History

#### Chosen of the Wolf

:   *Main article: [Blood Sweat & Tears](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Blood_Sweat_%26_Tears "Universe:Blood Sweat & Tears")*

On the battlefield of [Rokrund](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Rokrund "Rokrund"), a pregnant  [Ambessa Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa") was gravely wounded with an arrow to her stomach. As she lay dying, she briefly entered the [realm of death](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Spirit_Realm "Universe:Spirit Realm") and met the  Kindred, who tested her strength and resolve by placing her in combat against [mighty warriors of ages past](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Chosen_of_the_Wolf "Universe:Chosen of the Wolf"). After the Kindred judged her worthy, Ambessa was awarded a vision where she was sitting upon the throne of the  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") empire, and when she awoke in the realm of the living, the  Wolf vanished after selecting her as his chosen.[[3]](#cite_note-Ambessa_novel-3)

#### Encounter with Tryndamere

:   *Main article: [Still Here](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Still_Here "Universe:Still Here")*

As  [Tryndamere](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tryndamere "Universe:Tryndamere") was fighting enemy warriors in the snow, he collapsed and fell on the brink of death. When he rose up, he saw the Kindred approach him. Tryndamere rejected a swift death from  Lamb and entered a  rage, cutting through her arrows and even her bow with his blade, while also fending off numerous attacks from the  Wolf. When Kindred was about to claim him, they suddenly backed away as  [Ashe](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ashe "Universe:Ashe") arrived and killed the enemy warriors, who were about to stab Tryndamere in the back. Tryndamere's rage ended, and he found himself surrounded by the enemy corpses, while Kindred was nowhere to be seen.
structure.appearance:
As a spirit god, Kindred is an entity with many names and forms across many different cultures. Their primary appearance, which is their oldest and most prevalent representation, is the  Lamb and the  Wolf.

### Lamb

Lamb, as her name would suggest, looks like a lamb with pale fur, standing with her hind legs on cloven hooves. She doesn't wear clothes, as her body is covered in white fur. The most distinctive ornament on her attire is the  "wolf" mask which has a dark color, with cool lights glowing through the large eye sockets. She carries with her a silver, mystical bow, which she uses as a weapon.

### Wolf

Wolf, as his name would suggest, is an enormous spectral wolf with dark fur, often only appearing as a jagged maw within a dark cloud. He wears no clothes, as the rest of his body is covered in a long, spectral dark veil. On occasion, Wolf can manifest legs as he charges down his prey, appearing much larger and more monstrous than an ordinary wolf. The most distinctive ornament on his attire is the  "lamb" mask which is white in color, with cool lights glowing through the large eye sockets.
structure.personality:
In the beginning, Kindred was a single being, isolated from the others due to their nature as a god of death. Lonely and craving companionship, they took an axe and cut themself into two beings, Lamb and Wolf. Both are deeply attached to each other, existing separately but acting as one.

### Lamb

Lamb is the calm and graceful marksman that swiftly and painlessly ends the life of those that accept death by shooting them down with a single well aimed arrow. Should they run away from their fate, they will find themselves in the maw of Wolf. Lamb appears to be Kindred's primary decision maker and is often the one directing Wolf towards their goal or explaining the emotions of others to him. She is highly knowledgeable about the people of Runeterra, but is detached from them, treating them as nothing more than stories to be told. Despite being calmer and less prone to violence than Wolf, Lamb is noticeably more apathetic towards others.

### Wolf

Wolf is the bestial half of the Kindred, representing a violent death. Those who will not fall to Lamb's arrows doom themselves to Wolf's jaws as he goes on the chase. Always hungry, he feels emotion but does not truly understand it - the counterpart to Lamb's impassive knowledge of feelings. The Kindred stalk the world, bringing peaceful death to those who will fall by Lamb. All who do not make one more chase for Wolf, and he pursues his prey with a gleeful and savage excitement. Wolf enjoys hearing stories from Lamb and will often ask her questions, which she is always ready to answer.
structure.abilities:
- **[Spirit God Physiology](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Spirit_God "Spirit God"):** Kindred is an ancient divine being embodying a particular aspect of the world, in this case, death. Kindred nurtures themselves from both their role as death gods and from the belief and memory of worshipers.
  - **Immortality:** So long as there is life on Runeterra and there still be people that believe in them, Kindred will continue existing.
  - **Spiritual Connection:** Both parts of the Kindred are connected to each other through a powerful spiritual bond.
  - **[Avatar of Death:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kindred#Mark_of_the_Kindred "Kindred")** Kindred is a god of death, responsible for the passing of living beings to the afterlife. Kindred will come to those that are close to death and can either take them to the beyond or grant them  [respite](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kindred#Lamb's_Respite "Kindred") to allow them to live longer. Whether Kindred chooses the death or they're simply drawn to those close to death seems to vary. If the dying person chooses a peaceful death, then Lamb will take them swiftly with one of their  [arrows](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kindred#Dance_of_Arrows "Kindred"). If they choose to fight death, then Wolf will give  [chase](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kindred#Wolf's_Frenzy "Kindred"). The nature of the "choice" is not always clear and obvious, as many have chosen without knowing, due to living a life that put them in the path of one of the Kindred.

relations.relationship_description: Lamb and  Wolf (or any other 2 forms of Kindred) consider each other their only friend. In [Spirit Bonds](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Spirit_Bonds "Spirit Bonds"), it was implied certain parts of the Grey Man still exist somewhere in the Spirit Realm.

As a god of death, Kindred is related to all other representations of deaths in Runeterra. Some legends say the 2 [Mask Mother](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Mask_Mother "LoR:Mask Mother") created Kindred. While it's unknown how true the story is, both Lamb and Wolf call her their mother. At the end of [Soates' final play](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Finishing_Soates "Finishing Soates"), it is suggested that once the Kindred are forgotten (or when all living things have died out),  Lamb and  Wolf will kill each other, while 6 [The Etherfiend](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:The_Etherfiend "LoR:The Etherfiend") will feast away on what's left.

When Ambessa was gravely wounded at the battlefield of [Rokrund](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rokrund "Universe:Rokrund"), a lone  Wolf approached her, whom she recognized as a harbinger of the Kindred. As she was on the brink of death, Kindred took Ambessa to [Volrachnun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Volrachnun "Universe:Volrachnun") and gave her two tests. The first was a test of combat against  [the Shield](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Pantheon/Cosmetics "Pantheon/Cosmetics"). The second was a test of will and sacrifice. For passing her trials, Ambessa was rewarded a vision of her sitting on the throne of the  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") empire, which she could claim should she choose to return to the realm of the living.[[3]](#cite_note-Ambessa_novel-3) Ambessa's meeting with the Kindred alloyed her resolve and ambition, and she would make it her personal mantra to always be as fearsome and merciless as the Wolf.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Tryndamere has bested death repeatedly as a result of his  undying rage. Kindred nearly claimed Tryndamere during one of his near-death experiences, but vanished after  [Ashe](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ashe "Universe:Ashe") saved him from enemy warriors.[[5]](#cite_note-5)
Fiddlesticks, an equally ancient entity, is one of the only champions to refer to Kindred prior to their split, calling out to Kindred as the  *"Grey man..."*

After the tally-men of Kindred collected the bodies of Karthus' sisters, as was custom in the parts of  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") where they lived, Karthus followed them, asking them questions about their line of work. The tally-men of Kindred soon accepted Karthus into their ranks, first as a grave digger, then a pyre builder, then a corpse collector. Eventually, Karthus worked in the temple of the tally-men, tending to the sick in their final moments. Now, as an undead, Karthus still wears the tally-men's vestments and carries the staff, which he still etches every time he 'releases' a mortal soul from life.

structure.trivia:
- *Kindred* means 'one's family and relations', from Old English *cynrēde*[[6]](#cite_note-6)
  - Their title, the *Eternal Hunters*, possibly references the European folkmyth [Wild Hunt](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_Hunt) involving supernatural beings like [elves](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf) or [ghosts](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost).
- Kindred are Runeterra's most common spirit god embodying [death](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_(personification)), but they are not the only ones.[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-Kindred_as_a_spirit_god-8) They prefer to appear to those who have either reached their time or suffer a near-death experience, but they can attack and kill anyone [should they so choose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/All_Kindred_Eve "All Kindred Eve"). They can also prevent death if they want to.[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-Blood_Sweat_Tears-10) They are empowered by the relevance sentient beings give them as well as the extent of their sphere of influence.[[11]](#cite_note-11)
  - Lamb grants a swift and painless end to those who have accepted their fate. Those who deny Lamb's arrow, thereby choosing to fight until the bitter end, are chased down by Wolf.
- The [Yin and Yang](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yin_and_Yang) are presented in Lamb and Wolf's appearance and personality, representing two halves of a whole that could not exist without one another. For instance, while Lamb has more knowledge and wisdom than Wolf, she does not experience hunger or sadness to the extent that he does. As Kindred straddles the border between life and death, Lamb interacts more with the physical world than Wolf does to draw that parallel.
- The myth of Kindred takes many forms across Runeterra's cultures, in accordance with their different folk tales, understandings, and relationships to death. The Lamb and Wolf are known by many names, including  **Ina** and  **Ani** in the west, and  **Farya** and  **Wolyo** in the east.[[1]](#cite_note-A_Good_Death-1)
  - Kindred's base appearance depicts how they appear in southern  [Freljordian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord") mythology. This is their oldest and most prevalent representation, with their masks becoming a universal symbol across various cultures.
  - As stated in [All Kindred Eve](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/All_Kindred_Eve "All Kindred Eve"), the Kindred are seen by  [Shurimans](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shurima "Universe:Shurima") as elegant tusked gazelles partnered with speckled hyenas, and by  [Ionians](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") as a snake and a sparrow. Some Ionians also imagine them as  [the Taker](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kindred/Cosmetics "Kindred/Cosmetics"), represented as a little girl and her beastly companion. Other interpretations are a jaull-fish and a minnow, a bloody-antlered stag and a sleek rabbit, a rose and a stinging bee. Some northern myths depict Lamb as an [elnuk](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Elnuk "Elnuk"). Kindred's  [Chosen of the Wolf](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kindred/Cosmetics "Kindred/Cosmetics") skin depicts how they appeared to  [Ambessa Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa"), a  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") believer in Volrachnun as the afterlife.
  - It is suggested that people from cultures without a Kindred myth are not visited by them.  [Mordekaiser](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mordekaiser "Universe:Mordekaiser") is a prime example of this.[[12]](#cite_note-12)
- Different cultures have different preferences of the Kindred. In  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"), Lamb's arrows are praised as a decision to accept one's death with grace. In the  [Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord"), warriors fight for their lives and accept a violent death in battles with Wolf, while the children and weaklings will be claimed by Lamb.  [Noxians](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") revere the Wolf over the Lamb, as their culture values ferocity and strength in battle. In  [Bilgewater](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Bilgewater "Universe:Bilgewater"), the Lamb is seen as cowardly and weak.
  - Kindred is known to have worshipers, like the tally-men in  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus").[[13]](#cite_note-Karthus_bio-13)
  - As seen in [A Good Death](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/A_Good_Death "A Good Death") and [Finishing Soates](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Finishing_Soates "Finishing Soates"), plays about the Kindred were popular in the era before  [Jarvan III](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_III "Universe:Jarvan III").
  - In  [Bilgewater](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Bilgewater "Universe:Bilgewater"), a festival known as Kindred Eve is held in celebration of the Kindred, where people from across the isles gather on "Witch-Tree Rock" to reenact the tale of the Kindred. During the festival, a fight is staged between the most "cowardly" person in Bilgewater, known as the Lambfool, and a strong person, called the Wolfkin Warrior, with the outcome determining the behavior of the Bilgewater folk for the next year. The contest is often rigged in favor of the Wolf, as if the Lamb were to win, the people of Bilgewater would not be allowed to lie, cheat, or kill for an entire year.[[14]](#cite_note-All_Kindred_Eve-14)
    - Bilgewater's version of the Kindred myth describes a Pale Rider who rode a great black beast, whom people avoided since looking at him meant death. One night he came upon a forked path, with an edlock tree in the middle. He knelt before the ancient tree and cut "himself right down the middle" with an axe so he could go through both paths. One road led to a deep, dark wood, and the other toward a city of light. The two paths met again, and the Pale Rider's halves had grown different, despite being the same. They drowned the axe in a river and decreed to forever walk side by side so they would never be alone.
- As they are a neutral, primordial force of nature, the Kindred are neither good nor evil, instead viewing death as a natural process.
  - Factors that disrupt this cycle, such as the [darkin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Darkin "Darkin") or the curse of the  [Shadow Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shadow_Isles "Universe:Shadow Isles"), are seen as an abomination in the eyes of Kindred. Resurrection of any form ( [coincidental](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Azir "Universe:Azir"),  [forced](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sion "Universe:Sion"),  [experimental](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Orianna "Universe:Orianna")), or even  [artificial life extension](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Elise "Universe:Elise"), is considered cheating the inevitable.[[8]](#cite_note-Kindred_as_a_spirit_god-8)
  - Robotic lifeforms, such as  [Blitzcrank](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Blitzcrank "Universe:Blitzcrank"), may or may not be exempt from being paid a visit.
- Kindred does not follow the usual rules of space and time, giving them a unique perception of the universe and allowing them to be in multiple places at once.
  - Although  [temporal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ekko "Universe:Ekko")  [manipulation](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zilean "Universe:Zilean") exists in Runeterra, reversing a person's death will not prevent Kindred from eventually claiming them.

structure.name: Kobuko
structure.background: A jolly yordle from Bandle City, Kobuko spent years exploring the world and discovered that it is often harsh and unfair. And his search to understand this led him to Ionia, where he fell in love with the culture, the people, the environment, and the philosophies, and then added his own brand of yordle eccentricity to the mix. Now he travels across Runeterra, seeking to help others find joy and value in life, even through adversity, and encouraging those he meets to pursue their dreams, do what they love, and explore new possibilities.[[2]](#cite_note-Introducing_Kobuko-2)
structure.appearance: Kobuko is a bearded yordle with his hair tied into a ponytail. He wears a rope with beads around his neck, a green vest and a rope tied around his waist decorated with bells and an engraved gemstone tied to his chest. He has large hands with glowing palms and a swirling pattern on the back of each hand.
structure.personality: He personally likes to express himself through martial arts and dancing, but he'll eagerly join you in whatever brings you joy, even if he's bad at it, because you deserve a friend who wants to see you happy and thriving.[[2]](#cite_note-Introducing_Kobuko-2)
structure.abilities: - **Yordle Physiology:** Kobuko is a Yordle, a being coming from the [Spirit Realm](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Spirit_Realm "Spirit Realm") and possesses several abilities natural of his species.
structure.trivia:

structure.name: Shaco
structure.quote: *"Whatever you do, don't tell him you missed the punch line."*
structure.background:
### Early Life

Shaco was once a toy made for a young prince.

### Corruption and Sentience

At some point, the prince that owned Shaco died, and through dark magic and corruption caused by the death of his owner, Shaco gained sentience. Soon, he started killing people and delighting in their pain. Shaco became a highly sought after fugitive by authorities due to his high number of crimes, and he is now a widely known criminal with no one knowing his origins or the motives behind his crimes.
structure.appearance: Shaco dons the outfit of a jester with checkered pants, gold buttons, and spiked shoulderplates. He has pale skin, a disproportionately wide smile, and eyes with no pupils.
structure.personality: Shaco is an insane individual, committing atrocities just because he feels like it. He delights in others' pain and often finds what he does funny. There is no real motive to his crimes, although it is possible that he only does these things to entertain himself.
structure.abilities:
- **[Daggers:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Shaco#Backstab "Shaco")** Shaco carries two poisoned dual shivs with him, making him able to stab his enemies and slowly eat away at those who survive.
- **[Jack in the Boxes:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Shaco#Jack_in_the_Box "Shaco")** Shaco can drop deadly jack-in-the-boxes to surprise and attack his enemies.
- **[Invisibility:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Shaco#Deceive "Shaco")** Shaco can turn invisible at will, making him able to hide from enemies and pull off unexpected attacks.
- **[Cloning:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Shaco#Hallucinate "Shaco")** Shaco is able to make a clone of himself and control it, confusing enemies and making him able to attack his enemies with his clone as well.
structure.trivia:
- While his title is "The Demon Jester", Shaco is not a demon.[[1]](#cite_note-1)
- Shaco is mentioned in the title of [Lulu and Shaco's Quirky Encounter](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/The_Music_of_League_of_Legends "The Music of League of Legends"). It is unknown if Shaco has ever encountered  [Lulu](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Lulu "Universe:Lulu") in the lore.

structure.name: Malphite
structure.quote: *"Beware, minions of chaos! The Shard of the Monolith has come."*
structure.background:
### Origin and Creation

Malphite was originally created as part of a monumental project by the  [Ixtali](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ixtal "Universe:Ixtal") elemental mage Ne'Zuk, who sought to combat the destructive forces of the  [Void](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Void "Universe:Void"). Ne'Zuk crafted a massive fortress, known as the Monolith, made from stone and elemental magic. This fortress was designed to act as a barrier, a weapon, and a last line of defense against the Void's corrupting influence. Malphite was created as a guardian entity within this fortress.

However, the Monolith was not simply a structure of stone; it was a living being that possessed incredible elemental power, a living vessel of elemental stone and magic. Ne'Zuk’s creation was part of an ambitious plan to neutralize the Void, but, despite the immense power of the Monolith, the plan ultimately failed. The Void forces were too overwhelming, and the Monolith itself was shattered in the conflict.

### Shattering and Fragmentation

As the Monolith was destroyed, Malphite became the last surviving fragment of it. The battle against the Void tore the Monolith apart, and what was left of Malphite was scattered across Runeterra. For centuries, Malphite lay in a dormant, fragmented state, with his essence locked away in the ruins of the shattered Monolith. His body remained broken, but his spirit remained, lingering with a sense of purpose to continue fighting the Void.

### Awakening

Malphite’s regeneration began when the shards of the Monolith slowly started to reconnect. This fragment of him grew aware of its surroundings, with memories of the Monolith’s destruction and the threat of the Void. His awakened form is much more colossal, resembling a massive golem-like figure of stone and living magic, but still marked by the deep cracks and fractures that come from the shattering of his original form.

### The Void and His Purpose

The Void's influence continues to haunt Malphite. He sees the Void as an existential threat to all of existence, including his own. His consciousness is shaped by this overwhelming desire to stop the Void, even if it means sacrificing his very existence. He embodies the raw elemental energy of stone, yet he is not just an inert, mindless force. Malphite is driven by a will to protect the world, even though it is a world that often seems to have forgotten the ancient threats.

Although Malphite is a construct of stone and magic, he has an emotional core that shapes his personality. He is lonely, as he was alone for so long in the aftermath of the Monolith’s destruction, and he is often plagued by doubt. He struggles with the loss of the Monolith, questioning if there is any hope for the world or if it is too late to stop the Void. His solitude is made even more poignant by his inability to find others like him, as he is the last remnant of his kind.

He became an elemental force, still carrying the mission of protecting the world from the Void, even though the original Monolith’s destruction and the loss of his fellow constructs left him with a profound sense of isolation. His mission, to prevent the Void from infiltrating the world again, is all that keeps him moving forward.
structure.appearance: Malphite is a walking mountain, a rough assembly of stone and earth, sometimes featuring sparse patches of plant life. It is vaguely human-shaped, with enormously broad, bulky shoulders and a hunched posture. It has four-fingered hands, three-toed feet, and a relatively small head with eyes and a mouth that glow green. It features numerous upward-facing spikes resembling craggy mountain peaks on its head, back, forearms, and knees.
structure.personality: Stoic yet easygoing, Malphite is fond of making quaint observations. It is extremely friendly to mortals as well as other stone golems, who it often regards as family. However, it can become aggressive when necessary, unleashing the unstoppable force of its awesome might against its enemies. Acutely aware of its giant size and strength, Malphite is a protector of  [Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Runeterra "Universe:Runeterra"), standing stalwart against the forces of  [the Void](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Void "Universe:The Void") whom it was created to combat.
structure.abilities:
- **Golem Physiology**: Malphite is an immortal construct of living stone. His mountainous size affords him incalculable strength, stony durability, and surprising speed.
  - **Geomancy**: Malphite is able to form the land around him into various shapes, even using it as a projectile.

relations.relationship_description: Chip is literally a chip off of Malphite's body. Their relationship is like that of a loving father and son.
Malphite and Taliyah are friends. They play rock paper scissors, but Malphite always loses as he predictably always picks rock.

structure.trivia:
- *Malphite* means *bad stone* in  [Ixtali](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ixtal "Universe:Ixtal").
- Malphite was created by the [God-Warrior](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/God-Warrior "God-Warrior") Ne’Zuk, who was the original owner of  [Ezreal's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Ezreal "Ezreal") gauntlet.
- Being created to fight the  [Void](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Void "Universe:Void") war after the fall of [Icathia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Icathia "Icathia"), Malphite is between 3000 to 3500 years old.

structure.name: Skarner
structure.quote: *"I may have faded into legend—but I am no mere story."*
structure.background:
### Early Life

Skarner was born to the legendary brackern broodmother Nixalẹ alongside many other bracklings in his brood. While most left to form their own clans, Skarner remained alongside Nixalẹ to study her power and wisdom out of curiosity, giving him the opportunity to hone his elemental geomancy and learn how to feel underground vibrations to detect movement across the earth.

### Founding of the Yun Tal

When he got older, he felt a dramatic shift as humans [came to the land to found their settlement](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Westward_Migration "Westward Migration") now known as  [Ixtal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ixtal "Universe:Ixtal"). While most of Clan Ọ̀pal-hin distrusted the humans, Skarner was curious to learn more about them. He silently observed their civilization, noticing how they made the most of their lives creating and innovating before passing away. Believing the subjects of his curiosity to be fragile, he intervened to save them from a rockslide that would destroy their settlement, earning him their worship towards him as their protector. Believing his protection was the only way they could survive, Skarner made it his duty to guard the Ixtali while also shaping the earth to create new plots for them to expand their civilization, and in return they shared their culture. He was one of the founding members of the  [Yun Tal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yun_Tal "Universe:Yun Tal"), a ruling caste dedicated to leading the Ixtali to a brighter future.

### Isolation Beneath Ixaocan

As the protector of Ixtal, Skarner listened to the earth's vibrations for any threats to the nation, the most concerning being the encroaching Shuriman Empire. Eventually, the forces of  [Shurima](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shurima "Universe:Shurima") would arrive at Ixtal and offered them an opportunity to form an alliance. The Yun Tal accepted, despite Skarner's protest, due his distrust of their lust for power. After Shurima collapsed as the result of the [Icathian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Icathia "Icathia") rebellion, Ixtal had regained its independence, but Skarner was left distrustful towards the world outside Ixtal. His fears worsened after witnessing the destruction caused by the [Rune Wars](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Rune_Wars "Rune Wars"), eventually convincing the Yun Tal to isolate Ixtal from the rest of the world. Left bitter towards the Yun Tal's failure to protect Ixtal, he decided that he would be Ixtal's sole protector, creating an underground chamber beneath Ixaocan to amplify the vibrational threads around the continent so he could always sense any potential threats. Eventually, he decided to stay in his chamber permanently, but as newer generations of Ixtali started to question their civilization's self-isolation, Skarner's paranoia began to grow. Believing that ending their isolation would lead to disastrous consequences for Ixtal, Skarner swore to protect Ixtal no matter the cost, even if it meant their destruction.
structure.appearance: Skarner is a kaiju-sized scorpion-like creature with six legs, a pair of thick grasping pincers, and three long tails ending in stingers. He has a teal and white carapace decorated with orange, teal, and white paint. His head is vaguely human-like despite its chitinous exterior, having two glowing teal eyes and a hinged jaw and mouth, but with two insect-like mandibles. He wears (relatively) small decorative ornaments on his upper arms and central tail.
structure.personality: Skarner is a commanding and imposing presence, speaking with the authority of an ancient, powerful being. Still, he carries an aura of formality, wisdom, and solemnity. He is single-mindedly protective of  [Ixtal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ixtal "Universe:Ixtal"), seeing himself as its steward and most important protector. Though he cares greatly for mortals, he is keenly aware of their flaws and weaknesses, seemingly having little faith in them. Thus, he is extremely stubborn, prioritizing his own judgment above that of all others. He is absolutely certain that Ixtal should remain in isolation and is growing increasingly paranoid as more Ixtali begin to question their nation's solitude.
structure.abilities:
- **[Brackern](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Brackern "Brackern") Physiology**: Skarner is a brackern, a giant scorpion-like creature with a thick carapace, immense strength, innate elemental magic, and a long lifespan.
  - [**Prehensile Stingers:**](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Skarner#Impale "Skarner") Skarner has three stingers which can be used to grab objects.
  - [**Brackern Geomancy:**](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Skarner#Shattered_Earth "Skarner") Skarner can manipulate earth to his will, being able to use it as a weapon or to shield himself.
  - **Vibrational Thread Sensing**: Skarner can feel vibrations across the earth, allowing him to sense the actions of others even across a great distance.

relations.relationship_description: Skarner views Milio negatively and sees him as an extension of his great aunt, who rebelled against the Yun Tal.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
Skarner is aware of Qiyana's plot to seize power. Presumably, he disapproves.

structure.trivia:
**Skarner, the Primordial Sovereign**

- The full name of a Brackern consists of their first name, which clan they are part of, and whom they are the progeny of.[[3]](#cite_note-3)
- When Skarner uses  [Seismic Bastion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Skarner#Seismic_Bastion "Skarner"), he uses his geomancy to create earthquakes, while also summoning the earth to shield himself.[[4]](#cite_note-4)
- How Skarner senses vibrational threads is similar to how [Toph Beifong](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toph_Beifong) from [Avatar: The Last Airbender](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar:_The_Last_Airbender) sees the world, by feeling movement on top of the earth, which are like threads that track back to him.[[5]](#cite_note-5)
- Clan Ọ̀pal-hin were originally from the jungles of Ixtal, but there are numerous other clans across the Shuriman continent.[[6]](#cite_note-6)
- Skarner and the Brackern speak in vibrational tones that, when heard, burrow into the mind and are translated to the listener's own tongue.[[7]](#cite_note-7)
- The adornments on Skarner's body were painted on by Ixtali people and he cherishes them deeply.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

**Skarner, the Crystal Vanguard**

- The [Brackern](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Brackern "Brackern") are VERY old. They've been around far longer than humans, and because of their long life they experience time in a very different way than most other beings.
  - The crystals existed before even the Brackern, who evolved with the life stones' power. The Brackern possibly don't know how to create a new one, so it's possible they could eventually run out of stones if they're all destroyed.
    - Since Skarner has one of the oldest and strongest life stones in existence, he is the most powerful Brackern, but he's not stronger than all of them put together. Also, the consciousness within the stone chose Skarner in particular, not just for his strength but for other qualities like his persistence and courage.
- The Brackern's experience with humans has been steeped in violence. They believe humans caused so many conflicts and forced the Brackern to go into hibernation. Now that humans are exploiting the sleeping Brackern for their crystals, they're not going to become BFFs anytime soon.
- Skarner certainly had trouble communicating with humans. The Brackern use their life stones to communicate telepathically by sending raw emotion, images, and thoughts into each others minds in a kind of melody. That's part of why Brackern without life stones cannot communicate as well with their species. His connection to his fellow Brackern is very nearly unbreakable. Their minds reach out to each other and sing over great distances, even while they are unconscious - for example, they can hear each other's dreamsongs while hibernating. Skarner has never spoken in any other way, so he doesn't understand the human tongue, at least not yet. By the end of [Dreamsong](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Dreamsong "Dreamsong"), he does learn to understand (and speak) their language of violence. However, it's possible that Skarner could learn to trust a human, though, if they can hear his song or communicate another way.
  - [Seraphine](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Seraphine "Universe:Seraphine") is able to hear Brackern soul crystals, and her special interaction with Skarner implies that she is aware of the brackern's existence and Skarner's grief for his kind, so she is possibly the most likely to be able to communicate with him.
