structure.name: Riven
structure.quote: *"A warrior's blade reflects the truth in their heart. Mine is black, and broken."*
structure.background:
### Early life

Riven was born on a farm in the coastal farming village of [Trevale](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Trevale "Universe:Trevale"), in  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"). Her father had been a soldier, slain in battle and her own mother was said to not survived the birth, leaving young Riven to work the farms as an orphan. Working a farm wasn't her lifelong goal, however. She longed for more. Inspired by warband conscriptors that would frequent Trevale, she would eventually join the Fury Company and pledge her strength to the Noxian Empire. Alongside her sisters- and brothers- in arms, whose bonds were forged in the heat of battle, a bond she saw as unbreakable, Riven thrived.

Despite her youth, Riven proved to be a natural soldier. Years of working at the farm made her strong, and in turn, allow her to master the weight of a longsword so much taller and heavier than herself. So strong was her dedication, that it got her noticed by  [Boram Darkwill](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Boram_Darkwill "Universe:Boram Darkwill"), the emperor of Noxus, who bestowed Riven her own massive runic blade, said to be enchanted by a certain  [pale sorceress](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:LeBlanc "Universe:LeBlanc") in his court.

Not long after, Riven and her warband would sail for Ionia, intended to take part of the long planned Noxus-led occupation. The war dragged, and it became clear that Ionia would not kneel. Fury Company was eventually assigned to escort another warband, through the embattled Navori Province. The warband's leader, a commander by the name of Emystan, had just commissioned weapons from a Zaunite alchymist, and was eager to test them out. Riven had been glad to put her life on the Altar of the Noxian Empire across countless campaigns, but the something had been off about this one. The soldiers, the weapons' purpose, something was off. It made Riven uneasy.

This campaign, much like the others, was met with strong resistance. It was the land itself fighting back. Stranded on a muddy landslide during a rainstorm, the Ionian resistance saw an opportunity. Seeing the opposition, Riven called Emystan for backup. It would be the last Captain Riven would ever do.

A flaming arrow, flown from the ridgeside, embedded itself into the wagon. Riven had instinctively drawn her sword, but it wasn't enough to protect anyone but herself. Chemical flames burst from the wagon, engulfing Noxian and Ionian alike, leaving them to suffer a slow agonizing death. Saved from the toxic mist by the magic in her Runeblade, Riven could only watch in horror as both family and foe slowly choked to death on the poisonous fumes. There she realized the high cost of the war bent not on expanding Noxus's borders or spreading its ideals, but one of complete and utter annihilation. One of complete utter betrayal and atrocity.

Memories of the event would only come to Riven later in nightmares, but the impact was enough. Disgusted with the betrayal, Riven had come to hate the blade that saved her life, her final tie to Noxus. Seeking the assistance of a  [windblade master](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Souma "Universe:Souma"), Riven would have it shattered, but even that failed to bring her peace. She wandered the Ionian countryside, deciding exile was a better price for someone who'd wrought as much damage as she.

### Contemporary history

Eventually, her travels would return her to the village where she'd broken the sword. There, she would be taken in by a pair of Ionian farmers, distraught over the loss of their own sons, but unwilling to live in the past and fully ready to embrace the future. Once she'd regain her health, Riven would help them in the fields until one day Ionian soldiers came for her. Then, she learned that the master she'd sought help for to destroy her blade had perished, and that in seeing her blade, the Ionian soldiers have new evidence as to who might have done it.

Now dragged to court, Riven faced trail for the murder of  [Elder Souma](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Souma "Universe:Souma"), whom she currently had no true recollection of ever meeting. After being bombarded with questions, Riven's blade, the Runesword she had sought to destroy and now laid in pieces sans one, was brought out. The final piece, found embedded in the corpse of Elder Souma, was slotted back into the weapon and revived the deactivated weapon and her memories. Riven was in fact, she revealed, the one who killed Elder Souma.

That night she was made to stay in the trail room, to await her sentence. A hooded man, who'd had approached her the day before prior to her arrest, came to her. There, he revealed himself to be  [Yasuo](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yasuo "Universe:Yasuo"), Elder Souma's apprentice, who'd been tasked to guard the elder but had left to fight in the [Noxian Invasion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxian_Invasion_of_Ionia "Universe:Noxian Invasion of Ionia"). He'd return to his village to his master dead, his village attacked, and first and foremost had been accused of Souma's murder. Now seeking vengeance, he challenged Riven to a fight, to which she agreed.

The battle was on then.

Only stopping when Riven's Runic blade, activated but still very much in pieces, slid and a piece shot out, the piece flying in the direction of Riven's adoptive father, Asa Konte, who'd had come to Riven to free her from her chains. It would've killed him were it not for Yasuo's windwall, stopping right as it was about to embed itself onto the old man's neck. There it was where Riven understood, that they both could not escape their pasts, but can embrace change. When the magistrate returned, Riven was ready to face her sentence. The council, seeing as no longer wishing for additional bloodshed, had sentenced her to years of servitude in the farms around the village, starting that of the Kontes. Riven, now reforged somewhat, agreed.

### Recent events

In the later years, Riven was caught and she was forced to fight as a Reckoning in the Reckoner’s Arena, which is run by Darius’s brother, Draven. She later helped Lucian, Senna, and Vayne escape during the harrowing in Noxus and temporarily joined the Sentinels of Light to atone for her sins. Her whereabouts after the events of the Sentinels of Light were unknown, presumably returning to the Kontes’ farm.
structure.appearance: She was ruthless and efficient as a warrior, but her true strength lay in her conviction. She entered battles without any trace of doubt in her mind: no ethical pause, no fear of death. She is a determined and fiercely devoted individual with internal discipline.
structure.personality:
Riven is a tall woman with an athletic build, tanned skin, dark golden eyes, and platinum white hair tied up in a bow.

She usually wears a two-part white dress, as well as bandages on her right arm and she has parts of black armor that covers her shoulder, left leg, and a metal glove on her left hand.
structure.abilities:
### [Singed](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Singed "Universe:Singed")

Riven was a  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") soldier sent to  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") during the empire's invasion. A traumatic experience during the campaign involving  [Singed's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Singed "Universe:Singed") chemicals caused her to question her devotion and sever her ties to Noxus, wandering ever since.  [Singed](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Singed "Universe:Singed") was approached by a  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") military commander named Emystan, who Riven's unit was assigned to escort, to help her break the bitter stalemate of the war in  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia"). When Riven called to Emystan for support during a battle, both sides were annihilated by the chemicals he created. Seeing the approval of slaughter of the innocent caused by Singed and Emystan also made  [Quilletta Varn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Quilletta_Varn "Universe:Quilletta Varn") grew more disillusioned by the empire's ambitions, which led to her rebel against the empire and the events of  [Darius'](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Darius "Darius") comic [Blood of Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Blood_of_Noxus "Universe:Blood of Noxus").

### [Yasuo](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yasuo "Universe:Yasuo")

[Yasuo](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yasuo "Universe:Yasuo") suspected Riven of being the one who killed Elder Souma, whom Yasuo was supposed to protect (*"Wait, that  [technique](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Riven#Broken_Wings "Riven")... huh"*, *"Huh,  [three](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Riven#Broken_Wings "Riven") swift strikes... "*, *"Another  [wind](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Riven#Wind_Slash "Riven") blade?"*, *"Who taught you  [that](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Riven#Wind_Slash "Riven")?"*) Riven eventually confessed to unintentionally killing Elder Souma: desperate to erase her past as a Noxian invader and killer, Riven begged the elderly  [wind](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Yasuo#Last_Breath "Yasuo")-master to shatter her runic blade, which was the past's memento. Souma succeeded, yet a stray shard struck his neck, killing him.

The confession absolved Yasuo of murder, yet not of his personal guilt of abandoning his post that led to Souma's accidental death and him having to kill multiple brethen in self-defense, including  [his own brother](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yone "Universe:Yone"). Yasuo's presence or absence making a difference was highlighted during Riven's trial, when he focused the Wind Technique on Riven's sword as Souma would have, and the shard that killed his master nearly did the same to Asa Konte, Riven's adopted father. This time, Yasuo was able to stop the shard before it could cause any harm.

### [LeBlanc](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:LeBlanc "Universe:LeBlanc")

Her blade was enchanted by  [LeBlanc](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:LeBlanc "Universe:LeBlanc"), who is seemingly trying to take it back.

### Her Battlesisters

Riven's sisters in war  [Arrel](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Arrel "Universe:Arrel"),  [Marit](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Marit "Universe:Marit") and  [Teneff](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Teneff "Universe:Teneff") were tasked with and succeeded in bringing her back to  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"), where she was sentenced to life in the  [Fleshing Arena](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Reckoners "Universe:Reckoners"). The group leader,  [Tifalenji](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tifalenji "Universe:Tifalenji"), was sent by LeBlanc to retrieve the blade. She was angry when she found out it was broken (and LeBlanc will possibly be, too).

### [Draven](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Draven "Universe:Draven")

[Draven](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Draven "Universe:Draven") finds her a worthy opponent when she was forced to fight in his arena.

### [Sentinels of Light](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sentinels_of_Light "Universe:Sentinels of Light")

Riven helped the  [Sentinels of Light](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sentinels_of_Light "Universe:Sentinels of Light") escape from Reckoner's Arena and would later join them in their fight against  [Viego's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Viego "Viego") Ruination. Riven was initially rebuked by  [Irelia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Irelia "Universe:Irelia"), due to her past actions during the Noxian Invasion, but eventually gained her respect during their time together as Sentinels of Light.

structure.name: Jarvan_III
structure.background:
### Early Life

Jarvan III was the third heir to  [House Lightshield](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Lightshield "Universe:House Lightshield"), the royal family of  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") the since rule of Jarvan I. When he was a young boy, Jarvan enjoyed the theater and attended a rendition of *The King of All Fishes* by the playwright Tarnold, where he clapped the loudest out of anyone in the audience.[[3]](#cite_note-Soates-3) He was also raised on many old Demacian tales from his father, King Jarvan II, hearing tales of the great Orlon and his followers, including the founding of their kingdom.[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4) His childhood friend was  [Barrett](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Barrett_Buvelle "Universe:Barrett Buvelle") of  [House Buvelle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Buvelle "Universe:House Buvelle"), and as they grew up, Jarvan came to further rely on his friend's counsel, making him his chief advisor and right hand.[[5]](#cite_note-Fragile-5)

### Coronation and Marriage

Jarvan III was a young man when he received his coronation. After he became King, the [noble families](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noble_Houses_of_Demacia "Universe:Noble Houses of Demacia") fought each other to gain his favor, some even raising private militias to serve him. The first two weeks of his reign proved chaotic as he tried to broker peace between them, until an  [Illuminator](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Illuminators "Universe:Illuminators") named Lestara Demoisier confronted him for not prioritizing the kingdom's homeless and hungry. The young King Jarvan was blindsided by her criticism, but Lord  [Barrett](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Barrett_Buvelle "Universe:Barrett Buvelle") was ready with a plan to provide shelter to every homeless Demacian. Having learned of his people's plight, Jarvan approved Barrett's plan and thanked Lestara for bringing the issue to his attention.[[5]](#cite_note-Fragile-5)

As the feuding between the nobles escalated, Jarvan III decided to end the conflict by marrying Lady Catherine, who was popular amongst the people. They had a healthy relationship and announced they were expecting a son by the end of the year. The young  [Prince Jarvan](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_IV "Universe:Jarvan IV") was born; however, Catherine died in childbirth, leaving the king's hope for the future also torn by his grief. Jarvan III swore never to take another wife and ensured that he would train their son to be the next king of Demacia.[[6]](#cite_note-JarvanBio-6)

### Battle of Kalstead

At some point during his reign, Jarvan III's forces came into conflict with the empire of  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"), which was then ruled by Grand General  [Boram Darkwill](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Boram_Darkwill "Universe:Boram Darkwill"). As the empire was fighting wars on multiple fronts, Jarvan III took the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard") to aid the defense of [Kalstead](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kalstead "Universe:Kalstead") from the expansionist forces, hoping to curb the Noxian influence over  [Valoran](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Valoran "Universe:Valoran"). The newly-appointed Sword-Captain  [Tianna Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tianna "Universe:Tianna") won a decisive victory for her king, and the decimated Noxian forces were scattered and taken prisoner.[[7]](#cite_note-XinBio-7)[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4)

The prisoners, many of them conscripts bought out from the  [Reckoning](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Reckoners "Universe:Reckoners") pits, expected to be executed by the Demacians. But Jarvan III granted them mercy and freedom, should they agree to leave Kalstead in peace. When he met with the last of the prisoners, the undefeated Reckoner "Viscero", he invited him to share his story, despite Tianna's visible irritation with the man. The Reckoner told Jarvan III that his real name was  [Xin Zhao](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xin_Zhao "Universe:Xin Zhao"), and that the name "Viscero" had been taken from the old  [Ionian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") fishing boat he served on before being captured and taken to Noxus. He had become a Reckoner in order to survive, and had been sent to Kalstead only after the empire bought him out from the arenas. Hearing this, Jarvan III decided that Xin Zhao should be freed from the bonds of Noxus and gave him enough gold for one week's worth of travel.[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4)

To everyone's surprise, Xin Zhao refused the gold, having been moved by the king's show of mercy. He requested to join Jarvan III's personal guard; a suggestion which sparked outrage from Tianna, but Jarvan III simply found amusing. After asking for proof that the Reckoner would be capable of this task, Xin Zhao swiftly bested the guards present and revealed he could have killed the king at any moment during their conversation.[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4)

Jarvan III was deeply impressed with Xin Zhao's resilience and courage, and though Tianna demanded he be executed, the king made certain Xin Zhao would come back with them to the [Great City](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia"), where he would be given an opportunity to prove his loyalty. Jarvan III also took the opportunity to pass a lesson down to his  [son](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_IV "Universe:Jarvan IV") about mercy, and the passing of Demacian virtues to all who might be inspired by them.[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4)

Years passed, and Xin Zhao ultimately did prove himself, being chosen as King Jarvan's seneschal and protector, as well as his trusted advisor and bodyguard. Jarvan III watched with pride as the former Reckoner became a mentor to the young prince, training him to be both a warrior and a man worthy of one day inheriting the throne.[[7]](#cite_note-XinBio-7)

### The Wyldbloom

After many years of faithful service,  [Xin Zhao](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xin_Zhao "Universe:Xin Zhao") eventually approached the king with concerns about the appearance of a Wyldbloom in  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"); a spirit blossom which had bloomed far outside  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia"). As Xin Zhao had been troubled by the bloom's sudden appearance, King Jarvan gave the Seneschal command of one of his ships and insisted he return to his old home and investigate, in hopes that he would find the answer he was seeking.[[8]](#cite_note-Pilgrimage-8)

Eventually, Xin Zhao's spear returned home to Demacia, but its wielder did not. It was brought back by  [Yunara](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yunara "Universe:Yunara") of the  [Kinkou Order](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kinkou_Order "Universe:Kinkou Order"), who revealed to the king that Xin Zhao had fallen in battle against a  [demon](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Atakhan "Universe:Atakhan"). Jarvan III mourned the lost of his dear friend, but recounted how he loved the libraries and gardens of Demacia. He wished to give his Seneschal full honors and inquired what had happened to his body. Yunara informed him that seemingly nothing remained after the battle, but seeing her sorrow, Jarvan III told her that his death was not her alone to bear. He urged for her stay in Demacia and get to know the nation that Xin Zhao loved.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

### Fall of the Gates of Mourning

During the battle at the [Gates of Mourning](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Gates_of_Mourning "Universe:Gates of Mourning"), the  [Demacian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") forces suffered a particularly devastating defeat at the hands of  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") warmages. Many young soldiers were killed, including those in the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard"), as well as the High Marshal Purcivell Bronz, and even the honored Lord  [Barrett Buvelle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Barrett_Buvelle "Universe:Barrett Buvelle"), the King's best friend and a much-beloved figure in Demacia for his love of the country and his generosity to the public. Jarvan III was left shattered by Barrett's death, and in the following weeks, he arranged services for all those who had fallen.[[5]](#cite_note-Fragile-5)

Wracked with grief, and also compelled by renewed fears of [magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic") following the carnage, King Jarvan sought justice by increasing the power and influence of the  [Mageseekers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mageseekers "Universe:Mageseekers"), despite knowing in his heart that Barrett would not have wanted his death to be avenged. The funeral was held three weeks after the battle, and had so many mourners in attendance that the [Great City](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia") was not large enough to hold them all. After delivering his eulogy, and declaring his resolve to the public, King Jarvan held the reception in the gardens next to his palace.[[5]](#cite_note-Fragile-5)

After everyone else had left, Jarvan III spoke to Lady Lestara, Barrett's widow, as they both said their final goodbyes to him. As they reminisced on the impact Barrett had on both their lives, Lestara criticized Jarvan for seeking vengeance, as they both knew Barrett would not have approved of his decision to persecute the mages. The King's declaration, however, had been final, and the wishes of his late friend were not enough to convince him to go back on his word.[[5]](#cite_note-Fragile-5)

### Testing of Garen Crownguard

:   *Main article: [The Might of Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Might_of_Demacia "Universe:The Might of Demacia")*

Soon after  [Tianna Crownguard's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tianna "Universe:Tianna") resignation as Sword-Captain and elevation to the role of High Marshal, Jarvan III summoned a battalion of recruits to appear before the royal court in the Hall of Valor. Among these young soldiers was  [Garen Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen"), who was both Tianna's nephew and a close friend of his son,  [Jarvan IV](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_IV "Universe:Jarvan IV"). At Tianna's recommendation, King Jarvan allowed Garen to undergo the necessary trials to join the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard"). Garen trained in the capital and soon passed his trials, and was once again summoned by the King, this time to take his oaths before the throne, with both the prince and members of  [House Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Crownguard "Universe:House Crownguard") present for the ceremony. Garen would go on to prove himself time and again a dutiful servant of crown and country, and for this, he was eventually appointed the Vanguard's new Sword-Captain after Tianna's successor fell in battle.[[10]](#cite_note-GarenBio-10)

### Crownguard-Laurent Feud

:   *Main article: [The Grand Duelist](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Grand_Duelist "Universe:The Grand Duelist")*

After the youngest  [daughter](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Fiora "Universe:Fiora") of  [House Laurent](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Laurent "Universe:House Laurent") turned eighteen, an advantageous political marriage was arranged between her and  [House Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Crownguard "Universe:House Crownguard") as part of Demacia's grand game of alliances. The wedding was to be held at summer in the [Great City](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia"), and was a large enough event that King Jarvan himself was in attendance. When the day arrived, however, Fiora announced that she would rather die than marry someone against her will. The outburst publicly humiliated her betrothed, and his family demanded the matter be settled in a traditional duel to the death, which Fiora immediately agreed to.[[11]](#cite_note-FioraBio-11)

With the noble houses once again at each other's throats, Fiora's father Sebastien begged for Jarvan to intervene, as he had already mediated many such conflicts in the past. But Fiora had already accepted the duel, meaning the King was unable to cancel it. With no other option, Sebastien invoked his right to fight in his daughter's place.  [Tianna Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tianna "Universe:Tianna"), now the High Marshal, similarly named a champion to fight for her kinsman, this one an elite warrior from the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard"). In the face of almost certain defeat, which would lead to Fiora's exile and his house's ruin, Sebastien Laurent attempted to drug his opponent before the duel. He was caught, and arrested for violating Demacia's most fundamental code of honor.[[11]](#cite_note-FioraBio-11)

To finally settle the feud, Jarvan arranged for Sebastien's execution. But instead of a hanging as originally planned, Fiora proposed to the King that she fight her own father to the death as payment for his crimes, and for the right to claim the Laurent name from him and her brothers. King Jarvan watched the duel from his dais, and after Sebastien had been slain, he solemnly declared the quarrel between the families was finished, and named Fiora the new head of House Laurent.[[11]](#cite_note-FioraBio-11)

### Death & Legacy

On the day of his scheduled execution, the convicted mage  [Sylas](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sylas "Universe:Sylas") narrowly escaped before destroying an entire square and freeing the other mages from the  [Demacian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") mage prison.[[12]](#cite_note-Lux3-12) Many of them fled the [Great City](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Great_City_of_Demacia "Universe:The Great City of Demacia") through the sewers, but those who wanted vengeance joined Sylas on his march to the Citadel of Dawn, where they planned to publicly humiliate Jarvan III for all they had suffered. Having lost control of several portions of the city, Jarvan III met with his advisors and  [Jarvan IV](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_IV "Universe:Jarvan IV"), who began to discuss strategy to defeat Sylas and his insurrection. The King, however, blamed himself for the carnage, claiming that Sylas had only become a threat to Demacia because they had put him in chains.[[13]](#cite_note-Lux4-13)

As the rebels approached the royal palace, Jarvan III's guards rushed him to the nearest safe room, which was virtually impenetrable while locked from the inside. However, this safe room had already been infiltrated by the  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") assassin  [Katarina Du Couteau](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Katarina "Universe:Katarina"), who killed King Jarvan and his guards before using the chaos outside the palace as cover for her escape.[[2]](#cite_note-Katarina2-2) When Sylas and Jarvan IV discovered the King's body, the prince cried in horror, believing Sylas and the other mages were responsible and that his father had been foolish for trusting them. With the King dead, Sylas decided to humiliate Jarvan IV instead, but  [Lux](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Lux "Universe:Lux") rescued the prince, causing Sylas and the other rebels to flee through the sewers.[[14]](#cite_note-Lux5-14)

Shortly before his death, Jarvan III had written a letter that would have immediately halted the arrests of mages, in hopes that it would prevent the brewing [conflict](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Great_Mage_Rebellion "Universe:Great Mage Rebellion"). This letter was never made public, however, and when Jarvan IV found it, he had it destroyed.[[15]](#cite_note-Mageseeker-15) Jarvan III's funeral was held the day after Sylas's escape, where Jarvan IV vowed that as the new king, he would avenge his father and formally declared war against "the scourge of [magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic")."[[14]](#cite_note-Lux5-14)

Jarvan IV empowered the mageseekers to hunt down Sylas, however, his actions also drove  [Shyvana](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shyvana "Universe:Shyvana") away. He eventually saw the error of his ways and honored his late father's wish to abolish the mageseekers.[[15]](#cite_note-Mageseeker-15)
structure.appearance: Jarvan III was an elderly man with a white beard, who would sometimes be seen wearing blue and white robes trimmed with gold. On top of his head sat a golden crown with a blue gemstone at the center, emphasizing his position as ruler of  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"). Frequently, he would be seen wearing a full set of pristine, shining golden armor which covered his chest, arms, and legs, with no helmet.
structure.personality:
Jarvan III was a merciful and compassionate man, deeply committed to the ideals on which  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") was founded, including honor, fellowship, and justice. Unlike other rulers, Jarvan was relaxed with formalities and was open to criticism, believing input from his subjects made him a better king. He deeply respected those who were not afraid to voice their opinion, or even speak harshly or threaten him. Often, he would find humor in such situations as a means to alleviate tension. But he was also unafraid to use force if necessary, believing it his duty to maintain a steady hand for the hope of his people. Jarvan was a man of his word, and he maintained a stubborn stoicism once his decision had been made.

Despite his best efforts, Jarvan III's reign was marred by factionalism, prejudice, and civil unrest, and he often struggled with balancing his commitment to Demacian virtues and the responsibility to protect his citizens. He often found himself unhappy with the many compromises he made, including those to quell tensions between the feuding nobles. Though he was averse to needless bloodshed, the rapid expansion of  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") often made war necessary. And although he believed outsiders should be welcome within his kingdom, he was known to make emotional decisions after experiencing loss. After he lost  [Lord Barrett](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Barrett_Buvelle "Universe:Barrett Buvelle"), his misguided sense of justice led him to empower the  [Mageseekers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mageseekers "Universe:Mageseekers")—a decision he would later come to regret.
structure.abilities:
- **Leadership:** As the King of  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"), Jarvan III was responsible for all matters of diplomacy, including balancing the needs of its [noble houses](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noble_Houses_of_Demacia "Universe:Noble Houses of Demacia") and protecting the many citizens under his rule. His role placed him in command of all the elite soldiers of Demacia, including the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard"), which he used to combat the expansion of  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") across [Valoran](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Valoran "Universe:Valoran") and protect his allies, like [Kalstead](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kalstead "Universe:Kalstead").[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4)
- **Warrior:** In his prime, Jarvan III participated in numerous battles, and the  [Noxians](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") considered him a formidable warrior. Despite his age later in life, he remained healthy and strong until the day of his assassination.[[16]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-16)

relations.relationship_description:
Jarvan III was the father of Prince Jarvan, his only child and heir. He once described his son as his "life's joy", and would always try to pass the wisdom and values of the  [Demacian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") royal family onto him in hopes that he would one day become a good and just king.[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4) Jarvan IV loved and admired his father and would frequently try to prove himself worthy of the crown, even without his permission, which led to him nearly being killed by  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") forces.[[6]](#cite_note-JarvanBio-6)

Years later, during the [mage rebellion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Great_Mage_Rebellion "Universe:Great Mage Rebellion"), King Jarvan's death sent the prince into a spiraling grief and rage. His attempts to avenge his father led the kingdom into a full-blown civil war against  [Sylas](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sylas "Universe:Sylas") and his rebels, even though Jarvan III had spent his final days trying to stop the brewing conflict and halt the arrests of mages.[[6]](#cite_note-JarvanBio-6)[[15]](#cite_note-Mageseeker-15)

Jarvan III first met Xin Zhao after the Battle of [Kalstead](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kalstead "Universe:Kalstead"), where the famed  [Reckoner](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Reckoners "Universe:Reckoners") was given a chance to go in peace after sharing how he had been captured and forced to fight for in the  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") arenas in order to survive. Xin Zhao's story had resonated with King Jarvan, who likened it to the tales of Orlon and his followers seeking refuge from the world's many evils. Xin Zhao, too, had been moved by Jarvan's show of mercy, and judging him an honorable man, asked to enter his service as one of his guard. The king granted Xin Zhao's request, and in time, the former Viscero became Jarvan III's honored seneschal and trusted advisor, and one of his best friends.[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4)[[7]](#cite_note-XinBio-7)

As a  [Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Crownguard "Universe:House Crownguard"), Tianna was a devoted servant and protector of the king, a role she took great pride in for her and her family. She first served as Sword-Captain of the king's  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard") at the Battle of [Kalstead](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kalstead "Universe:Kalstead"), where she won a decisive victory, with only  [one](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xin_Zhao "Universe:Xin Zhao") of the enemy soldiers inflicting major casualties against the Demacians.[[4]](#cite_note-Sail-4) Tianna was later promoted to High Marshal following the battle at the [Gates of Mourning](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Gates_of_Mourning "Universe:Gates of Mourning"),[[5]](#cite_note-Fragile-5) a position she continued to hold after the king's death.

Lord Barrett of  [House Buvelle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Buvelle "Universe:House Buvelle") was the childhood best friend of Jarvan III. They first met when he was six years old, when the young prince was caught crying and fighting with another boy in the stables. Barrett had managed to calm Jarvan down by simply smiling and informing him that he expected better from the prince than to abuse a poor stable boy. Barrett had always impressed Jarvan with his kindness and wisdom, and for that, he was relied on frequently as an advisor later in life. Jarvan III truly believed Barrett made him a better man, and many of the programs he enacted to help the citizens of  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") were a direct result of his friend's influence.[[5]](#cite_note-Fragile-5)

After Barrett's death at the hands of  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") mages, Jarvan sought to avenge his death, even though he knew Barrett would not have approved. His decision to empower the  [Mageseekers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mageseekers "Universe:Mageseekers"), which he had thought would bring justice for his friend, instead placed Barrett's library and his  [daughter](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sona "Universe:Sona") in danger of scrutiny, while also leading the kingdom down a much darker path.[[5]](#cite_note-Fragile-5)

structure.name: Quinn
structure.quote: *"Most soldiers only rely on their weapons. Few truly rely on each other."*
structure.background:
### Early life

Quinn and her twin brother Caleb were born in [Uwendale](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Uwendale "Uwendale") to a weaponsmith and a ranger. When 7 [King Jarvan III](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:King_Jarvan_III "LoR:King Jarvan III") visited the village, they were impressed by the knights in their shining armor, and began to imitate them. Their father supported them in their endeavors, but as they grew older, the children took after their mother and spent time ranging in the wilds.

As young adults, Quinn and her brother were a formidable team of rangers, proficient in tracking and hunting prey. Quinn used a bow, while Caleb used a spear.

### Death of Caleb

Quinn and Caleb were hired to accompany a hunting parting of nobles from the capital. The nobles hunted a giant [Tuskvore](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tuskvore "Tuskvore"), but did not manage to kill it. The wounded beast turned on the hunters, and the twins intervened. As they drove off the creature, it killed Caleb. The leader of the nobles, 2 [Lord Barrett Buvelle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Honored_Lord "LoR:Honored Lord"), helped Quinn bury her brother, who saved their life.

The death of Caleb broke Quinn, she couldn't focus on her tasks and would often make mistakes in the wilderness. A few months after the incident, Lady Lestara  [Buvelle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Buvelle_House "Universe:Buvelle House") visited Quinn's family and asked what her house could do for the grieving family. Quinn did not have an answer for her; She politely thanked her for the offer and turned her away.

### The bond with Valor

One year after Caleb's death, Quinn returned to his grave as she often did. Due to her carelessness, she was taken by surprise when a tuskvore attacked her. She noticed it was the same beast that killed her brother, from the eye he took out before his death. Quinn fought the tuskvore, but found that she couldn't win. Just as it was about to kill her too, an [Azurite Eagle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Azurite_Eagle "Azurite Eagle") swooped in and distracted the creature. With this help, Quinn managed to kill the tuskvore.

She nursed the wounded bird back to health and named him  [Valor](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Valor "Universe:Valor"). The connection she felt with the eagle helped Quinn, and she once again contemplated how to serve  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"). With help from her father, she crafted her repeater crossbow, then journeyed to the [capital](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/The_Great_City_of_Demacia "The Great City of Demacia") to become a ranger-knight.

### Contemporary history

:   *Main article: [Fragile Legacies](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Fragile_Legacies "Fragile Legacies")*

At the funeral of Lord Barrett Buvelle, Quinn spoke with his widow Lestara Buvelle. Lestara expressed her gratitude for saving his life two years ago, and asked again how she could repay Quinn. Quinn hesitated at first, then asked Lady Buvelle to sponsor her for knighthood. Lestara agreed and spoke with  [Tianna Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tianna "Universe:Tianna"), and Quinn became a ranger-knight in the same week.

As ranger-knight, Quinn served in the Demacian military with her companion Valor. She has traveled far across Runeterra in her missions, including  [the Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord") and  [Noxian-held territories](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus").[[1]](#cite_note-1)

### Shield of Remembrance

:   *Main article: [Shield of Remembrance](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Shield_of_Remembrance "Shield of Remembrance")*

In the late autumn of [996 AN](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Timeline "Timeline"), Quinn received orders from  [Tianna Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tianna "Universe:Tianna"). She was to meet with  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen") and a detachment of the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard") and escort them to [Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Nockmirch "Nockmirch"), but was distracted by a burned cabin in the woods. There she met up with 3 [Greenfang Warden](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Greenfang_Warden "LoR:Greenfang Warden") Dalin, and decided to pursue the attackers. They tracked the group to the eastern border, where Quinn confronted them. She learned that the widow and her child who lived in the cabin were not abducted, but that she willingly returned to [Skaggorn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Skaggorn "Skaggorn") with her brother. It was forbidden to leave the country due to the ongoing rebellion, but the group knew of a secret passage unknown to the Demacian guards. Quinn decided to still let them go, ordering Dalin to stand down. She then told him to ensure a watchtower was built so this could not happen again, and ran off to make her original assignment.

### Nockmirch Expedition

:   *Main article: [Garen: First Shield](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Garen:_First_Shield "Garen: First Shield")*

After running through the forest for multiple days and nights, Quinn met with the Dauntless Vanguard and boarded the ship *"Stormbright"*. As ranger, it was her duty to scout ahead and make sure the environment was safe. She was the one to discover a fortified bridge spanning the ravine between [Rijenland](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Rijenland "Rijenland") and [Alderburg](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Alderburg "Alderburg"), and later discovered the  [noxian army](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") nearby. She rushed back to Alderburg to alert  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen"), and they left with the Vanguard. Quinn was supposed to make it back to Demacia and alert them, but she was wounded while trying to open the gates of the bridge for the trapped soldiers. Valor, despite also being wounded, made it out and managed to lead 5 [Silverwing riders](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Swiftwing_Lancer "LoR:Swiftwing Lancer") to the trapped Demacians. Quinn and the survivors then made it back to the [Great City](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/The_Great_City_of_Demacia "The Great City of Demacia") to recover from their wounds.

### Recent events

Quinn continues to lead the  [rangers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacian_Rangers "Universe:Demacian Rangers") in the fight against  [Sylas'](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sylas "Universe:Sylas") rebellion. Their involvement seems to help the soldiers.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
structure.appearance: Quinn is a lean, fierce-looking woman with stern features.[[3]](#cite_note-Ch3-3) She has amber eyes, described as similar to Valor's golden eyes.[[4]](#cite_note-Ch5-4) She usually wears light leather armor, and also travels with no or only a light pack. Quinn is almost always accompanied by her [Azurite Eagle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Azurite_Eagle "Azurite Eagle"), Valor.
structure.personality:
Quinn is friendly and well-liked with her subordinate rangers, rarely using her superior position to give direct orders. She takes her duty seriously and always tries to protect those she is in charge of. She does what is right, even when it goes against rules or the law.[[5]](#cite_note-Shield_of_Remembrance-5)

She is generally wary of strangers and "doesn't like people overmuch as a rule". She is more comfortable alone in the wild than among company.  [Cithria](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Cithria "Universe:Cithria") notes that she exudes an "easy confidence".[[3]](#cite_note-Ch3-3)
structure.abilities:
- **Ranger-Knight of Demacia**: Quinn is extremely proficient in hunting and tracking prey, both animals and humans. She can be patient and has attention to detail. She can conceal herself and her tracks well in the forest.
  - **Heightened Senses**: Her senses are far keener than the average.[[3]](#cite_note-Ch3-3)
- **Animal Bond**: Like most  [Demacian Rangers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacian_Rangers "Universe:Demacian Rangers"), she has a close bond to her companion,  [Valor](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Valor "Universe:Valor"). He is capable of understanding some of her commands.
  - Valor can take out a specific target that Quinn calls out, or distract enemy archers.
  - He can even carry her over short distances or when gliding down from heights.[[5]](#cite_note-Shield_of_Remembrance-5)
- **Athletic**: Quinn is a fast and endurant runner in the wilderness. She is able to run multiple days and nights with minimal rest. She can also sprint at high speeds, and is a nimble fighter.
- **Repeater Crossbow**: Quinn built this weapon with help from her father. Its firepower is weaker than a regular crossbow, but it can fire multiple bolts without having to reload.
- **Intelligence**: Quinn has shown excellent deduction capabilities.[[5]](#cite_note-Shield_of_Remembrance-5) By her own account, she speaks a dozen languages.[[4]](#cite_note-Ch5-4)

relations.relationship_description: Quinn's twin brother Caleb died while defending  [Barrett Buvelle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Barrett_Buvelle "Universe:Barrett Buvelle"), the adoptive father of  [Sona](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sona "Universe:Sona"), from a [tuskvore](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tuskvore "Universe:Tuskvore") attack. After his death, Lestara Buvelle petitioned to  [Tianna Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tianna "Universe:Tianna") to let Quinn become a ranger-knight.

Quinn is the leader of the  [Demacian Rangers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacian_Rangers "Universe:Demacian Rangers"), whose known members include 6 [Genevieve Elmheart](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Genevieve_Elmheart "LoR:Genevieve Elmheart") and her 5 [greathorn named Cern](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Greathorn_Companion "LoR:Greathorn Companion") , the [Yordle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Yordle "Yordle") 4 [Betrand](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Grizzled_Ranger "LoR:Grizzled Ranger") and 3 [his badgerbear Beemer](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Loyal_Badgerbear "LoR:Loyal Badgerbear"), the 3 [Greenfang Warden](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Greenfang_Warden "LoR:Greenfang Warden") Dalin and his dog Rigby. She's receives her orders from High Marshal  [Tianna Crownguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tianna "Universe:Tianna") and carries them out dutifully.

She has worked with  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen") and the  [Dauntless Vanguard](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Dauntless_Vanguard "Universe:Dauntless Vanguard") on their [expedition to the Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Garen:_First_Shield "Garen: First Shield"). Quinn and Garen like and respect each other.

structure.trivia:
- Her name derives from Proto-Celtic *\*kʷennom* "head, chief",[[6]](#cite_note-6) referencing [Conn of the Hundred Battles](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conn_of_the_Hundred_Battles).
  - Coincidentally, she is also the leader of the  [Demacian rangers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacian_Rangers "Universe:Demacian Rangers").
  - Her brother's name *Caleb* (כָּלֵב) means "dog" in Hebrew (after [the eponymous Biblical scout](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caleb)), from Proto-Semitic \**kalb-*.[[7]](#cite_note-7)
- Quinn is a ranger-knight. There are rangers in the  [Demacian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") military, but not all rangers have the rank and privileges of being knights. To be a knight, especially as a commoner, a person typically requires a sponsorship from a [noble house](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noble_Houses_of_Demacia "Universe:Noble Houses of Demacia"). The  [Buvelles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Buvelle "Universe:House Buvelle") did not just vouch for Quinn, they sponsored her ascension to becoming a knight and paid for and equipped her with the necessary resources that she would need.[[8]](#cite_note-8)
- Valor is shown playing  [Tellstones](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tellstones:_King%27s_Gambit "Tellstones: King's Gambit") with Quinn, even besting the ranger from time to time.[[9]](#cite_note-9)
- In the  [old lore](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Old_lore "Universe:Old lore"):
  - When receiving her scouting mission to the  [Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord") to assess the tribal situation there, she met  [Jarvan IV](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Jarvan_IV "Jarvan IV") and  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Garen "Garen"). Jarvan IV is 'not what she expected' while Garen is 'by the books' (Valor doesn't respect him).
  - Quinn and Valor [journeyed](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Journey_Into_The_Freljord "Universe:Journey Into The Freljord") into the  [Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord") at  [Jarvan IV's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Jarvan_IV "Jarvan IV") behest, managing to escape death by the  [Ice Witch's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Lissandra "Universe:Lissandra") hand.

structure.name: Azir
structure.quote: *"[Shurima](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Shurima "Shurima") was once the glory of [Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Runeterra "Runeterra"). I will make it so again."*
structure.background:
### Early life

Azir was the last son of the emperor of Shurima. He never received the same love from the emperor as did the other children. It was highly unexpected that he would be the one to become emperor. He spent most of his time studying the texts rather than training for combat.

Azir met a slave looking for texts for his master in the library. Surprisingly, he was able to help Azir understand complex grammar from an ancient text. The two quickly became friends after this, and Azir named the boy Xerath, even though slaves were not allowed names.

One day, while the royal family was travelling in the desert, they were attacked by assassins. Azir and Xerath had gone out to plot the stars. Xerath managed to suppress the attacker while Azir plunged a dagger into his throat. But Azir’s brothers had all been killed before Renekton managed to slay the assassins. Azir promised that one day, he and Xerath would be brothers.

Azir, now heir to the throne, began to train in combat under the tutelage of Renekton. He learned to wield the sword and spear.

Strangely, all the sons of the emperor’s wife began to die before they were born. Then one was finally born. But during a great storm, the emperor’s wife was killed along with her newborn son. It was said that the emperor went mad with grief and took his own life, leaving Azir to take the throne.

### The Catastrophic Ascension

Xerath had secretly longed for the power of ascension himself and saw Azir as a threat to his own aspirations; a world without slavery, and to end that, he secretly planned to guide Azir to the Dais of Ascension himself. On the day of Ascension, just as Azir is ascended-Xerath used his magic to subvert the ritual, causing it to fail and unleashing a catastrophic explosion that destroyed the capital city of Shurima, killing many of Azir's people in the process.

In the aftermath of the failed ascension, Azir was presumed dead, and Shurima fell into ruin and decay. However, Azir had actually ascended in a flawed and incomplete manner, becoming trapped in a state of suspended animation, his body and spirit separated from each other. Over the centuries, Azir's spirit remained dormant, while his body was preserved in a state of stasis within a chamber in The Sun Disc, an ancient structure that had been built to harness the power of the sun and the magic of the Ascended. It wasn't until the present day, when [The Sun Disc](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/The_Sun_Disc "The Sun Disc") was rediscovered and reactivated, that Azir's body was reawakened, and his spirit was reunited with it. When the tomb containing the Sun Disc and Azir was opened, chaos broke out and  [Sivir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sivir "Universe:Sivir")'s blood spilled over to the sand, awakening the falcon god in the process.

As Azir awakened, he was confronted by the brutal reality of his empire's decline and the treachery of those who had sought to undermine him, especially the now berserk  [Xerath](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xerath "Universe:Xerath"). Despite these obstacles, Azir remained determined to reclaim his throne and rebuild Shurima, using his newfound power and knowledge to unite his people and restore their former glory.
structure.appearance:
Azir is a tall male humanoid figure with features of a bird, specifically a falcon, his head is that of a golden falcon with blue eyes that shine like sapphires. He wears ancient golden Shuriman armor with red ribbons hanging from his arms and a white cape on his back.

When he was human, Azir was a brown-skinned man and quite stocky, with long dark hair tied in dreadlocks and various trappings of royalty.He didn't wear a shirt but his chest and arms were adorned with all kinds of Shuriman amulets and necklaces, he wore white baggy pants with red ribbons around his hips.
structure.personality:
Azir is a proud, determined ruler who sees potential in others. While he originally had no chance of being emperor, he befriended Xerath and saw him more than just a mere slave, but also a friend and even a brother. He wished to repay Xerath by giving him rewards and a higher status, but the societal values of Shurima prevented this. Despite this, Azir wished to become emperor to abolish slavery and give Xerath what he would've wanted, but his power led to him becoming hubristic, which was Azir's biggest weakness and one of the causes of Shurima's downfall. While he did have selfless intentions for the empire, his arrogance prevented him from communicating his goals with Xerath and seeing when he was being manipulated, and his shortsightedness towards the consequences of his actions caused Xerath's resentment to grow to the point where by the time he announced his plan, it was too late and Xerath had already made his decision to betray him.

Since his resurrection, Azir now wishes to rebuild the empire and return Shurima to its former glory is a very noble gesture, calling upon the help of his allies in order to do so.

However Azir has shown a quite noble and generous side, since one of the things he always wanted to do after becoming emperor was to abolish slavery and help the poor, he has shown a kinder side of him when he saved Sivir's life.
structure.abilities:
- **[Ascended](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Ascended "Ascended"):** Azir is an Ascended. The Ascended are mortals that were empowered by The Sun Disc into immensely powerful demigods. Each Ascended has unique powers depending on the individual they were prior to the Ascension.
  - **Regeneration:** Azir can heal from almost any injury in a matter of seconds.
  - **Superhuman Strength:** Azir is much stronger than any normal human.
  - **Immortality:** The ascended do not age, and do not need to eat or sleep. Barring beings of similar power, the Ascended cannot be killed.
  - **Sand Magic:** Azir can control the sands of the Shuriman desert to his desires, creating almost anything that he desires, like massive building and cities around him.
    - **Sand Soldiers:** Azir mainly uses his power over the sand to create his mighty Sand Soldiers, powerful constructs that serve as his personal army. The Sand Soldiers are completely under his control, are far more powerful than a normal human and don't need neither sleep nor food.

relations.relationship_description: [Xerath's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xerath "Universe:Xerath") treachery made Azir furious at his former soul brother betraying his trust to become an Ascended being and destroying Shurima in the process. He can't let go because he truly loved his nation, however much his ambition may have led him astray. He can't accept responsibility for what happened to his kingdom - he blames Xerath, but was it really Xerath's fault...? Or was it the emperor who couldn't see the cruel intent of his most trusted advisor - and friend? And yes - for the moment, he is an emperor without an empire. An emperor without a people. He has nothing - but he'll do everything with his newfound power to change that, and rebuild Shurima into the thriving, powerful empire it once was.

Given  [Ezreal's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ezreal "Universe:Ezreal") exploration of the Shurima Desert and robbing of artifacts from its tombs, it's likely Azir won't be entirely fond of him.

Azir dislikes  [Sivir's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sivir "Universe:Sivir") graverobbing but does not resent her. She is family after all, and saving her from  [Cassiopeia's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Cassiopeia "Cassiopeia") backstabbing meant everything at the time of his revival. He would hold his hatred for Cassiopeia for almost ending his bloodline forever.

When he was young, Azir was taught ancient knowledge from  [Nasus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Nasus "Universe:Nasus") and combat from  [Renekton](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Renekton "Universe:Renekton"). The Ascended brothers' teachings will prove useful for the trials ahead.

Azir is disappointed that a mighty warrior such as  [Renekton](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Renekton "Universe:Renekton") has been reduced to a rabid beast after being tortured beyond insanity for imprisoning himself with Xerath.

On the other hand,  [Nasus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Nasus "Universe:Nasus") might be the only remaining Ascended that can help the Emperor. Azir deeply respects Nasus, though the Curator looks down on him for his arrogance and for what his hubris did to Shurima.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

structure.trivia:
- Azir is inspired by the Egyptian gods [Horus](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horus) and [Ra](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ra).
- Based on the timeline in [Realms of Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Realms_of_Runeterra "Realms of Runeterra") and his lore, Azir is between 3000 – 3050 years old.
- As suggested by  [Taliyah's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Taliyah "Taliyah") quote  *"Close to the ground, the sparrow flies faster than the falcon."*, his Ascended form resembles that of a falcon.
- Azir's mother was born in [Vekaura](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Vekaura "Vekaura").  [Xerath](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xerath "Universe:Xerath") later destroyed the city during the events of [Bloodline](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Bloodline "Bloodline").
  - Azir originally intended to destroy [Saikhal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Saikhal "Saikhal"),  [Xerath's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Xerath "Xerath") birthplace, for revenge but was convinced not to as he was reminded that it would make him the same thing as what Xerath has become.
    - Azir knows a lot of secrets about  [Xerath's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Xerath "Xerath") past that are only known to the two.
- As stated by Riot Opeli in Azir's Q&A thread, Azir was a benevolent leader, a kind dictator devoted to his people's well-being and prosperity. Though he got a little ahead of himself with the over-enthusiastic Ascension ritual, even that was done with good intentions, for he saw Ascension as a means to have Shurima grow and influence the entire world.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
  - This desire was never derived from conquest, as Azir truly believes Shurima was the pinnacle of civilization and could only continue to prosper.
  - Azir put off abolishing slavery because doing so in a short period of time would likely lead to massive protests and possibly a coup. As power went to his head, however, he forgot that others also had worthwhile ideas.
  - Azir currently wishes for the other city-states to join his empire so that they may benefit from Shurima's culture and way of life. This might prove difficult after being trapped in limbo for millennia, given the likes of [Zaun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Zaun "Zaun") are the antithesis to Shurima.
    - So for now, Azir's motivation is to restore Shurima's glory.
  - Back in the empire's heyday, Azir was popular with the ladies.[[3]](#cite_note-3) This charisma might help him restore his people to greatness.
- As stated by [Gem 'Lonewingy' Lim](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Gem_%27Lonewingy%27_Lim "Gem 'Lonewingy' Lim") in Azir's Q&A thread, Azir's gauntlets have ribbon-like tassels to emphasize his regal status and to resemble embroidered robes which in turn represent feathers, cementing the bird-like appearance.[[4]](#cite_note-4)
- [Xerath's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Xerath "Xerath") Ascended power was stolen from Azir, but manifests in the wrong way due to its not being intended for him.
- At the end of [Twilight of the Gods](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Twilight_of_the_Gods "Twilight of the Gods"),  [the Chalicar](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Sivir#Boomerang_Blade "Sivir") had absorbed the - for want of a better phrase - Darkin DNA essence, which, combined with Ta'anari's heart, would allow humans to craft the weapons tailored to trap the remaining Darkin at a later date.[[5]](#cite_note-5) Tomb of Emperors is Shuriman, but the events of the story imbued the Chalicar with a resonance to the Ascended, so it acted as a channel between  [Sivir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sivir "Universe:Sivir") and her distant ancestor, Azir which allowed her blood to revive him. As the Alchemists of Old said, "Like attracts like...".[[6]](#cite_note-6)
- **Azir's Q&A (Creative)** by [Riot Narrative team](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Category:Riot_Games_staff "Category:Riot Games staff") : (Note: In case people question the authenticity of the contents above, the copy-and-paste version of the orginal text is added here: [[7]](#cite_note-7) )
  - 1. What kind of a ruler was he?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): He was a benevolent leader. Still a dictator, but a kind one, and he was interested in his people's well-being and prosperity. He got a little ahead of himself, though - hence the over-enthusiastic Ascension ritual - but even that was done with good intentions. He wanted Shurima to grow and influence the entire world.
  - 2. Why can't Azir just let go his lost empire? What he gonna rule there anyway, sands? Though I can somehow see him modeling his whole empire with sand then play empire in his head. Now I kinda got sad for him...
    - [Riot-Runaan](https://web.archive.org/web/20200315031328/https://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/RiotRunaan): He can't let go because he truly loved his nation, however much his ambition may have led him astray. He can't accept responsibility for what happened to his kingdom - he blames Xerath, but was it really Xerath's fault...? Or was it the emperor who couldn't see the cruel intent of his most trusted advisor - and friend? :O And yes - for the moment, he is an emperor without an empire. An emperor without a people. He has nothing - but he'll do everything with his newfound power to change that, and rebuild Shurima into the thriving, powerful empire it once was.
  - 3. Does Azir plan to rebuild Shurima?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): Yes! It's his main motivation.
  - 4. Does Azir wish to just peacefully rebuild Shurima and see if people join his ways? Or will he do it with force?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): He wishes to do it peacefully, but he's not afraid of using force. It will only happen if he's forced his hand.
  - 5. What's the CURRENT state of Shurima? We've heard that it's been swallowed by the desert, and that Xerath, apparently, blew up the city, but...An empire isn't just one city. What about the rest of Shurima? What did they do for the world around them when they were at their prime?
    - [Riot-Runaan](https://web.archive.org/web/20200315031328/https://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/RiotRunaan): We talked about Shurima as a place with a really thriving culture - a place with not only a strong military and a powerful emperor, but a place with a sense of personal identity (art, music, literature, trade, magical technology etc). Azir's motivation to bring the golden light of Shurima to other nations was/is not really a "conquering" aim - it's that he truly believes that Shurima was the height of civilization, and could only continue to grow more wonderful. After Xerath's corrupt ascension, everything was more or less buried beneath the sands and left to ruin, but Azir definitely doesn't think that's the end of things.
  - 6. Did Azir have any inkling that Xerath was going to betray him, or was he blind to that possibility?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): He was blind to it. He totally trusted Xerath. :(
  - 7. Did Azir rule alone, or would there have been a...Mrs. Azir?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): It's safe to say he was... popular with the ladies.
  - 8. What does Azir think of Nasus? Does he respect him or dislike him?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): Azir deeply respects Nasus. Although Nasus views him as a little arrogant because he got to see what happened to Shurima as a result of Azir's hubris.
  - 9. What does Azir think of Yordles? Does Azir know Anivia at all or have any relation to her? Did Azir ALWAYS love birds?
    - [Riot-Entropy](https://web.archive.org/web/20150922130948mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Riot%20Entropy): Azir would welcome their furry enthusiasm, provided they directed it toward expanding Shurima's greatness. Azir was once human, so he's a great deal younger than Anivia. Nasus on the other hand... Birds soar to great heights. I can't help but think Azir would admire that.
  - 10. Does (Ascended) Azir sleep in a bed or a nest? If it's a nest, what's it made of?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): I don't think he sleeps! At all!
  - 11. Given the fact that the Shurimans aren't the only sun revering culture, what does Azir think of Mount Targon and the Solari?
    - [Riot-Entropy](https://web.archive.org/web/20150922130948mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Riot%20Entropy): At the very least, intrigued. Though one can't help but wonder if once the whole "You like the Sun? Me too!" phase passes they might have some serious differences to sort out.
  - 12. How much of Runeterra (regions, city states etc.) does Azir know/remember from old-Shuriman days? How much has changed for him?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): For some people, Shurima is like an Atlantis to them - they believe it's only a myth (although, obviously, they will be proven wrong). For others, like the people currently inhabiting the desert of Shurima, they knew it existed a long time ago and there are believed to be no "true" Shurimans remaining. Even Renekton and Nasus were stories for them. A LOT has changed for Azir. He has a lot of catching up to do.
  - 13. Was he always so...birdy? I mean he has fabulous legs but I wonder were they like that when he was young and...alive?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): No, he was human originally. But I also think he has fabulous legs. :P
  - 14. Now that he is returned, what are his views on the other City-States like Noxus and Piltover?
    - [Riot-Opeli](https://web.archive.org/web/20150909033638mp_/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/player/NA/Opeli): Azir believes that the other city-states would benefit from Shurima's culture and way of life. He'll try to get them to join his empire and conform to his ideals. HOWEVER, he is in for quite the culture shock because so much has changed while he's been... away. I think Zaun would boggle him the most. But he wouldn't let anyone see that.
