structure.name: Norra
structure.background:
She lives in a vine-covered cottage nestled deep in the forest, accompanied by her magical cat, Yuumi. A curious yordle enchantress, she spent her days collecting odd artifacts—shattered pottery, colorful glass shards, and intricately stitched fabrics—each a puzzle to unravel. Yuumi, ever the loyal companion, used her protective magic to shield Norra on their adventures across realms.

Their journeys were guided by Norra’s  [Book of Thresholds](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Book_of_Thresholds "Universe:Book of Thresholds"), a powerful tome that opened portals to distant places.

One night, Norra vanished through a perilous portal, resulting destroying the portal. Stranded in a mysterious dimension, she worked tirelessly to find her way back, thoughts of her cozy cottage and Yuumi driving her onward.
structure.appearance: Norra is a yordle with a bunny-like appearance, wearing large, round glasses framed in purple. She wears a tall, colorful hat decorated with blue and pink feathers and a wide brim with red and white accents. She is dressed in a long, flowing purple robe with intricate patterns, gold and blue accents, and a red scarf or sash. She accessorizes with a necklace featuring a large white gemstone and a bracelet with a blue gem on her right hand.
structure.personality: Norra is a delightful mix of whimsy, curiosity, and resilience.
structure.abilities:
- **Yordle Physiology:** Norra is a Yordle, a being coming from the [Spirit Realm](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Spirit_Realm "Spirit Realm") and possesses several abilities natural of her species.
  - **Immortality:** Being spiritual beings, Yordles don't age the same way as normal humans, and they can't normally die.
  - **Yordle Magic:** Just like any [Yordle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Yordle "Yordle"), Norra is capable of performing yordle magic.
    - **Portal Conjuration**: Norra is a master at conjuring inter-dimensional portals that lead to and fro the material or spirit realms
    - **Paper Enchantment**: Norra can use her magic to create papercraft objects that magically assume properties of their real counterparts, examples include [puffcaps](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Teemo "Teemo"), [flashtraps](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Caitlyn "Caitlyn"), [chimes](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Bard "Bard") etc

relations.relationship_description: [Yuumi](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yuumi "Universe:Yuumi") and  [Book of Thresholds](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Book_of_Thresholds "Universe:Book of Thresholds") are currently looking for her.

structure.name: Rhaast
structure.quote: *"I will survive eternity. They will die today."*
structure.background:
### Early Life

When Rhaast was chosen for Ascension, his fellow Ascended,  [Zaahen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaahen "Universe:Zaahen"), helped guide the ceremony. Rhaast's wit and ambition were as sharp as his scythe.[[1]](#cite_note-ZaahenBio-1) Before the ritual, he gifted a beaded belt to a [friend](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Forsaken_Baccai "LoR:Forsaken Baccai") who would later become a [Baccai](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Baccai "Universe:Baccai").[[2]](#cite_note-2)

After enduring the horrors of the Void and the [Shuriman Empire fell](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Fall_of_Shurima "Universe:Fall of Shurima"), Rhaast, like the other remaining Ascended, became purposeless and their older, petty ambitions resurfaced. They taught themselves forbidden sorceries, and came to view themselves as the rightful inheritors of the world. They declared themselves *Sunborn* and clashed with both each other and the mortal races. Their battles brought so much devastation that the mortals eventually began to call these Sunborn *[Darkin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Darkin "Darkin")*, an old Shuriman word which most closely translated to *The Fallen*.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Rhaast eventually made his way to  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia"), along with several other Darkin, and amassed an army of followers to conquer the land. His former Ascended brother  [Zaahen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaahen "Universe:Zaahen") followed them to the First Lands and aided the  [Kinkou Order](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kinkou_Order "Universe:Kinkou Order") in ending their carnage, ultimately sealing Rhaast within his scythe.[[4]](#cite_note-Truth-4) During his confrontation with Zaahen, the two fought for many days and nights, even as their mortal allies rested to count their dead. Zaahen offered Rhaast a chance to fight beside him again—as he had with all his brethren he hunted—but Rhaast, like the others, refused, reveling in his newfound power. He questioned why Zaahen had not joined them, declaring that they were the new masters of this world. As they exchanged blows, Zaahen replied that they were the masters of nothing and if the Darkin could not be saved, they had to be destroyed.[[1]](#cite_note-ZaahenBio-1)

Rhaast became known one as one of the five Darkin that will bring ruin to the world when they reunite, along with  [Aatrox](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Aatrox "Universe:Aatrox"),  [Varus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Varus "Universe:Varus"),  [Naafiri](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Naafiri "Universe:Naafiri"), and an unnamed fifth Darkin.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

### Finding a Host

Centuries later, during the Noxian invasion of  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia"), Rhaast's scythe was unearthed and was to be transfered to  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"). Unwilling to let Noxus use a Darkin against their homeland,  [Zed](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zed "Universe:Zed") of the  [Order of Shadow](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Order_of_Shadow "Universe:Order of Shadow") sent his pupil,  [Shieda Kayn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kayn "Universe:Kayn"), to intercept them.[[6]](#cite_note-KaynBio-6) Kayn and his fellow acolyte Nakuri ambushed the Noxian caravan. One desperate Noxian attempted to wield Rhaast to defend himself, but Kayn easily dispatched him. As Kayn picked up the weapon, Rhaast whispered to him, urging him to prove himself worthy of his power. Nakuri urged Kayn to destroy the Darkin, but he refused. Kayn killed Nakuri and claimed the scythe as his own.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

While Kayn saw Rhaast as a tool to help him one day lead the Order of Shadow, Rhaast saw Kayn as the ideal host to free himself from his imprisonment. Due to Kayn's strong will, Rhaast was unable to fully overtake him, leaving the two locked in a battle of wills to determine who would control whom.[[6]](#cite_note-KaynBio-6) When Kayn is not wielding Rhaast, the Darkin's corruption recedes from his body.[[8]](#cite_note-8)
structure.appearance:
Rhaast's consciousness is sealed within his Darkin Scythe. Mirroring the build of Rhaast itself, the scythe seems to be made of hardened blood and steel, reflecting the body of the Darkin, contorted and reshaped by Hemomancy. It is jagged with serrated blades along the edge of it's heel, and it possesses a red eye with a slitted pupil.

When in his physical form, Rhaast is a substantially larger being, towering over most humans and other humanoid creatures. His body is primarily made of a dark red like chitin, with his arms and head made of a steel-like armor that likely is grafted to his skin. He also possesses two blade-like horns that branch out from the side of his head and curl in at the top. His eyes are a blank red and his sharp teeth are bared like a skulls'.

In this form, having taken Kayn's body, he possesses Kayn's pants and belt with minor color changes, although he seemingly uses the boots as bare legs. While wielding it in this form, the scythe's pupil also becomes jagged and the blade gains teeth.
structure.personality:
Unlike the other Darkin, who have a clear purpose for their carnage, Rhaast takes an almost childish joy in his quest for destruction and bloodshed.

In his unleashed form, Rhaast is incredibly hammy and arrogant, maniacally laughing at his own evil deeds and appearing excited whenever he kills someone. Rhaast loves wisecracks almost as much as he hates humans, sarcastically joking that his dead victims should "walk it off" since he was hardly even trying.

Despite this, Rhaast is capable of patience, as in his scythe form, Rhaast is able to tone back his bloodlust in favor of attempting to carefully manipulate Kayn over a long period of time. But Rhaast is always ready to murder, and will gladly tell Kayn to do so.
structure.abilities:
- **[Darkin Physiology:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Darkin "Universe:Darkin")** Rhaast is a Darkin, originally one of the many [Ascended](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Ascended "Ascended") God-Warriors of Shurima in ancient times trapped within a weapon. As a Darkin, Aatrox has immense physical strength, gigantic size and access to some celestial magics.
- **[Hemomancy](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kayn#The_Darkin_Scythe_R "Kayn"):** Rhaast, just like any Darkin, has blood magic abilities, able to use blood as a weapon as well as a tool.
  - **Body Manipulation:** Rhaast can take over and change the form of the body of any mortal that wields Rhaast's scythe. In order to change the form of their body, however, Rhaast needs to kill others and use their flesh and blood to change his form.
- **Ascension:** Rhaast, just like any Darkin, started out as a Sunborn, which granted him immense physical abilities, gigantic size and access to celestial magics.
  - **Immortality:** Rhaast is immortal. His consciousness is trapped within his weapon, and the weapon is indestructible. There is no known way to permanently kill Rhaast.
- **Scythe Proficiency:** Rhaast is trained in the use of his scythe, which is imbued with magic of the Ascended. He uses this in battle and killed the many with it.
  - **[Darkin Scythe](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kayn#Reaping_Slash_R "Kayn"):** Rhaast wields his scythe, now being known as the Darkin Scythe.

relations.relationship_description:
Rhaast regards most of his fellow Darkin as his brothers and sisters, having fought alongside and against them during the Great Darkin War. Although his relationship with many of them is not defined, he has a common enemy in  [Xolaani](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xolaani "Universe:Xolaani"), likely having conflicted against her along with Aatrox. Unlike his methodical siblings, however, Rhaast is largely impulsive and considered to be too brash in his bloodlust, often garnering disapproval from his fellow Darkin.

#### [Aatrox](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Aatrox "Universe:Aatrox")

Being brothers in arms, Aatrox and Rhaast share common goals and similar fates tied to their origin as both Sunborn and Darkin. Having a deep kinship and mutual respect for one another, it is likely that they trust each other with little hesitation.

Though along with this fellowship, Aatrox seemingly harbors a somewhat scornful view of Rhaast, criticizing him for both his choice in weapon and failure to overtake Kayn as a host.

#### [Varus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Varus "Universe:Varus")

Unlike his relationship with Aatrox, which may be tainted with a slight form of disdain, Rhaast possibly possesses a different sort of filial relationship with the Darkin archer. Having fought alongside him in both The Great Darkin War and the War of The False Kanmei, it is evident that the two Darkin are commonly seen next to one another, and likely were captured in Ionia at the same time.

Within various interactions, both Rhaast and Varus' dialogue with one another resemble quippy exchanges, with Varus casually discussing choice of vessels, and Rhaast referring to him as 'Demon Pants'.

Nevertheless, Varus, much like the other Darkin, still chastises Rhaast for his lack of impulse control, accusing him of making the other Darkin seem foolish.

#### [Naafiri](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Naafiri "Universe:Naafiri")

As one of his Darkin siblings, it is assumed that Rhaast and Naafiri have great history. Having been released from imprisonment since finding a host, Naafiri has now begun to search for him along with the other three Darkin that made up their primary force, looking to bring them all together to claim the world once and for all.

Naafiri remarks that she greatly approves of Rhaast's choice in vessel, but similarly to their siblings, she deems Rhaast's inability to overtake Kayn as 'unfortunate'.

#### [Kayn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kayn "Universe:Kayn")

In a currently fruitless internal battle with the young assassin, Rhaast's relationship with Kayn persists as both complicated and conflicted.

Despite being in a consistently aggressive fight for power, the two continue to work symbiotically in order to achieve their common goals of killing their targets, often sharing a mutual enthusiasm for the blood they spill together.

Throughout the majority of their interactions, both Rhaast and Kayn retain a level of somewhat friendly banter in the face of their obstruction of each other's desires, their sarcastic remarks rarely proceeding beyond surface-level teasing insults.

When overtaking Kayn in the conceptual future, Rhaast often mentions him in his goading, referring to him as 'the great Kayn' and consistently using his succession of him as a point of pride.

#### [Zed](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zed "Universe:Zed")

Possessing a somewhat indifferent view of Zed, Rhaast still appears to hold Zed in lesser respect than he does Kayn, often mocking him and his organization.

Rhaast also comments that Zed's order 'shackles Kayn', although this may simply be a mere form of manipulation to convince Kayn to give Rhaast his body.

structure.name: Kalista
structure.quote: *"Turncoats, oath breakers and betrayers… we hate them all."*
structure.background:
### Early Life

Kalista was born in the long-forgotten kingdom of  [Camavor](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Camavor "Universe:Camavor"), as the daughter of the heir to the Argent Throne and the niece of  [Viego](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viego "Universe:Viego"). Despite being his niece, Kalista and Viego were close in age and was one of his closest friends, acting as a big sister towards him. Eventually her father passed and when her grandfather was on his deathbed, he tasked her with monitoring Viego's reign, due to him being unprepared to rule. Kalista served him with utmost loyalty as the general of Camavor. Viego would fall in love with  [Isolde](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Isolde "Universe:Isolde") and two would soon wed. Kalista saw Isolde as a sister and enjoyed the positive influence she had on her uncle.

When Viego was targeted by an assassin sent to kill him with a poisoned blade, Kalista deflected the blade in time but accidentally caused it to graze Isolde instead. With the best medics and priests in Camavor unable to save her, a grief-stricken Viego sent Kalista, along with the captain of the Iron Order,  [Hecarim](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Hecarim "Universe:Hecarim"), to find a cure. While most nations were unable to give her the results she wanted, she learned of the  [Blessed Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Blessed_Isles "Universe:Blessed Isles") and was able to get the Waters of Life that could cure even the direst of ailments. But when she got back, Isolde had already succumbed to the poison. Viego, maddened by grief, saw Kalista as a traitor to the crown and got her imprisoned.

### Invasion of the Blessed Isles

In the dungeons, Kalista was visited by Hecarim, who manipulated her into revealing the location of the Blessed Isles all so he could reap glory for himself. Hecarim then told Viego about the information she gave him, which led to the fleets of Camavor sailing to the capital of the Blessed Isles, [Helia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Helia "Helia").

However, the elders of the Blessed Isles refused to let the Camavorans pass, as they believed that death was final and to cheat it would break the natural order of the world. Viego ignored their warnings and ordered Kalista to kill them. She refused and tried to get Hecarim to stand with her, but he and his knights killed her by driving their spears into her back, before killing her lover  [Ledros](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ledros "Universe:Ledros") and all the Camavoran soldiers loyal to her. Then, they began to raid the Blessed Isles, looting their treasures and killing all of the natives they could find. But thanks to Viego's failed attempt to revive his wife, the Blessed Isles' protective barrier was tainted by the magic of Viego's  [blade](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Blade_of_the_Ruined_King "Blade of the Ruined King"), causing a disaster which turned it into the ghostly realm now known as the  [Shadow Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shadow_Isles "Universe:Shadow Isles").

### Spirit of Vengeance

Many of the people within the Isles at the time of the Ruination, both living and dead, were reborn as ghostly [wraiths](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Wraith "Wraith"). Kalista was one such wraith, who remembered nothing but her feelings of vengeance toward Hecarim as she died. She became a spirit of vengeance, travelling all over Runeterra to appear before those who made pacts in her name, absorbing their souls to kill the ones whom had betrayed them. But with each soul she absorbed, her humanity disappeared as she became a hive mind of vengeful souls who avenged the wronged across Runeterra.
structure.appearance:
In life, Kalista was a woman with an athletic physique, brown skin, brown eyes, and long, flowing black hair. Her regal Camavoran armor was blue plate with a gold trim. She wore a cloth around the back of her legs and an open-faced helmet with a long, dark plume. She wielded a spear.

In death, Kalista is a translucent, teal spirit. She appears emaciated and hunched, with several spectral spears protruding from her torso. While her armor remains opaque, it is now black and dark brown with tattered cloth portions. Her spears, which now materialize in her hands, are jagged and spectral.
structure.personality:
While being of royal blood, Kalista was surprisingly down to earth in life and had a strong sense of justice. She got along far better with the common footsoldiers in the military than the nobles trying to curry favour with her. She was also depicted as caring sister figure to a young  [Viego](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viego "Universe:Viego") when he suddenly was to be crowned as king of  [Camavor](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Camavor "Universe:Camavor") and tried to be his emotional and moral support during his reign, with some help from  [Isolde](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Isolde "Universe:Isolde").

When she became a wraith, Kalista lost much of her humanity. With only the memories of betrayals she has suffered in her life, an intense thirst for revenge persisted, becoming a vengeful spirit.
structure.abilities:
- **Wraith:** Kalista is one of the Shadow Isles's wraiths, created when the Ruination came to be. The Black Mist consumes ones original personality, leaving only a specter consumed by negative emotions and obsessions. In Kalista's case, she became an spirit of vengeance after being betrayed in life.
  - **Immortality:** Being already dead, Kalista can't die again. She can only be banished and loose her material form for a while.
  - **Spiritual Construction:** Wraiths can create solid constructs from spectral energy, such as bodies and physical objects. These constructs mainly base themselves around how they looked in life.
  - **Transitory State:** Being ethereal beings, Wraiths can shift from the physical world and spiritual one at will. This means they can become intangible and invisible, and teleport from one place to another.
  - **Spirit of Vengeance:** After dying, Kalista became a vengeful spirit that hunts down others that have betrayed their oaths. This grants her many terrible powers.
    - **Pacts of Vengeance:** If someone craving vengeance call upon Kalista, she will come to their aid and grant them their vengeance, stalking her mark until they die by her spears.
    - **Soul Absorption:** When the pact is done, the dying will be absorbed inside Kalista and became part of an endless vortex of souls inside of her.
- **Trained Warrior:** Kalista is a incredible warrior that can easly defeat many foes in battle.

relations.relationship_description: Kalista is the  [Ruined King's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viego "Universe:Viego") niece and was one of his generals in life. Kalista's father was the previous king of  [Camavor](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Camavor "Universe:Camavor"). Viego became the king after his brother died in battle. Despite being her uncle, Kalista and Viego were around the same age and friends for a long time since he was largely ignored in favor of Kalista's father. When her father died and Viego became king, his negative traits were worsened and they began to drift apart, however she was still loyal to him. Kalista managed to protect Viego from an assassin, but resulted in Isolde getting poisoned instead. She would set sail in order to find a cure, but found it too late and was imprisoned as a traitor for her failure.She was eventually convinced by  [Hecarim](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Hecarim "Universe:Hecarim") to lead  [Viego](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viego "Universe:Viego") and their army to the Blessed Isles for the Waters of Life. When the masters of the island refused to let them use the water, Viego ordered her to kill anyone who opposed them. Kalista refused and was stabbed by Hecarim before her forces clashed with the Iron Order.

[Commander Ledros](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ledros "Universe:Ledros") was her lover in life and is trying to free her soul.  [Thresh](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Thresh "Universe:Thresh") tried to persuade him to give up trying to free  **Kalista** and so far has succeeded at obtaining his silver pendant which Ledros may use to remind Kalista of her humanity, but Ledros instead has tried to end the curse of the Ruination himself.

[Hecarim](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Hecarim "Universe:Hecarim") and his Iron Order are now restlessly hunted and "killed" by her, but they always come back due to the Black Mist.

[Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir") was soul-marked by Kalista but he was able to banish her with the help of a magical artifact. He was a prince of Camavor, and Viego and Kalista's distant relative who was centuries old by the time they were born.
Kalista occasionally comes after  [Tahm Kench](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tahm_Kench "Universe:Tahm Kench"); however, he is safe from her due to his contracts with the victims.

In her journey to the Blessed Isles, Kalista crossed paths with  [Ryze](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ryze "Universe:Ryze") during his formative years. Initially, she found the young apprentice brimming with arrogance and entitlement, reminiscent of her uncle,  [Viego](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viego "Universe:Viego"). Their first encounter ended with Ryze's arm twisted, after which Ryze started to be far more respectful towards the Camavoran princess.

When hearing had Kalista sacrificed herself in order to give the people of Helia a chance to escape from the invading Camavorans, Ryze regretted not having had the opportunity to apologize for their initial meeting.

structure.trivia:
- Kalista is between 1050 years old, born at some point before the Ruination of the  [Blessed Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Blessed_Isles "Universe:Blessed Isles").
  - She was in her 20s, roughly the same age as  [Viego](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viego "Universe:Viego") during the first Ruination.
  - She's old enough for legends to spread about her across the world. Every place has a different, but similar story about summoning her.
- According to  [Viego's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Viego "Viego") biography, her kingdom was from an unknown continent outside of the known map.
- 'The Spear of Vengeance' (the specter Kalista became after the  [Ruination](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Blade_of_the_Ruined_King "Blade of the Ruined King")) is a [hivemind](https://web.archive.org/web/0/http://boards.na.leagueoflegends.com/en/c/gameplay-balance/qlEEXEiO-kalista-qa-completed?comment=02450000) of betrayed souls (hence she referring to herself as 'we') while Kalista herself is buried deep beneath them all, with every new soul burying her ever-deeper within the entity she has become. Very little of who she once was remains, but it surfaces occasionally.  [Ledros](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ledros "Universe:Ledros") almost managed to free her from her curse.
  - Kalista is one of the strongest characters from [Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Runeterra "Runeterra"), being basically the Avatar of Vengeance at this point.
  - She would feel all sorts of things in the moments when she is more lucid; remorse, anger, regret, sadness, grief, rage...
- Her spears are the spectral remnants of the way she was originally murdered.
  - She would have used a spear in life. She was a heroic leader - think of her as having been kind of female (and honorable) Achilles.
- Kalista is a lawful neutral character who acts according to both her drive to enact vengeance on betrayers and her own law.
  - Her 'alignment' depends on one's perspective - it's all in the eye of the beholder. To some, she would be seen as evil because she is an undying spirit, full stop. However, she was a hero in life, and very much an honorable one at that. She didn't ask to become what she is, and is now consumed with enacting vengeance. So, to some, she might be seen as an avenger, a spirit of justice. To those she is pursuing? They'd probably think she is evil - she certainly couldn't be bargained or argued with, and she'd see things very much in black and white. What if someone did do a horrible betrayal, but has atoned for it? She'd not be bothered with those kind of details...
    - She'd be very black and white, it is possible even if someone may have a very good reason for betraying someone, in her eyes just the fact that there is betrayal may damn them in her eyes.
    - She is also very focused. She's not an indiscriminate killer, and would not destroy everything in her path to get to her target. She's got all the time in the world (she'd not exactly got to worry about ageing any more...), so she can be patient in order to get her target without involving unnecessary deaths.
- Kalista can travel mystically across Valoran, and there's no escaping her once she's got her target without using powerful spirit magic, as  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir") did in the story [The Daring Darling](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/The_Daring_Darling "The Daring Darling").

structure.name: Amara
structure.background:
### Early Life

Not much is known about Amara's early life. At some point during her younger years, she made a fortune as a merchant in  [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover") and had a son named Rohan. Secretly, she was also a [mage](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic") inducted into the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose"), and would protect the cabal's interests by spying on the people of Piltover.

### Piltovan Bicentennial

In exchange for her generous donations to the esteemed Piltover Academy, Amara was allowed certain leniencies in regard to her trading ventures.[[1]](#cite_note-1) Thus, she was one of the several people affected when the newly-appointed Councilor  [Jayce Talis](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jayce "Universe:Jayce"), in his desire to ensure the safety and protection of the Hexgate, ordered the  [Piltover Enforcers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover_Enforcers "Universe:Piltover Enforcers") to strictly inspect and seize all illegal merchandise that went through them.[[2]](#cite_note-105enemy-2)

With her business now in legal trouble, Amara went to Councilor  [Irius Bolbok](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Bolbok "Universe:Bolbok") for help and he offered to make other possible arrangements to ensure that the leniencies that she once enjoyed remained intact. However, when Councilor  [Mel Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mel "Universe:Mel") informed Jayce of this development, he decided to try a different approach and told Amara that he was looking for new investors for his [hextech](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Hextech "Universe:Hextech") research and that she would be first in line to any hextech advancements that he made if she chose to support him. Delighted at the chance of obtaining hextech advancements for herself, Amara eagerly accepted Jayce's offer, which lead him to make similar offers with everyone else who had been affected by his decision to tighten security around the Hexgate.[[2]](#cite_note-105enemy-2)

### Arrival of General Medarda

After the Black Rose had killed  [Ambessa Medarda's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa") son  [Kino](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kino "Universe:Kino"), Ambessa took her warband to Piltover to meet with her daughter, who happened to be Councilor Medarda.[[3]](#cite_note-3) The general's sudden arrival caught Amara's attention and she began requesting in-person meetings with her, but Ambessa refused every time. The next few days were tumultuous, and after a  [terrorist attack](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Jinx#Super_Mega_Death_Rocket! "Jinx") killed three of Piltover's councilors, Amara was present at the service for them. The service was soon attacked by  [Zaunite](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaun "Universe:Zaun") terrorists and eventually put down by Ambessa herself.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

### Death & Legacy

At some point after the attack, Ambessa finally accepted Amara's requests for a meeting, and she arrived to discuss a certain "debt," referring to a [child](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mel "Universe:Mel") of Ambessa's that she had hidden away from them. Amara ambushed Ambessa and her lieutenant,  [Rictus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rictus "Universe:Rictus"), with magic, and revealed herself as a Black Rose agent. Amara tried to kill Ambessa, but the general bested Amara and ended her life. Amara promised that her death would mean nothing, warning Ambessa that she should have given up the feud.

Ambessa later covered up Amara's connection to the Black Rose, blaming her death on Zaunite assassins and using the fabricated incident as one of her excuses to instate martial law in Piltover.[[5]](#cite_note-5)
structure.appearance: Amara was an elderly woman with gray hair, very pale skin, and dark purple eyes. She was often seen wearing expensive Piltovan clothing with red gems and golden accessories. She also wore purple eye-shadow, dark burgundy lipstick, and a burgundy marking resembling a [Bindi](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bindi_(decoration)) on her forehead.
structure.personality: Amara was shrewd and cunning, and was able to easily dance her way through Piltovan politics. She cared a great deal about her business and showed no hesitation in confronting those who obstructed her for any reason. She was also open to making lucrative business deals, even if it meant crossing lines and causing corruption. Secretly, Amara lived a double life as an agent of the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose"), and she would exercise this same ruthlessness in service to the cabal.
structure.abilities:
- **[Mage](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic"):** As a member of the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose"), Amara had access to their magic and could summon  [dark ethereal chains](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LeBlanc#Ethereal_Chains "LeBlanc") covered in thorns to ensnare her enemies, and was able to mold these thorns into the shape of a dark metal dagger.
- **Merchant:** Amara was a successful trading merchant, given that she was able to secure business deals with many important figures among the  [Piltovan](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover") elite.

relations.relationship_description: At some point in her life, Amara learned she was a mage and was inducted into the ranks of the Black Rose cabal, eventually serving as an agent to defend their interests in  [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover"). Amara was fiercely loyal to the Black Rose and was willing to give up her own life for a chance to fulfill her mission to assassinate  [Ambessa Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa") on  [LeBlanc's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:LeBlanc "Universe:LeBlanc") orders.[[6]](#cite_note-6) Amara's mission failed, but even as she died she taunted Ambessa, claiming that her death meant nothing and the Black Rose would eventually win their feud.

Amara had business contracts with several members of Piltover's ruling council, most notably Councilors  [Shoola](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shoola "Universe:Shoola"),  [Bolbok](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Bolbok "Universe:Bolbok"), and  [Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mel "Universe:Mel"). She would also eventually secure a lucrative hextech deal with  [Jayce](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jayce "Universe:Jayce") after he became a councilor. She was a prominent and influential figure in Piltover, and was invited to and attended the memorial service for Councilors Bolbok,  [Hoskel](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Hoskel "Universe:Hoskel"), and  [Kiramman](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Cassandra "Universe:Cassandra").

Although Amara was a spy for the Black Rose, the people of Piltover remained unaware of this fact even after her death. Amara's death was later blamed on  [Zaun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaun "Universe:Zaun") and used by  [Ambessa](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa") as one of the reasons for the assembly she called in the destroyed Council chamber, where they enacted martial law.

As one of the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose")'s loyal agents, Amara was aware of the their feud with Ambessa and was thus hostile to her, albeit secretly. Under the guise of an aristocrat from Piltover's mercantile clans, Amara persistently requested meetings with Ambessa to the point she found it annoying and eventually gave in. When Amara finally met Ambessa alone, she attempted to assassinate her. The assassination failed, and Ambessa killed Amara.

structure.name: Blitzcrank
structure.quote: *"A SINGLE GEAR TURNING CAN MAKE ALL THE DIFFERENCE."*
structure.background:
### Creation

After a massive chem-spill devastated entire districts of  [Zaun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaun "Universe:Zaun"), a series of [mechanical golems](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Golem "Golem") were sent out to clean up the mess. Designed to remove the toxic waste claiming the neighborhoods, these lumbering golems, toiled continuously in extremely hazardous locations, fulfilling their programming to better the city for the people of Zaun. Eventually, one particular golem was rendered inoperative, discarded as useless scrap. It wasn't until the esteemed inventor  [Viktor](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viktor "Universe:Viktor") discovered the abandoned golem, seeing the potential within its inert chassis. Viktor ran a series of experiments to improve the automaton, implanting a priceless [hextech crystal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Hextech "Hextech") from the deserts of  [Shurima](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shurima "Universe:Shurima") into the forsaken golem as an immense upgrade.

As the machine rumbled to life, Viktor named it *Blitzcrank* after the fizzing arcs of lighting that danced around their frame; an unexpected side effect of the hextech crystal within their chassis. As Blitzcrank was sent down into the most toxic parts of Zaun, they proved more than capable of laboring just like their steam-powered brethren. However, Viktor witnessed Blitzcrank miraculously accomplish tasks with vastly improved speed and efficiency, realizing that his custom-built golem had actually been learning rather than simply laboring.

### Growing Sentient

As Blitzcrank continued to clean up the chemical spills of Zaun, they began to innovate, interpret and extrapolate on their daily directives, serving the people of Zaun much further. Blitzcrank's intelligence would grow so much that they would interact with the Zaunite citizens on a regular basis, something unheard of for a laboring steam golem. Meanwhile, Viktor would attempt to replicate his achievement to no avail, as origin of Blitzcrank's blossoming consciousness became complete enigma to him, but most likely the product of the hextech crystal.

As Blitzcrank continued to learn and grow, concepts such as moderation and nuance remained alien to the golem, as Blitzcrank would persue any effort with their entirety or not at all. This would cause Blitzcrank to overdo or misinterpret requests at times, such as smashing down the front of a tenement to help a single resident who lost their keys. At one point, Viktor dispatched Blitzcrank to clean up runoff of caustic chemicals. Reasoning that the most efficient means to prevent further pollution was to eliminate the source of said pollution, Blitzcrank proceeded to destroy the factory, their lightning-wreathed fists not stopping until it was reduced to a mound of rubble and twisted iron.

A local chem-baron who had owned the factory became enraged when Blitzcrank destroyed it, demanding that Viktor either destroy the golem or pay a steeper price in blood. Viktor became devastated, having witnessed Blitzcrank's growth in sentience and considering them a living being. He eventually concocted a scheme to smuggle Blitzcrank to safety, but discovered that his creation had already left to ensure the safety of their creator as the two parted ways.

### Modern History

Having grown into self-sufficiency, Blitzcrank decided to take up their own mission independent of their creator, looking to resolve Zaun's local problems and better life for its citizens their own way. They would often patrol the city, serving to assist and protect any Zaunites without pausing for instruction. Always searching for any problems in need of solution, Blitzcrank aims to shepherd Zaun down the path of becoming the greatest city in the world. It's also rumored that Blitzcrank has slowly been upgrading their own form, adding modifications to their own body to help further their goal.

While swinging around Zaun with their rocket arms, Blitzcrank found themself at the *Rising Howl,* a massive Hexdraulic Conveyor designed to allow vertical travel between the Sump to the Boundary Markets atop Zaun. Blitzcrank stopped at the elevator to enjoy the noise and unique sounds from the massive machine, curiously surveying the many passengers riding it.

As the Howl began to descend from the Entresol level, it abruptly jammed, causing a terrible malfunction as it painfully braced against the support beams before dropping entirely. As the elevator quickly fell and the passengers screamed, Blitzcrank attempted to grasp onto the support beams and stop the Howl from falling. During the chaos, a young boy almost fell out of the Howl's window before Blitzcrank grasped him with his arm mid-air. Blitzcrank eventually managed to grasp onto the support beams, abruptly stopping the elevator and saving the lives of all the passengers. Once the elevator began to stabilize, the Howl's passengers were directed to medical workers by the conductor, who graciously thanked the golem. Blitzcrank simply responded by saying they were 'fulfilling their purpose' before bidding the passengers a good day.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

### Recent events

Blitzcrank helped out  [Ekko](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ekko "Universe:Ekko") when he was fighting a gang of chempunks, grabbing some of them and blasting them with a wave of electricity to protect the young boy.[[2]](#cite_note-2) After this, he would quickly befriend Ekko and the rest of his gang, including  [Zeri](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zeri "Universe:Zeri"). At one point, Blitzcrank became badly damaged after a violent encounter with a couple of scrappers, causing the detachment of their arm. Luckily, Zeri was nearby to help save and repair them.[[3]](#cite_note-notefromz-3)
structure.appearance: Blitzcrank is a big [Techmaturgical](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Techmaturgy "Techmaturgy") [Golem](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Golem "Golem") build out of golden/bronze colored steel plating. It has a big steam engine attached to its back which it retained from its original creation. Their body is staticly electrified by the [Hextech crystal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Hextech "Hextech") within them. This is most notable around the screws that represent their knuckles.
structure.personality: Unlike other [Techmaturgical](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Techmaturgy "Techmaturgy") [Golems](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Golem "Golem"), Blitzcrank is able to learn and adapt, similar to [artifical intelligence](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/artifical_intelligence). Despite its imposing size and cold steel, Blitzcrank is a kind hearted, altruistic golem and will lend a helping hand to anyone in  [Zaun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaun "Universe:Zaun") who needs it.
structure.abilities:
- **[Golem Physiology:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Golem "Golem")** Blitzcrank is a golem, an artificial construct made of metal and powered by technological programming. After Blitzcrank's body had a [hextech crystal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Hextech "Hextech"), they evolved a form of advanced sentience and are continuously growing their intelligence every day.
  - **[Rocket Arms:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Blitzcrank#Rocket_Grab "Blitzcrank")** Blitzcrank has upgraded their own body with augmentations that allow their arms to detach and launch forward, connected by wires and chains to their chassis. Blitzcrank can use these arms to climb great heights, swing long distances or grab people from afar.
  - **[Electrical Field:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Blitzcrank#Static_Field "Blitzcrank")** Because of the hextech crystal at their core, Blitzcrank constantly emits electrical energy and sparks. Using the power of the crystal, Blitzcrank can launch a wave of electricity outwards, capable of shocking and stunning opponents surrounding them.

relations.relationship_description:
Created in the service of  [Zaun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaun "Universe:Zaun"), Blitzcrank prides himself in protecting the citizens of Zaun from the chemical spill that dots the city's landscape. Far more effecient than their [peers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Golem "Golem"), they were able to clean up multiple spills without sustaining any damage that would have cause for repair.

After a while Blitzcrank was learning beyond what their initial directives had set out for them. They started to innovate, interpreting and extrapolating on their daily directives. As a result, they did far more to serve the people of Zaun, and even began to interact with them on a regular basis.

[Viktor](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viktor "Universe:Viktor") discovered a [Golem](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Golem "Golem"), after it was abandoned because it was rendered inoperative. In a stroke of brilliance, Viktor implanted a Hextech crystal into the machine that would elevate it far beyond the original scope of its creation. After the machine rumbled to life, Viktor named his new creation Blitzcrank after the fizzing arcs of lightning that danced around their frame. It was an unexpected side effect of the hextech crystal.

Viktor is protective over his creation. When it is threatened to be destroyed, he start planning how to get it to safety. Before he was able to enact this plan, the golem already left his facility.
[Ekko](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ekko "Universe:Ekko") and Blitzcrank have fought chempunks together.

Blitzcrank used to help  [Zeri](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zeri "Universe:Zeri") climb the Clocktower of  [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover"). She notes that their arm is no joke. At one point, Blitzcrank became badly damaged after a violent encounter with a couple of scrappers, causing the detachment of their arm. Luckily, Zeri was nearby to help save and repair them.[[3]](#cite_note-notefromz-3)

structure.trivia:
- Originally, Blitzcrank was referred to with *He/Him* pronouns in the lore. In the [V9.22](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/V9.22 "V9.22") revision of the [biography](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/The_Great_Steam_Golem "The Great Steam Golem"), the pronouns switched from *It* to *They/Them* when Blitzcrank gains sentience, meaning Blitzcrank is non-binary.
- In the [old lore](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Runeterra_Legacy "Runeterra Legacy"), Blitzcrank used to run a dating service called ['Blitzcrank's Fleshling Compatibility Services'](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Journal_of_Justice#XVII "Journal of Justice").
- Blitzcrank's lore is seemingly based on [The Bicentennial Man](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bicentennial_Man) by [Isaac Asimov](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Asimov).
- Blitzcrank has a loving fascination for  [Poros](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Poro "Poro"), going so far as to protect them from  [dangerous predators](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Baron_Nashor "Baron Nashor").[[4]](#cite_note-4)

structure.quote: *"The chimes of his footsteps are echoes of change."*
structure.background:
### Early Life

Bard is a [Celestial](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Celestial "Celestial") who existed at the [Creation of the Universe](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Creation_of_the_Universe "Creation of the Universe") within the [Celestial Realm](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Celestial_Realm "Celestial Realm"). Initially drifting aimlessly, Bard found a new purpose when the [Celestial Dragon](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Celestial_Dragon "Celestial Dragon")  [Aurelion Sol](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Aurelion_Sol "Universe:Aurelion Sol") forged [the universe](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Physical_Realm "Physical Realm")'s first stars, producing a symphony of creation. Bard traversed the celestial harmonies of the universe and began to attract new companions called [*meeps*](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Meep "Meep"); celestial spirit creatures spawned from the residual inspiration used to create the stars.

As Bard continued his travel, the meeps alerted him to a world with a unique song of its own called  [Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Runeterra "Universe:Runeterra"), a realm filled with primitive and chaotic music that disharmonized with the rest of the cosmos. While he appreciated its inherent beauty, he realized that this song had become destructive and needed intervention before it can threaten the fabric of the universe.

Venturing into the planet's physical realm, Bard first touched down on the continent of  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") and created a physical form from the trinkets and fabrics of a shawm-player's wagon. He roamed Runeterra for an extensive period, confusing and bewildering any of those he would encounter. On his travels, Bard discovered that many powerful and unpredictable objects, such as the [World Runes](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rune "Universe:Rune"), had mysteriously been left scattered on the planet's surface by some unknown entities, which threatened to disrupt the balance of the universe.

As a caretaker, Bard personally took the task of retrieving these misplaced objects and restoring cosmic harmony in an effort to protect Runeterra from the  [forces that lay beyond](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Void "Universe:Void"). Seeing into the future, Bard saw an impending cataclysm that would span across all realms, anticipating for when he must choose a side to maintain the cosmic balance.

### Modern History

#### Bard Mountain

In the midst of the vicious [Noxian Invasion of Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Noxian_Invasion_of_Ionia "Noxian Invasion of Ionia"), a group of villagers settled around a mountain with a sacred temple at the very top of it. The  [Noxians](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") eventually discovered the village and, in their conquest to take over the continent, sought out an immensely powerful, egg-like artifact of celestial origin in the mountain. The Noxians slaughtered most of these Ionians and ransacked the village in search of this artifact. Meanwhile, the village sage used the powerful artifact to obliterate a group of these soldiers, causing collateral damage to the surrounding area and slicing an entire mountain in half. Bard's instantly turned his attention to the shockwave made by the artifact as he rushed to the site of the invasion.

Flying through the clashing Ionian and Noxian armies, Bard quickly flew up the mountain's steps and grabbed the artifact, taking it to the peak and placing it on a sacred pedestal. From there, Bard blew into his cosmic instrument, summoning a chorus of meeps to witness him as he used his powers to transport both himself and the artifact into the celestial realm away from the hands of mortals who could potentially weaponize it. Those witnessing the event saw Bard's transportation manifest into a three-pointed constellation in the sky, naming the mountain [*Bard Mountain*](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Bard_Mountain "Bard Mountain") in his honor.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

#### Encounters with Mortals

While on his quest to preserve powerful artifacts, Bard would encounter many people who witnessed his mysterious deeds. Some artists and performers considered him a source of immense inspiration for great works of art, while others would be bewildered and confused by his bizarre nature.

According to a travelling balladeer from the  [Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord") who made a stop in  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"), his mother had an ancient  [chime](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Bard#Traveler's_Call "Bard") that managed to attract a stray meep shortly before floating away. After chasing the flying chime, Bard himself appeared and placed the man in a dream-like state, temporarily transforming him into a meep thus allowing him to perceive the universe as Bard does. In this form, he realized the coming dangers that Bard is attempting to avoid before returning to his mortal body.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

A man named Old Gaff claimed that he saw Bard in the sky once, flying across the heavens like a falling star.[[3]](#cite_note-3) The day after, while sweeping the floors at his house, Old Gaff witnessed a similar entity to Bard named  [Byrd](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Byrd "Universe:Byrd"), who created a physical form from his pots and pans before waddling away to a nearby temple as if it were looking for something.[[4]](#cite_note-4) At the temple, Old Gaff found Bard summoning a massive vortex of meeps, all singing and dancing in a beautiful choir as they rose upward before disappearing in a flash of light, leaving only a single chime in Old Gaff's hands.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

### Recent events

Bard continues his journey to protect the beauty of Runeterra by restoring its cosmic equilibrium, safeguarding immensely powerful artifacts that could potentially be misused by mortals in the future.

Most recently on his travels, Bard has taken notice of  [Xolaani](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xolaani "Universe:Xolaani"), a [Darkin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Darkin "Darkin") who has just recently possessed a brand new  [host](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jun "Universe:Jun").[[6]](#cite_note-6) However, it's unclear what her significance to Bard is as he hasn't been shown to intervene.

### Future

At least fifty years in the future, one of the survivors of the Noxian invasion at Bard Mountain lives to become an elderly story teller, remaining on that very same mountain. Here, the storyteller would tell three teenagers various stories and describe the many constellations in the skies that represent significant events of the past; [arrival of the Watchers in the Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Founding_of_the_Freljord "Founding of the Freljord"), the [fall of](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Fall_of_Shurima "Fall of Shurima")  [Shurima](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shurima "Universe:Shurima") and the [ruination of the](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Ruination_of_Helia "Ruination of Helia")  [Shadow Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shadow_Isles "Universe:Shadow Isles"). The final constellation he talks about is the three pointed mask of Bard himself, which he witnessed on that very same mountain many years ago as a child.[[7]](#cite_note-7)
structure.appearance:
Bard is an ethereal Celestial being who created a corporeal form in order to traverse and interact with the physical world.[[8]](#cite_note-8) Bard's true form is able to abandon this body while it "deflates".

This corporeal form appears mystical and alien, but is shaped like a tall humanoid with a stout, heavy build. Bard's "face" is a circular golden mask featuring three identical glowing points, perhaps meant to resemble two eyes and a mouth. He has an enormous mane of white hair and a hefty beard, both of which are tied off at the bottom. A massive ivory horn protrudes from the back of his head. The bulk of his "body" is composed of simple ceremonial robes adorned with numerous bells and chimes. His legs end in points as if they were stilts.

Bard carries a musical horn, brown and gold with jade decorations. Curiously, the horn's opening appears to be plugged by a large jade sphere, implying that the instrument is powered by a force other than airflow.
structure.personality:
Unlike other Celestials that care for and meddle with the existence of mortal beings, Bard focuses more on the 'bigger picture,' interested more in the cosmic balance of Runeterra and assessing any threats that can endanger the fabric of all reality. The only time Bard notices or wholly interacts with a mortal being is if they are involved with some significant event or power that threatens the cosmic balance. Bard simply doesn't care for individual lives and instead is more concerned with the 'bigger picture' and seeing preserving life as a whole.

Bard would never intervene in combat with someone unless they themselves have some significance that could potentially alter the world's cosmic balance, almost completely ignoring anybody and everything that isn't his concern. Though Bard has the absolute best intentions in mind, he can come off as incredibly strange and whimsical in his behaviors, popping in and out of existence without warning almost mischievously.
structure.abilities:
- **[Celestial Physiology:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Celestial "Celestial")** Bard is a Celestial, an entity coming directly from the [Celestial Realm](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Celestial_Realm "Celestial Realm") before transcending down to the [Physical Realm](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Runeterra "Runeterra"). As a Celestial, Bard possesses a variety of different abilities and is essentially immortal. However, as with most Celestials, Bard does not have a physical body of his own and must create one out of many materials and objects. In Bard's case, he created a physical body out of the instruments and trinkets found in a  [Ionian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") shawm-player's wagon.
  - **Cosmic Hearing:** A unique feature to Bard is his ability to perceive the universe purely as music rather than through sight, something unheard of for other celestials. He mainly uses this as a way to not only appreciate the beauty of the universe but also to sense out any threats to the stable harmonies of the universe, being able to sense and disruptions such as the impending  [Void](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Void "Universe:Void").
- **[Cosmic Music Manipulation:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Bard#Tempered_Fate "Bard")** Using a large horn as his main weapon, Bard can completely warp reality by playing music and manipulating the songs that dictate the laws of the universe. Bard typically uses this to freeze targets in place, bind them or transport things instantaneously, but the true extents of his powers are unknowable by mortal minds.
  - **[Portal Creation:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Bard#Magical_Journey "Bard")** By blowing into his horn and manipulating the music of the universe, Bard can create portals of various kinds with ease. Portals created by Bard are capable of traveling through space, time and even to entirely different dimensions.
- **[Meep Familiars:](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Bard#Traveler's_Call_2 "Bard")** Bard has attracted a chorus of mystical entities called [meeps](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Meep "Meep"), mysterious celestial spirits who are derived from leftover inspiration during the [Creation of the Universe](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Creation_of_the_Universe "Creation of the Universe"). Even though these creatures are capable of surviving on their own, they've traveled with Bard for so long they've formed a symbiotic bond.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

relations.relationship_description:
Bard knows about and has met many Celestials on his travels around the cosmos. Unlike other Celestials however, Bard perceives the world in a completely unique way; as harmonious music rather than through sight. Along with that, Bard doesn't manifest in the physical realm through possessing a mortal body like the [Aspects](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Aspect "Aspect") do, Bard instead possesses a collection of trinkets and instruments strewn together into a suitable form. Bard is aware of other Celestials and their affairs in meddling with  [Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Runeterra "Universe:Runeterra"), such as how they had left behind countless [powerful artifacts](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rune "Universe:Rune") on the planet, but he simply questions why they would leave these objects behind and endanger the universe.

#### [Aurelion Sol](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Aurelion_Sol "Universe:Aurelion Sol")

At the [first breath of creation](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Creation_of_the_Universe "Creation of the Universe"), Bard simply drifted across the cosmos without purpose or perception. It wasn't until Aurelion Sol forged the first stars that Bard began to perceive the universe as music, flowing across the harmonies between the stars and witnessing the beauty of the universe.

Bard perceives the universe as musical melodies and first took notice to Runeterra because of its inherent dissonance in the universe's harmonies. Though the music of Runeterra is primitive and chaotic it is also beautiful in its freedom, something that specifically took Bard's interest. However, he also sees the danger of this as Runeterra has the capability of growing so chaotic and destructive that it could end the stability of the cosmos, dedicating himself to becoming the cosmic caretaker of this world and keeping incomprehensible powers out of mortal hands.

Ever since touching down at  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia"), Bard continues to passively restore the balance of powers in Runeterra rather than interfering in major historical events, having no direct ties to major events such as the [arrival of the Watchers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Founding_of_the_Freljord "Founding of the Freljord"), the [Fall of Shurima](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Fall_of_Shurima "Fall of Shurima") or the [Ruination of Helia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Ruination_of_Helia "Ruination of Helia"). Though these events involved powerful forces, they had no major cosmic ramifications and thus didn't take Bard's notice.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

#### [Ryze](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ryze "Universe:Ryze")

Though its unknown whether or not the two have actually met in the past, it is very likely considering Ryze's age and their conjoined efforts in safeguarding powerful magics such as the [World Runes](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rune "Universe:Rune").

structure.trivia:
- Despite the lack of a physical form, Bard is not omnipotent. He can be banished or imprisoned by powerful magics or even meet an ultimate end if a magic equally or more powerful than him were to be discovered.[[11]](#cite_note-11)
- The green ball that sits in Bard's weapon is a harmonic key that splits layers of reality and taps directly into the magical friction that all worlds emit.[[12]](#cite_note-12)
- Though Bard only speaks in musical chiming noises, he is actually speaking in a voice that is incomprehensible by mortal ears. Very few, most notably other Celestials, are actually able to understand him.

structure.name: Udyr
structure.quote: *"I can taste our enemies' hunger for victory. Let them starve."*
structure.background:
### Early life

Udyr was born under a blood-red moon in the  [Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord"). At a young age, he had a deep connection to spiritual magic, greater than any spirit walker in history. However, his powers proved to be a curse to the young boy. Unlike other spirit walkers, Udyr was connected to every spirit, hearing their every need and want. Bombarded by their chaotic thoughts, Udyr's parents sought to find a spirit walker to help him master his powers, but each one told them: spirit walker training was focused on opening oneself up, not closing oneself off. One evening, his tribe would be attacked by the Frostguard, minions of the  [Ice Witch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Lissandra "Universe:Lissandra"). As they slaughtered his tribemen, Udyr became overwhelmed by grief and anger. For the first time, he tapped into his powers with purpose and unleashed an avalanche that buried the marauders. In the aftermath, Udyr would spend the next several years wandering alone, doing what needed to be done to survive.[[1]](#cite_note-UdyrBio-1)

On one fateful day, Udyr aided a Winter's Claw hunting party in battling a troublesome wildclaw. Impressed by his power, they brought him back to their warmother, Hejian, who sought to train him alongside her daughter,  [Kalkia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kalkia "Universe:Kalkia"). The two would grow close, with Udyr showing her how to survive in the wild and Kalkia showing him how to live amongst men. When a pack of diseased rimefang wolves attacked the Winter's Claw, Udyr was affected by their madness, becoming lost to their hunger. He blindly attacked the tribe, nearly killing a child, before being restrained by Kalkia and her mother's True Ice. After the wolves had been slain, Hejian banished him from their tribe. Udyr retreated to the mountains, far from anyone he could hurt, and lived in solitude. Kalkia would occasionally visit the spirit walker, until she had to assume the role of warmother. Despite lifting his banishment, Udyr remained in self-imposed exile, but swore to protect Kalkia and those she loved. However, this would be the last time they ever saw each other.[[1]](#cite_note-UdyrBio-1)

A monk from  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") arrived in the Freljord and sought out Udyr to help him master the dragon spirit within him. Udyr refused to aid the monk, but he challenged him for the right to train with him. The two battled until they reached their limits, but neither ended as the victor. The monk finally introduced himself as  [Lee Sin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Lee_Sin "Universe:Lee Sin") and noted the battle proved they both had much to learn. Lee Sin invited the spirit walker to return with him to train in Ionia, where they have spent generations training to keep the spirits at peace. With nothing him tying him to the Freljord, Udyr agreed.[[1]](#cite_note-UdyrBio-1)

### Time in Ionia

Seeing a kindred spirit in the monk, the two would forge a friendship as they traveled to the Hirana Monastery. By the time they reached the Monastery, they found it besieged by  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") invaders. Udyr and Lee Sin battled the soldiers of Noxus and repelled their assault. After their victory, the two asked the abbott to train them, he agreed, but self-mastery has no guarantee end. The two would spend the next several years at the Hirana Monastery, training with the Shojin Order. During this time, Udyr helped Lee find balance with the dragon spirit and embraced the harmony of the Ionian way of life.[[1]](#cite_note-UdyrBio-1)

Despite enjoying the tranquility of Ionia, Udyr's powers began to plateau. Deciding to return to the Freljord to continue his growth, he would say goodbye to his friend, but not before he was gifted with one of Lee's blindfolds, a reminder to their commitment to self-mastery.[[1]](#cite_note-UdyrBio-1)

### Return to the Freljord

When Udyr returned, he was greeted by a new conflict between the Avarosans and the Winter's Claw. The Avarosans wanted to unite the Freljord under one banner, but Udyr saw that as detrimental to the land's spiritual health, believing that struggle and conflict were needed to keep the Freljord healthy. Instead, he offered his counsel to the opposing side, his old tribe, the Winter's Claw, and was met by  [Sejuani](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sejuani "Universe:Sejuani"), the daughter of Kalkia. Despite accepting his aid, Sejuani was wary of Udyr, having heard the stories of his bloodlust and uncontrollable power. He would earn her trust and mentored the young warmother, watching her become a fierce leader, the two becoming as close as father and daughter.[[1]](#cite_note-UdyrBio-1)

During a joruney to [Winterspike](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Winterspike "Universe:Winterspike"), Udyr pondered a riddle left to him by the Hirana monks as he continued to seek mastery over the clashing spirit within him. He stopped at a frozen lake and was confronted by a massive tiger spirit born from the ice, an embodiment of the rage, violence, and voices he feared most. The spirit attacked him, but Udyr refused to give in to his anger. As he endured its blows, Udyr realized that denial was not the answer. He embraced his anger and unleashed his full power to defeat the spirit. As the lake thawed and the voices quieted, Udyr cleaned his wounds and reflected on who he was. While Udyr had accepted who he is, his struggle to balance with the spirits was far from over.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Udyr was eventually called to a meeting by the other spirit walkers. During his journey, he encountered the Seal Sister, disguised as an old woman, who asked for his help in several impossible tasks. Entertained by his futile attempts, she gave him her blessing in the form of salty bread and icy water. When he consumed them, spiritual magic surged through Udyr, causing him to pass out. When he awoke, he felt new power coursing through him and continued his journey south. When Udyr reached the meeting of the spirit walkers, they discussed a strange spiritual shift they had all felt. Fearing the Freljord was dying, Udyr believed the cause to be the Avarosans. Their actions in unifying the Freljord had deprived it of the challenge necessary to sustain its spiritual health. While some were skeptical of his theory, others agreed, and pledged their aid to him and the Winter's Claw.[[1]](#cite_note-UdyrBio-1)

### Allying with the Volibear

Growing food shortages in the already barren tundra forced the Winter's Claw to more aggressively expand their territory. Weakened by the famine and not wanting to see more of her tribesmen fall, Sejuani proposed allying themselves with the Ursine of the  [Volibear](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Volibear "Universe:Volibear"). Udyr was called upon to aid in negotiations, but the spirit walker did not trust the Storm Bear or his ilk. Despite his objections, Sejuani remained determined in forging the alliance, and not wanting to see her harmed, Udyr agreed to aid her.[[3]](#cite_note-Silence-3)

The Winter's Claw summoned the Ursine, led by the Hounded Lord, a former pupil of Udyr. When Sejuani attempted to negotiate with the Hounded Lord, he deferred her to their god, the Volibear, and summoned him to their meeting. Speaking through both Udyr and the Hounded Lord, Volibear questioned what battle would be worthy of his support. Sejuani vowed to raze the southern farms, destroy their settlements, and conquer the Freljord, pleased with these terms the Storm Bear agreed to lend her his strength, if she asked. Udyr tried to object before Sejuani could accept his offer, but was paralyzed by fear. When the Volibear demanded a sacrifice, Udyr instead offered the war and its dead, enraging him. The spirit walker goaded the god into accepting their offer and the Ursine would join the Winter's Claw in their next raid. In the aftermath of the battle, Udyr surveyed the damage inflicted by the Winter's Claw and the Ursine, noting that they were gaining more power. He confronted the avatar of the Volibear and vowed to protect Sejuani and prevent him from taking her.[[3]](#cite_note-Silence-3)

Some time later, Udyr would take a leave of absence from the Winter's Claw, needing time away from the spirits to strengthen his will.[[4]](#cite_note-4)
structure.appearance: Udyr has a stocky body shape and is adorned by tattoos of the various Freljordian gods on his body. His fists are wrapped in bandages, with his left hand having a headwrap given to him by  [Lee Sin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Lee_Sin "Universe:Lee Sin"). He wears heavy pants with a belt made with prayer beads and open toed shoes.
structure.personality: Udyr is an introspective person, driven by his spiritual powers that grants him a unique understanding of the world. Having grappled with these overwhelming powers since a young age, he embodies a sense of stoic determination and resilience. His demeanor is often calm and reserved, reflecting the solitude he embraced during years of self-imposed exile. Udyr is guided by a sense of duty, particularly towards those he considers family, such as  [Kalkia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kalkia "Universe:Kalkia") and later,  [Sejuani](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sejuani "Universe:Sejuani").
structure.abilities:
- **[Spirit Magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic")**: As a shaman of the Freljord, Udyr possesses a powerful connection to the spirits and Old Gods of the Freljord.
  - **Divine Empowerment**: Due to his connection with the spiritual Gods, Udyr has the ability to extract power from them and use it as his own, so far he has demonstrated the ability to use the power of 4 gods.
    - **[Ice Magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Wingborne_Storm "Udyr")**: By channeling the power of  [Anivia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Anivia "Universe:Anivia"), Udyr can use ice magic, conjure blizzards, and envelop himself in ice and snow.
    - **[Fire Magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Blazing_Stampede "Udyr")**: By channeling the power of  [Ornn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ornn "Universe:Ornn"), Udyr can use fire magic, this allows him to create fire and envelop his body in fire and lava.
    - **[Storm Magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Wilding_Claw "Udyr")**: By channeling the power of  [Volibear](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Volibear "Universe:Volibear"), Udyr can use storm magic, allowing him to conjure storms and summon lightning.
    - **[Metal Magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Iron_Mantle "Udyr")**: By channeling the power of the  [the Iron Boar](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ildhaurg "Universe:Ildhaurg"), Udyr can use metal magic as he can encase his body in durable metal and create shields.

relations.relationship_description: Udyr serves as the shaman for the  [Winter's Claw](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Winter%27s_Claw "Universe:Winter's Claw") and is  [Sejuani's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Sejuani "Sejuani") oathfather. He was once close to  [Kalkia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kalkia "Universe:Kalkia"), Sejuani's mother.

Udyr and  [Lee Sin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Lee_Sin "Universe:Lee Sin") formed a friendship after the latter traveled to the Freljord to learn more about spirits. He traveled with Lee Sin back to Ionia in order to learn more about spirits and aided in defending the Hirana monastery from Noxian invaders. Lee Sin gave Udyr the blindfold he adorn on his arm, a reminder of his commitment to self-mastery.

Udyr can harness the power of Freljordian demigods, such as  [Ornn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ornn "Universe:Ornn"),  [Anivia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Anivia "Universe:Anivia"),  [Volibear](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Volibear "Universe:Volibear"), the  [Seal Sister](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Seal_Sister "Universe:Seal Sister"), and  [the Iron Boar](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ildhaurg "Universe:Ildhaurg"). Despite harnessing the power of the Great Spirit of the Bear, Udyr does not trust  [Volibear](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Volibear "Universe:Volibear"). He respects his brother  [Ornn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ornn "Universe:Ornn"), the Great Spirit of the Ram, far more.

structure.trivia:
- Udyr's visuals in  [Legends of Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Legends_of_Runeterra "LoR:Legends of Runeterra") represents him after returning to the Freljord.[[5]](#cite_note-5)
- [Spirit Guard Udyr](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr/Cosmetics "Udyr/Cosmetics") represents him during his time in Ionia.
- Being a Spirit Walker, Udyr can harness a small portion of power of a dozen Great Spirit animals such as  [Tiger](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Tiger_Stance "Udyr"),  [Turtle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Turtle_Stance "Udyr"),  [Bear](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Bear_Stance "Udyr"),  [Phoenix](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Phoenix_Stance "Udyr"),  [Ram](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Ornn#Call_of_the_Forge_God "Ornn"),  [Lynx](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Monkey's_Agility "Udyr"),  [Boar](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Monkey's_Agility "Udyr"), and more.
  - [Volibear](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Volibear "Universe:Volibear") and  [Ornn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ornn "Universe:Ornn") represent the Great Bear and Ram respectively. As such Udyr can harness a small portion of their powers.
  - [Bear Stance](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Bear_Stance "Udyr") is based off of  [Volibear's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Volibear "Volibear") power and  [Phoenix Stance](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Udyr#Phoenix_Stance "Udyr") is based off of  [Anivia's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Anivia "Anivia") power.
  - Part of his power possibly comes from his diluted vastayan heritage.[[6]](#cite_note-6)
- Udyr is implied to be bisexual, having had relations with  [Sejuani's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sejuani "Universe:Sejuani") mother,  [Kalkia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kalkia "Universe:Kalkia"), and hinted towards having had an relationship with  [Lee Sin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Lee_Sin "Universe:Lee Sin").
