structure.name: LeBlanc
structure.quote: *"I am not looking for counsel. If I wanted a second opinion, I would simply ask myself."*
structure.background:
### Early Life

Not much is known about LeBlanc's early life, except that she was born over a thousand years ago and was uniquely skilled at magic, specializing in illusions.

### Reign of the Iron Revenant

During the reign of the Iron Revenant  [Mordekaiser](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mordekaiser "Universe:Mordekaiser"), LeBlanc was one of the many acolytes who served his empire of death. Having learned of Sahn-Uzal's conquests, LeBlanc believed there was no one her master would not use or sacrifice should it benefit him, and when Mordekaiser raised an army of undead shadows from his past, she watched as he tortured and enslaved his Bringer of Ruin,  [Atakhan](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Atakhan "Universe:Atakhan"), even though the [demon](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demon "Universe:Demon") had been a dutiful servant in his previous life. In the following years, LeBlanc witnessed untold death and destruction as Mordekaiser laid waste to the continent of [Valoran](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Valoran "Valoran"). His reign lasted for centuries, until at the height of Mordekaiser's power, she noticed a brewing unrest among the fractured Noxii barbarian tribes, who had long suffered as a result of the Revenant's tyrannical rule.[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer_of_Ruin-2)

LeBlanc met with the fiendish blood mage  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir"), who was considered a god by these barbarians, and when she gave him an offer they feasted as equals in his home. Here, the pale sorceress and barbarian god wove magic so dark that the wine at their table soured, and the roses withered, vibrant red turning to black.[[3]](#cite_note-VladBio-3) As the Noxii alliance marched on Mordekaiser's [Immortal Bastion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Immortal_Bastion "Universe:The Immortal Bastion"), LeBlanc pledged to neutralize the source of her master's dark power at its source, cutting him from the well of death that fueled his empire. When they confronted him, LeBlanc and Vladimir cast Mordekaiser from the material realm by severing the anchors of his soul from his armor,[[4]](#cite_note-MordeBio-4) which was later hidden in a secret place far beneath his own fortress.[[5]](#cite_note-Thorns-5) LeBlanc and Vladimir also managed to seal the Revenant's demons, Atakhan and  [Tybaulk](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tybaulk "Universe:Tybaulk"), before hiding them away as well.[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer_of_Ruin-2)[[6]](#cite_note-Embers-6)

The Noxii tribes were victorious, and the barbarians laid claim to the Immortal Bastion, believing its wicked power had been locked away for good. Unbeknownst to them, remnants of Mordekaiser's magic still stirred, as LeBlanc had seized her master's dark arcane secrets for herself.[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer_of_Ruin-2) To hide her deception, she too eventually vanished into the pages of history, and by the time the ancient [Rune Wars](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rune_Wars "Universe:Rune Wars") devastated and wiped out nearly every civilization, nearly all records of LeBlanc's existence had been burned away, with her only traces being old, ephemeral legends that a pale sorceress once helped the Noxii tribes defeat Mordekaiser.[[7]](#cite_note-LeBlancBio-7)

### Plotting in the Shadows of Noxus

In the centuries that followed the ancient Rune Wars, LeBlanc and Vladimir recruited many into the order of the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose"), which grew into a cabal of the most powerful mages in all of Runeterra. The Black Rose grew its influence to further the interests of those who wielded such powerful magic, with its rank-and-file members among the greedy, powerless nobility being nothing more than pawns to their ends. The barbarians who had survived the Rune Wars forged a new empire,  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"), in the shadow of the [Immortal Bastion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Immortal_Bastion "Universe:The Immortal Bastion"). As Noxus began their conquests, under LeBlanc's leadership, the Black Rose manipulated its nobility, its military, and even its throne from the shadows, and were secretly responsible for a large number of the empire's most significant military campaigns. Eventually, LeBlanc extended her influence well beyond Noxus, sending her dark magic to twist every corner of Runeterra, including the  [Freljord](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Freljord "Universe:Freljord"),  [Targon](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Targon "Universe:Targon"), and the deserts of  [Shurima](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shurima "Universe:Shurima"). LeBlanc's dark political games pushed Runeterra to the brink of all-out war on numerous occasions, always done secretly and in the name of furthering the cabal's interests.[[7]](#cite_note-LeBlancBio-7)

One of the nobles who joined the Black Rose was named  [Lady Elise](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Elise "Universe:Elise"). LeBlanc, seeing in her a certain cunning and ruthlessness, would approach the poisoned, bedridden woman with the offer of joining the Black Rose. In an attempt to prove her worth, Elise would set sail to the  [Shadow Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shadow_Isles "Universe:Shadow Isles") in order to find an esteemed item for the cabal, only to be mutated into a half-spider creature under the control of  [Vilemaw](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vilemaw "Universe:Vilemaw"), the Spider King. LeBlanc saw this as a opportunity to travel to the Isles in safety, and she would give Elise acolytes for sacrifice and in turn she would bring powerful artifacts from the isles.[[8]](#cite_note-EliseBio-8)[[9]](#cite_note-Shuttered-9)

One such event secretly orchestrated by LeBlanc happened during the first war between Noxus and  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia"), where the Hand of Noxus  [Sion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sion "Universe:Sion") charged into battle and caught King Jarvan I, tearing the crown from his head and killing him with his bare hands. LeBlanc used her magic to disguise herself as a Demacian soldier, blocking the army from rescuing their king until both he and Sion were dead on the ground. Sion was made into a hero of Noxus, his legacy immortalized as one who gave his life for the purpose and glory of empire, and his statue becoming a symbol for all Noxians to aspire towards.[[10]](#cite_note-The_Root_of_Empire-10)[[11]](#cite_note-SionBio-11)

### Reign of Boram Darkwill

#### Resurrection of Sion

During the final days of the [First Demacian-Noxian War](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:First_Demacian-Noxian_War "Universe:First Demacian-Noxian War"), LeBlanc supported the rise of a new Grand General,  [Boram Darkwill](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Boram_Darkwill "Universe:Boram Darkwill"), and after he took the throne, the Black Rose spearheaded the resurrection of the empire's long-dead hero  [Sion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sion "Universe:Sion"), even though his body had been entombed in a statue to honor him for all time. Darkwill could not refuse a gift from his mysterious allies, but upon witnessing how uncontrollable the undead warrior had become, Darkwill changed his mind, ordering Sion to be sealed back up.[[11]](#cite_note-SionBio-11)

Eventually, Darkwill began to refuse the Black Rose's counsel, and LeBlanc realized the Grand General had grown wary of her influence. To regain control, LeBlanc orchestrated a plot to fake her own death, manipulating the young nobleman  [Jericho Swain](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Swain "Universe:Swain") into revealing the cabal and having it appear that the most prominent conspirators, including LeBlanc herself, were executed by his hand.[[12]](#cite_note-SwainBio-12)

#### Medardan Succession War

:   *Main article: [Ambessa: Chosen of the Wolf](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa:_Chosen_of_the_Wolf "Universe:Ambessa: Chosen of the Wolf")*

As part of her plot to control the Great Houses of Noxus, LeBlanc set her sights on the powerful  [House Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Medarda "Universe:House Medarda"), sending two of her best mages—the  [Solari](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Solari "Universe:Solari") Rudo and  [hemomancer](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Crimson_Circle "Universe:Crimson Circle") Inyene—to install Ta'Fik Medarda as her puppet in Menelik's place. LeBlanc also ordered Inyene to begin experimenting with a technique called "magical transference" in a desert laboratory south of [Tereshni](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tereshni "Universe:Tereshni"), which attempted to replicate the tattoos of the legendary rune mage  [Ryze](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ryze "Universe:Ryze"). Inyene began their flesh rune research by raising an army of rune-soldiers for Ta'Fik to defeat his rival in the succession:  [Ambessa Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa"). When this task was completed, Inyene began work on *Nullification*, which would empower one mage at the expense of another, who would be left in a powerless, catatonic state. Inyene's experiments were so brutal that Rudo abandoned the Black Rose and vowed to destroy the project, joining forces with Ambessa to defeat Ta'Fik and Inyene.[[13]](#cite_note-AmbessaBook-13)

LeBlanc and her spies kept tabs on Ambessa as she was in the [capital](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Immortal_Bastion "Universe:The Immortal Bastion") seeking Darkwill's support, and again when she fought Ta'Fik's rune-soldiers in [Rokrund](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rokrund "Universe:Rokrund"). During this time, their attention fell upon a young mage in Ambessa's army,  [Rell Canwell](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rell "Universe:Rell"), whose powers of *ferromancy* were discovered when she suffered a near-death encounter against a [basilisk](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Basilisk "Universe:Basilisk"). After Ambessa's forces defended the city using Rell's new abilities, LeBlanc disguised herself as Ambessa and infiltrated the citadel, kidnapping the girl without a trace. When Ambessa had finally won the conflict and destroyed Inyene's research notes, LeBlanc confronted her in the desert, declaring that her efforts were futile, as the Rose had already made copies and were going to turn Rell into a weapon to make up for the deaths of Inyene and Rudo. Since LeBlanc could not control the Medarda clan, she decided to destroy it instead, leaving Ambessa alive so she could watch her family legacy crumble around her. At around the same time, the Black Rose began experimenting on Rell, forcing her into combat with other young mages. The girl swore vengeance on her captors. The Black Rose welcomed her into their ranks.[[13]](#cite_note-AmbessaBook-13)

#### Invasion of Ionia

After many years of planning, Darkwill finally launched his invasion of  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") in 984 AN,[[14]](#cite_note-Realms-14) which was long-considered his greatest ambition in a list of the empire's other conquests. Still, as he grew older and more paranoid, Darkwill was approached again by LeBlanc and seduced by her promises to extend his life, and LeBlanc once again had control of the throne. She and Darkwill sent  [General Swain](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Swain "Universe:Swain"), the very same nobleman she had manipulated all those years ago, to die on the battlefields of  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia"), and though he survived the Placidium he had also lost an arm and was cast out of the military in disgrace.[[12]](#cite_note-SwainBio-12)

However, Swain returned one day, for within the Immortal Bastion had lied a power that many had tried and failed to obtain: the power of  [Raum](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Swain#Vision_of_Empire "Swain"). Swain had found a way to use Raum to his own benefit, and became empowered by the knowledge, powers, and restored physical form that it gave him. Though his coup took years to plan, Swain and his allies managed to overthrow and kill Darkwill in a single night, after which Swain claimed the title of Grand General and established the  [Trifarix](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Trifarix "Universe:Trifarix") in Darkwill's place.[[12]](#cite_note-SwainBio-12) The Black Rose attempted to stop by his coup by unleashing their living weapons against him, including their barely controlled homunculus  [Briar](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Briar "Universe:Briar"), but Swain was able to escape from her attack and the homunculus was captured by his guards.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

Swain's rise to power concerned LeBlanc, as he could not be easily corrupted nor manipulated like Darkwill had been. To reassert her control over Noxus, she made plans to destroy the new Grand General, working to assassinate him many times over the next few years.[[5]](#cite_note-Thorns-5)[[16]](#cite_note-Powder-16)[[1]](#cite_note-Katarina_5-1)

### Feud with Ambessa Medarda

:   *Main article: [Arcane](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Arcane_(TV_Series) "Universe:Arcane (TV Series)")*

#### Death of Kino

LeBlanc's feud with Ambessa continued for many years after the death of Ta'Fik, and as the warlord continued to lose her allies and territory, she became increasingly desperate to uproot the cabal once and for all.[[17]](#cite_note-203finally-17) Ambessa's son,  [Kino](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kino "Universe:Kino"), became deeply entangled in the Black Rose's web while investigating the death of his  [father](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Azizi "Universe:Azizi"),[[13]](#cite_note-AmbessaBook-13) and he uncovered evidence in [Basilich](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Basilich "Universe:Basilich") which revealed that Rudo and Ambessa had an affair decades prior. The affair led to a [child](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mel "Universe:Mel") who inherited Rudo's magical abilities, and believing that child to be Kino, the cabal kidnapped him. It became quickly apparent that Kino was not Rudo's child, and when Ambessa left Kino to die instead of saving him, LeBlanc killed Ambessa's son. With no allies left that she could turn to, Ambessa set sail for  [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover").[[18]](#cite_note-205blisters-18)[[19]](#cite_note-CL_Clark_interview-19)

#### Conspiracy in Piltover

LeBlanc's agent in the region, the guild merchant  [Amara](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Amara "Universe:Amara"), attempted to assassinate Ambessa when they learned she was after [hextech](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Hextech "Universe:Hextech") weapons to avenge her son's death. The attempt failed, and the Black Rose later kidnapped Ambessa's daughter, the disowned heir  [Mel](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mel "Universe:Mel"), to determine if she was the child they were searching for.[[17]](#cite_note-203finally-17) As a test of Mel's potential, LeBlanc trapped Mel in a special chamber called an Oculorum and guided her through the test, disguising herself as Kino. Eventually, Mel saw through the illusion and attacked LeBlanc, and when LeBlanc was about to kill her, Mel's powers manifested in a radiant burst of light.[[18]](#cite_note-205blisters-18) After this, LeBlanc congratulated Mel, continuing to hide her true face behind illusions as she revealed the depths of her mother's deception, urging her to save Piltover from its destruction at her mother's hands. LeBlanc then recruited Mel into the Black Rose's ranks, gifting her a special amulet that could summon her at a moment's notice.[[20]](#cite_note-208killing-20)

Mel cooperated with LeBlanc during the battle at the Hexgate, and after Mel and  [Caitlyn Kiramman](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Caitlyn "Universe:Caitlyn") managed to strip Ambessa of her  [kaenic rookern](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kaenic_Rookern "Kaenic Rookern"), LeBlanc used her  [magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LeBlanc#Ethereal_Chains "LeBlanc") to ensnare and kill Ambessa. However, Mel suddenly betrayed LeBlanc, using her powers to expel the sorceress's influence from the city, after which Mel took charge of Ambessa's warbands and returned to Noxus.[[21]](#cite_note-209dirt-21) After Ambessa's death, LeBlanc laid a black rose on a pedestal with the  [Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:House_Medarda "Universe:House Medarda") crest, marking the final end of her old rival.[[10]](#cite_note-The_Root_of_Empire-10)

### The Darkin Plot

#### Summoning of Atakhan

After facing an unexpected turn of events in  [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover"), LeBlanc and  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir") began planning their next move. Vladimir was interested in  [Mel's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mel "Universe:Mel") arrival in  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") and suggested focusing their efforts on the "opportunity" she presented them. However, LeBlanc had become convinced that what had occurred in Piltover meant they had "bolder" in their next move,[[22]](#cite_note-Welcome_to_Noxus-22) and despite Vladimir's reservations, she set her sights on something far more dangerous: a [Darkin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Darkin "Universe:Darkin") weapon.[[23]](#cite_note-The_Demon's_Hand-23)

To locate this ancient relic, LeBlanc required the knowledge of an equally ancient being, so together with Vladimir, she took the helm of  [Atakhan](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Atakhan "Universe:Atakhan") and set the [demon](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demon "Universe:Demon") free from its thousand-year imprisonment. The demon, driven by its baseless hunger for carnage and suffering, was given distorted visions of its past, roaming Runeterran battlefields until at last, it ended up in the grassy field where General Khatash-Li and Atakhan had fought in the distant past, with the same table and [deck of cards](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/The_Demon%27s_Hand "The Demon's Hand") he had been playing with his king,  [Sahn-Uzal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mordekaiser "Universe:Mordekaiser").[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer_of_Ruin-2) LeBlanc disguised herself as a wounded stranger and played the game with Atakhan, speaking to it to reunite its old and fractured memories. She gifted the demon sigils to aid it in the game, which were secretly a means to free it from its baseless hunger and force the demon under the  [Black Rose's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose") control. At the final eclipse, Atakhan won the game, but at the cost of its freedom as LeBlanc revealed herself, entrapping it with chains and shattering the illusion around them to reveal their true location: a tiled white room.[[23]](#cite_note-The_Demon's_Hand-23)

LeBlanc and Vladimir told the demon that it would be set free again if it revealed the location of the Darkin weapon. Though it was enraged, Atakhan obeyed the sorceress, painting an inky image onto the wall[[23]](#cite_note-The_Demon's_Hand-23) which revealed an  [Ionian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") gateway into the [Spirit Realm](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Spirit_Realm "Universe:Spirit Realm"). LeBlanc was eager to claim her prize, but Vladimir was more reluctant, believing they lacked the means, as they both had no "host" and the new  [Grand General](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Swain "Universe:Swain") was unlikely to agree to another invasion of the region. Still, LeBlanc believed they could acquire the Darkin without the might of  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"), and after chaining the demon once again, they made preparations to head to Ionia.[[24]](#cite_note-A_Dark_Gambit-24)

#### Trials of Twilight

LeBlanc dispatched Atakhan to Ionia to hunt down the Darkin weapon hidden within the Temple of Twilight. The Temple's return from the Spirit Realm sent the local demonkin into a frenzy, luring its guardian,  [Yunara](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yunara "Universe:Yunara"), away from her post. Under the cover of night, LeBlanc and Atakhan were able to breach the temple's defenses,[[25]](#cite_note-25) before the structure retreated back into the Spirit Realm. Yunara and her new ally,  [Xin Zhao](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Xin_Zhao "Universe:Xin Zhao"), were alerted to the attack on the temple and prepared undergo the Trials of Twilight to reach the Darkin weapon before Atakhan did.[[26]](#cite_note-26)

As they pursued the invaders, Xin Zhao was tormented by [dark visions](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Beginning_of_the_End "Universe:Beginning of the End") of  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") in ruins, his  [king](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_III "Universe:Jarvan III") slain, and the Demacians  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen") and  [Jarvan IV](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_IV "Universe:Jarvan IV") being corrupted by the Darkin. LeBlanc was present during these visions, but during the trial, they were interrupted by the voice of the  [Darkin Glaive](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaahen "Universe:Zaahen"), who discouraged the Seneschal from taking up the weapon just for the sake of victory.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

By the time Xin Zhao and Yunara reached the glaive, LeBlanc and Atakhan had already claimed it, embedding it within the demon's shadowy flesh. The two tried to fight off Atakhan and free the Darkin glaive, but the combined might of the sorceress and demon proved too much and overwhelmed the duo. As LeBlanc subdued Yunara with her  chains and Atakhan bore down on Xin Zhao, the Seneschal reached out to the weapon and communed with the spirit inside,  [Zaahen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaahen "Universe:Zaahen"). Despite Zaahen's protests, Xin Zhao was able to plead with him to use his power to save them. Taking Xin Zhao as his host, Zaahen returned to the world once more and destroyed Atakhan with a single strike of glaive, forcing LeBlanc to retreat.[[28]](#cite_note-TwilightsEnd-28)

Despite her failure to acquire the Darkin and the loss of her new pet, LeBlanc was pleased with what they had just learned: [demons](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demon "Universe:Demon"), like the  one wielded by  [Jericho Swain](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Swain "Universe:Swain"), could be killed. As  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir") looked troubled by the return of the Darkin, LeBlanc simply smiled as she began to conceive her next plan.[[28]](#cite_note-TwilightsEnd-28)

### Recent Events

:   *Main article: [Sisterhood of War](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sisterhood_of_War_Part_1:_Old_Wounds "Universe:Sisterhood of War Part 1: Old Wounds")*

In 996 AN, LeBlanc demanded  [Tifalenji](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tifalenji "Universe:Tifalenji") to return  [Riven's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Riven "Universe:Riven") runic blade back to her, threatening to take her life if she didn't bring it back.[[29]](#cite_note-Sisterhood1-29)

:   *Main article: [Daredevil Impulse](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Daredevil_Impulse "Universe:Daredevil Impulse")*

On the same year, LeBlanc took the form of a tattoo artist and kept an eye on  [Samira](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Samira "Universe:Samira"). Later, she revealed herself to  [Captain Indari](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Indari "Universe:Indari"), Samira's mentor, and declared the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose") had plans for her.[[30]](#cite_note-Daredevil-30)

:   *Main article: [Garen: First Shield](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen:_First_Shield "Universe:Garen: First Shield")*

In 997 AN, one year after the death of  [King Jarvan III](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_III "Universe:Jarvan III"), the relationship between Demacia and the [Nockmirch](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Nockmirch "Universe:Nockmirch") lacked communication thanks to the turmoil of the [Great Mage Rebellion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Great_Mage_Rebellion "Universe:Great Mage Rebellion"). LeBlanc took advantage of this and created a clone of  [Garen's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen") great-uncle Hargold in order to pressure Lord Eldwyn to side with Noxus. Her efforts ended up failing and Nockmirch renewed its truce with Demacia.[[31]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-31)
structure.appearance: LeBlanc is a beautiful slender sorceress with dark long hair, golden eyes and paper-like white skin, hence her moniker **The Pale Woman.** She wears a black, red-trimmed dress which is cut down the middle resulting in a deep V-neckline, along with a decorative golden chestplate, heels, earrings, and a headpiece that points up above her head. On her face, LeBlanc wears golden makeup underneath her eyes which resemble tear marks. LeBlanc wears a seemingly living cape that hovers just behind her shoulders, which has a golden reflective surface on the inside which resembles a shattered mirror, and dark colors on the back surrounding the golden sigil of the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose"). The cape has a tall collar that extends above her head. She carries a dark, glowing red staff in her right hand, which has a dark Black Rose sigil floating directly above it.
structure.personality:
LeBlanc is a deceptive individual, often using her sorcery to trick, confuse, or convince people into serving her and the interests of the Black Rose. LeBlanc is also clever, using all manner of methods to serve the interests of her and the Black Rose. Her ultimate goal is to have control of Noxus, whether publicly or by proxy.

Although she seeks the striving of herself and her coven, LeBlanc never takes the spotlight of her schemes. Instead, she manipulates others to do the dirty work for her, as she convinces them through their little struggles as she sees the big picture.
structure.abilities:
- **[Master Sorceress](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic")**: While it is unknown if she was born with magical abilities or learned the magic arts through training, LeBlanc can harness powerful magic capable of creating  **[blasts of energy](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LeBlanc#Sigil_of_Malice "LeBlanc")**,  **[energy constructs](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LeBlanc#Ethereal_Chains "LeBlanc")**, and  **[item enchantments](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Riven#Runic_Blade "Riven")**. She also has an extensive knowledge of the arcane and the nature of magic itself, which helped her in noticing that  [Rell](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rell "Universe:Rell") had the right type of magic that could stop  [Mordekaiser](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mordekaiser "Universe:Mordekaiser") when he returns.
  - **[Illusion Magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LeBlanc#Mimic "LeBlanc")**: Illusions are LeBlanc's signature magic. She is capable of casting illusions, clones, changing appearances and being at multiple places at once. This magic gave her notoriety and the nickname **The Deceiver.**
    - **[Teleportation](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LeBlanc#Distortion "LeBlanc")**: LeBlanc is capable of teleportation from one place to another.
    - **[Clone Creation](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LeBlanc#Mirror_Image "LeBlanc")**: LeBlanc is able of creating mirror images of herself that act independently but on her command. She is also capable of creating clones of other people as well.
    - **Shapeshifter**: LeBlanc can take on the appearance of others, seemingly at will. When she encountered  [Ambessa Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa") in the desert, she took the forms of important figures in her life, including her cousin Ta'Fik, her protégé  [Rell](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rell "Universe:Rell"), and her lieutenant  [Rictus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rictus "Universe:Rictus").[[13]](#cite_note-AmbessaBook-13) Years later, she did the same to Ambessa's daughter  [Mel](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mel "Universe:Mel"), taking the forms of Ambessa,  [Kino](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kino "Universe:Kino")  [Jayce](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jayce "Universe:Jayce"),  [Elora](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Elora "Universe:Elora"),  [Lady Mion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mion "Universe:Mion"), and Mel herself.
- **Immortality**: LeBlanc is millennia old, being around before the foundation of Noxus.
- **Guile**: LeBlanc is a master in political intrigue and has changed the course of civilizations. She deceived  [Mordekaiser](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mordekaiser "Universe:Mordekaiser") and locked him away in the [spirit realm](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mitna_Rachnun "Mitna Rachnun"), and planned  [Swain's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Swain "Universe:Swain") death on the Ionian battlefields by manipulating  [Boram Darkwill](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Boram_Darkwill "Universe:Boram Darkwill").
- **Magic Staff**: Like some certain mages, LeBlanc has a staff with which she better channels her magical powers. Her staff is tall, black, and red, with the sigil of the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose") floating above the top.

relations.relationship_description:
LeBlanc was familiar with Mordekaiser's past life as **Sahn-Uzal**, and when he returned centuries later as the Iron Revenant, she was forced into his service as part of his inner circle. LeBlanc witnessed the resurrection of Mordekaiser's fallen soldiers from his past, which included the demon  [Atakhan](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Atakhan "Universe:Atakhan"), and she watched fearfully with his other servants as he brutally tortured and enslaved the demon back under his will. In the following years, LeBlanc witnessed his brutal conquests against the Noxii tribes, and when they decided to unite against him, LeBlanc sensed opportunity and joined forces with them and  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir") to steal her master's power for herself.[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer_of_Ruin-2) Unbeknownst to LeBlanc, Mordekaiser had always planned on her betrayal, as he had never fully trusted her to begin with.[[4]](#cite_note-MordeBio-4)

LeBlanc hid Mordekaiser's armor in a place deep beneath the [Immortal Bastion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Immortal_Bastion "Universe:The Immortal Bastion"), where she plans for his eventual return and always seeks out new power so that she may destroy him once and for all.[[5]](#cite_note-Thorns-5)

Atakhan and Tybaulk were  [Mordekaiser's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mordekaiser "Universe:Mordekaiser") personal hound demons who served in his second conquest.[[6]](#cite_note-Embers-6) Having learned the myths of Sahn-Uzal, LeBlanc was aware of Atakhan's past service to Mordekaiser, as well as that of its human host, Khatash-Li. She later witnessed Atakhan's brutal enslavement after Mordekaiser's return from death.[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer_of_Ruin-2)

After Mordekaiser's defeat, LeBlanc and  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir") also defeated and imprisoned his demons, which they hoped to bind in service to the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose"). Although Tybaulk escaped the Rose and has since been tamed by  [Annie Hastur](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Annie "Universe:Annie"), Atakhan remains bound to LeBlanc's will, despite its wish to be free once more.

LeBlanc and Veigar were both forced to work for  [Mordekaiser](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mordekaiser "Universe:Mordekaiser") as part of his inner circle.[[32]](#cite_note-32) She finds it somewhat tasteless that Veigar aspires to be like their former master, believing Mordekaiser to be an unworthy role model.

LeBlanc is the Matron of the Black Rose, whose members include  [Cassiopeia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Cassiopeia "Universe:Cassiopeia"),  [Elise](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Elise "Universe:Elise") and  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir").

While originally treating each other as equals, LeBlanc's relationship with  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir") has soured over time. LeBlanc has been waiting centuries for Vladimir to die so she can take his power away for herself.

LeBlanc tasks  [Elise](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Elise "Universe:Elise") with bearing magical artifacts for her from the  [Shadow Isles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shadow_Isles "Universe:Shadow Isles") and in exchange, she gives Elise acolytes to offer as sacrifices to  [Vilemaw](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vilemaw "Universe:Vilemaw").

[Sion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sion "Universe:Sion") was resurrected under the help of the Black Rose, likely at LeBlanc's command.

LeBlanc assisted Boram Darkwill's rise to Grand Generalship, but when he refused the counsel of her hand-picked advisors, she orchestrated a plot to fake her own death, manipulating  [Jericho Swain](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Swain "Universe:Swain") into revealing the Black Rose and its members so that he would publicly execute them.[[33]](#cite_note-Swain_and_LeBlanc-33) Darkwill believed LeBlanc to be dead after this, and as he grew complacent with his victory she slowly continued to manipulate him, eventually regaining his favor after promising to extend his mortal lifespan. LeBlanc's manipulation of Darkwill made him her "puppet emperor," which continued until his eventual death at Swain's hands.

As a means to solidify her control over  [Darkwill](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Boram_Darkwill "Universe:Boram Darkwill"), LeBlanc manipulated the young nobleman Jericho Swain into revealing and executing the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose") and its members, including his own parents, as a means to fake her own death. Swain killed LeBlanc by his own hand during a high society waltz, and for many years, he believed she was dead.[[33]](#cite_note-Swain_and_LeBlanc-33) In the later years of Darkwill's life, Darkwill had fallen under LeBlanc's manipulations and he sent Swain to meet his death at the [Battle of the Placidium](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia#Battle_of_the_Placidium "Universe:Ionia") in  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia"). Some of the LeBlancs refused to eliminate him for goods, believing that he was no longer a threat to their schemes. This allowed Swain to survive the encounter, which led to him receiving a vision from the  [ravens](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Swain "Universe:Swain"), where he learned about LeBlanc's survival and Darkwill's betrayal. After Swain's takeover of Noxus and the establishment of the  [Trifarix](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Trifarix "Universe:Trifarix"), he and LeBlanc have become political rivals, with Swain ordering assassinations of Darkwill loyalists (many of whom had connections to the Black Rose)[[34]](#cite_note-Katarina_1-34) and LeBlanc ordering assassinations on Swain himself,[[16]](#cite_note-Powder-16) spending all of her time (which is multiplied by her many  [doppelgangers](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LeBlanc#Mirror_Image "LeBlanc")) plotting his destruction.[[35]](#cite_note-35)

Ambessa was locked in a feud with the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose") for some time, and as a result of their feud, LeBlanc killed Ambessa's son,  [Kino](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kino "Universe:Kino"). Desperate and vengeful, Ambessa set out to acquire [hextech](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Hextech "Hextech") weapons to destroy the Black Rose, but LeBlanc foresaw an approaching [calamity](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viktor "Universe:Viktor") that would destroy  [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover") as a result of Ambessa's actions. LeBlanc tried many times to kill Ambessa, first using assassins and eventually enlisting the help of Ambessa's daughter,  [Mel](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mel "Universe:Mel"). LeBlanc did not have a high opinion of Ambessa, believing she was prideful for letting her son die and "blinded" by a "thirst for legacy" to the destructive consequences of her actions.[[20]](#cite_note-208killing-20) LeBlanc eventually killed Ambessa when Mel and  [Caitlyn Kiramman](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Caitlyn "Universe:Caitlyn") stole her  [kaenic rookern](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kaenic_Rookern "Kaenic Rookern"), taunting her for how much trouble she had caused, despite not being a [mage](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic").[[21]](#cite_note-209dirt-21)

As the hidden daughter of a powerful  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose") mage, Mel was kept a secret from LeBlanc until long after Rudo's death. When she learned of her existence, LeBlanc believed that Rudo's child belonged to the Black Rose and began looking for her. During her search, LeBlanc killed Mel's brother  [Kino](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Kino "Universe:Kino") and her friend  [Elora](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Elora "Universe:Elora"), whom she treated as nothing more than collateral damage. Then, she kidnapped Mel and trapped her in an Oculorum to test her abilities. LeBlanc accompanied Mel throughout the test, disguised as Kino, until Mel saw through the illusion and broke free with her magic, completing the test.[[18]](#cite_note-205blisters-18) After this, LeBlanc spoke to Mel while donning a number of forms—Kino,  [Ambessa](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa"),  [Lady Mion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mion "Universe:Mion"), and Mel herself—who were all people important to Mel's past. LeBlanc did not reveal her true face to Mel, nor did she introduce herself by name. Instead, she congratulated Mel on unlocking her abilities as a [mage](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic") and attempted to recruit her into her "new family".

LeBlanc was manipulative of Mel, mixing in excuses and lies as she shifted blame away from herself for Kino's murder. In turn, Mel did not trust LeBlanc, immediately pinpointing her as an illusionist while claiming her abilities as an empath made LeBlanc "afraid" of her.[[20]](#cite_note-208killing-20) Still, LeBlanc and Mel managed to work together to stop the approaching [calamity](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Viktor "Universe:Viktor") Ambessa was about to unleash, and at the battle at the Hexgate, LeBlanc successfully killed Ambessa after Mel summoned her using the special amulet. After Ambessa was defeated, Mel turned on LeBlanc, calling her a "Deceiver" and destroying her shadowy form.[[21]](#cite_note-209dirt-21)

LeBlanc has a special interest in Samira, believing her to be a potential asset to their organization. Samira's instructor,  [Captain Indari](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Indari "Universe:Indari"), is a secret member of the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose") acting on LeBlanc's orders.[[30]](#cite_note-Daredevil-30)

When Rell learned she was a mage after a near-death encounter with a [basilisk](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Basilisk "Universe:Basilisk"), LeBlanc and her agents became interested in weaponizing her potential. LeBlanc arrived personally in [Rokrund](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Rokrund "Universe:Rokrund")—disguised as  [Ambessa Medarda](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ambessa "Universe:Ambessa")—to deceive and kidnap Rell, who was summarily trained and experimented on to enhance her powers of ferromancy to be used as a weapon for the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose")'s ends.[[13]](#cite_note-AmbessaBook-13) Rell swore vengeance on the Rose for what they did to her and the other subjects. She eventually managed to escape, and LeBlanc has been hunting her down ever since.

Riven's  [blade](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Riven#Blade_of_the_Exile "Riven") was enchanted by LeBlanc herself. LeBlanc later sent a small warband that included Riven's old team mates to bring her and the blade back to Noxus.

LeBlanc may be plotting a war between  [Demacia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Demacia "Universe:Demacia") and  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") at the moment, with either one of her Black Rose spies or even a clone of herself having encountered  [Garen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Garen "Universe:Garen") and  [Quinn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Quinn "Universe:Quinn") in the process.[[31]](#cite_note-GarenNovella-31)

It is implied that LeBlanc was involved in the capture of  [Jarvan IV](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jarvan_IV "Universe:Jarvan IV") by the Noxian army, based on the flavor text of 7 [King Jarvan III](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:King_Jarvan_III "LoR:King Jarvan III").

structure.name: Urgot
structure.quote: *"There is only one way to measure a man. Tear him… into… pieces."*
structure.background:
### Early life

Urgot was born and raised in  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"). He became a Noxian soldier and high executioner, or headsman, executing enemies of the state and carrying out missions for the Noxian emperor.

### Transformation in the Dredge

:   *Main article: [The Dreadnought](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/The_Dreadnought "The Dreadnought")*

During [Swain](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Swain "Universe:Swain")'s uprising, Swain needed a way to keep Urgot out of the Noxian capitol, as he was seen as a threat to Swain's plan. Urgot was subsequently sent to  [Zaun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaun "Universe:Zaun") under the pretense of being sent there in order to eliminate a conspiracy against the emperor of Noxus. Urgot was then captured by Chem-Barons and taken to The Dredge, a chemtech prison mine, to be tortured. However, Urgot proved to be resistant to pain, which scared the mine's warden and enboldened Urgot. Urgot had an epiphany, believing Zaun to be great because of its pain, and proceeded to take control of the prison and plunge it into anarchy.

During his reign over the prison, Urgot convinced his fellow prisoners into following him while killing those who didn't. He removed some of his body parts that he deemed "weak" and replaced them with machinery. Eventually, a Noxian agent arrived in the Dredge. He recognized Urgot and begged him to help him escape, to which Urgot killed him. In doing so, he had another epiphany, believing that it was not strength that ruled  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus"), but men. Believing men to be weak, he decided that he would plunge the world into chaos in order to cull those that he did not find worthy.

Urgot started a riot which ignited a chemtech vein in the prison, destroying it and shaking Zaun. Many prisoners were killed in the explosion, but many more fleed to the Sump. It was in the Sump where he started gaining more and more followers, preparing to strike again.

### Son of Ur

:   *Main article: [Son of Ur](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Son_of_Ur "Son of Ur")*

Shortly after causing the Dredge to explode, Urgot destroyed the Black Lanes, a market at the heart of Zaun. There, he killed people that worked for a man called Chem-Baron Crimson, along with Crimson himself. While killing Crimson, four adolescents that were part of the Sump Riders gang arrived in the Lanes and saw what was happening. Three of the adolescents died from inhaling toxic fog while Urgot explained to the fourth how all of the men who died, including Chem-Baron Crimson, controlled the city with fear and deserved to die. He let the fourth kid escape, telling him to spread the message about what had happened there.

### Child of Zaun

:   *Main article: [Child of Zaun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Child_of_Zaun "Child of Zaun")*

A messenger chosen by Urgot, known as The Voice, had been giving speeches and sermons promoting discontent and anger in the Sumps, The Voice preached about a figure he called 'The Dreadnought' and claimed that he would enact justice unto the Piltovans who put the people in the Sumps. Because of the effects these sermons were having on the people,  [Vi](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vi "Universe:Vi") was sent down to the Sumps to investigate. Vi attended one of The Voice's sermons with one of her childhood friends, Roe, and disrupted it, saying that The Voice was just using the people of Zaun to further his own selfish goals. She wasn't able to convince anybody of this, and got ready to leave the Sumps and go back to Piltover, assuming that The Voice and his followers were not much of a danger.

Shortly after this, The Voice, along with his followers, attacked a recently built tower made for Hextech manufacturing. During the attack, Urgot revealed himself to the followers of The Voice. He was revealed to be The Dreadnought that The Voice had spoken about. After deciding that he was not worthy, Urgot killed The Voice. He then released a canister of poisonous gas into the crowd of people that were attacking the tower, calling it a test of strength. Many people died because of this gas, including one of  [Vi](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vi "Universe:Vi")'s childhood friends, Roe. Those who survived continued the attack on the tower, only to be stopped by  [Vi](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vi "Universe:Vi") and  [Caitlyn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Caitlyn "Universe:Caitlyn") along with other Piltovan enforcers. After a battle in which many people on both sides were hurt and killed, Urgot's forces were eventually defeated and Urgot was captured and put in prison.
structure.appearance: Urgot is a large figure, standing taller than almost any human. He has six gold and black mechanical legs with green tubes attached to them. These legs give way to a mechanical waist, from which a green tube attaches to a makeshift mask covering Urgot's mouth and nose. He has the upper torso of a muscular man, paler than most because of a large amount of time without seeing Sun in the Dredge, Sumps, and later on, prison. Instead of a right arm, he has a machine gun attached to a piece of machinery where his shoulder would be. The rest of his torso, save for his head, is covered in tattoos.
structure.personality: Urgot is a determined individual, wanting nothing more than to free Zaun from its captors, the chem-barons, and take revenge on Piltover, which has deliberately ignored Zaun, and in his eyes, let it rot while they enjoyed their luxurious lives. While he works tirelessly to free Zaun, he does not consider himself the savior of Zaun, only a personification of its discontent and anger. He believes that Zaun must be ruled by anarchy to reach its true potential, along with the entire world, and that what he considers "the worthy" will be the only ones left standing. Urgot has made this his ultimate goal, and will not stop until he has accomplished it.
structure.abilities:
- **Mechanical Alterations:** Urgot's partially mechanical body contains parts that prove useful in combat.
  - **Machine Gun Arm:** Urgot's machine gun arm is able to fire live bullets at high speed and freqency, often proving lethal for his enemies.
  - **Shotgun Legs:** Urgot's mechanical legs conceal shotguns that can shoot heavy blasts in an arc around them. The placement of Urgot's legs around himself gives him the ability to shoot these in any direction around himself.
  - **Mechanical Feet:** Urgot's mechanical feet are heavy and capable of exerting enough force to crush many strong and durable objects that regular feet would not be able to damage.

- **Physical Strength:** Urgot is a naturally strong person, able to crush small metal objects[[1]](#cite_note-1) and lift up a person into the air with ease.[[2]](#cite_note-2) Not only does this prove useful for intimidation, but if all else fails, his great strength means that his hand can still do some damage.

relations.relationship_description: Swain saw Urgot as a threat to his plan to take over Noxus, and as such betrayed Urgot by sending him to Zaun to be captured by Chem-Barons.

Vi and Caitlyn were the ones to capture Urgot and imprison him. After a [brief escape attempt](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Warriors "Warriors"), the two defeated Urgot again and reimprisoned him.

structure.trivia:
- Urgot was a big person, but became enlarged by his augmentation.[[3]](#cite_note-3)
- While it is not explicitly said, it is commonly believed that The Voice from the Child of Zaun story is also the narrator of the Son of Ur story (the only surviving adolescent).
- There are many interpretations of the Noxian value of strength and how determine who is worthy. Urgot's unique interpretation of this is that only in [the war of all against all](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellum_omnium_contra_omnes) can the worthy prove themselves and survive.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellum_omnium_contra_omnes)

structure.name: Jack
structure.background:
Little is known about Jack's past, but at one point he signed a contract with  [Tahm Kench](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tahm_Kench "Universe:Tahm Kench"). Known as 5 [Jack the Winner](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Jack,_the_Winner "LoR:Jack, the Winner"), he was a regular participant in boxing matches hosted on the ship known as 7 [The King's Court](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:The_King%27s_Court "LoR:The King's Court"), but later took over the ship for himself, using it as his base of operations for his criminal organization. As The King's Court sailed across the seas of  [Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Runeterra "Universe:Runeterra"), Jack gained a reputation for his fighting business and intimidation tactics.

Jack later travelled to [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Ionia "Ionia") to fight in  [Sett](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sett "Universe:Sett")'s arena in [Navori](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Navori "Navori"), participating in a match against the Boss himself. Jack empowered himself into a more muscular form, causing Sett to feel a rush in confidence knowing that Jack would bring a worthy fight.
structure.appearance: Jack is a large, brawny man with pale white skin, red eyes and a hybrid appearance between a human and a shark, being mostly humanoid only having sharp teeth and a long tail. He has tattoos on his chest, arms and tail. He typically wears a top hat with a piranha symbol in the front, a black vest made from reptilian scales, worn-down brown pants with vertical stripes and dirty leather shoes, though he occasionally wears a monocle. Jack can enter a more muscular form when provoked, where his muscles grow larger to the point where his clothes tear and turquoise veins can be seen across his skin.
structure.personality:
Jack is a cocky and reckless boxer. Although he has a good sense of humor and can be a nice guy to those who are his friends, he is constantly looking for a good fight.

However, when provoked, he gives in to his bestial impulses and is incredibly violent and bloodthirsty, striking fear into anyone within his reach.
structure.abilities:
- **Shark Physiology**: Jack is a member of a race of sharks of humanity which gives him the appearance and traits of a white shark with fangs and fins.
- **Transformation**: When Jack smells blood, he is taken by his killer shark instincts, which makes him take on a larger and more muscular form, attacking his opponents in a brutal and violent way, causing them to lose parts of their body if they survive the confrontation.
  - **Enhanced Strength**: While transformed, Jack gains increased physical strength, being able to break the floor of the fighting arena with a single blow.
- **Master Boxer**: Jack is an experienced Boxer who fights relying on the strength of his fists, he has already defeated and received training from other boxers who have faced him in the past.

relations.relationship_description: Jack encountered Tahm Kench at some point and signed a contract with him. While Jack regularly invites the demon to his activities as a VIP guest, Tahm Kench would provide his patronage towards Jack as long as his deal still holds.

Pablo fought alongside Jack in many boxing matches, with them forming a mutual bond. After Pablo 3 [lost three of his arms](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Five-Punch_Pablo "LoR:Five-Punch Pablo"), he became a coach for Jack and helped to prepare him between rounds.

Jack visited Sett's arena to fight in a match alongside him. When Jack unleashed his empowered form, Sett was impressed with the fight that Jack put up, feeling grateful that he could have a worthy challenge again.

structure.trivia: - Jack is voiced by [JB Blanc](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JB_Blanc), who also voices  [Braum](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Braum "Braum") in all appearances, 2 [Fortune Croaker](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Fortune_Croaker "LoR:Fortune Croaker") and 4 [Laurent Bladekeeper](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Laurent_Bladekeeper "LoR:Laurent Bladekeeper") in  [Legends of Runeterra](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:Legends_of_Runeterra "LoR:Legends of Runeterra") and  [Vander](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Warwick "Universe:Warwick") and  [Bolbok](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Bolbok "Universe:Bolbok") in  [Arcane](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Arcane_(TV_Series) "Universe:Arcane (TV Series)").[[2]](#cite_note-2)

professional_status.occupations:
- Pit Fighter
- Boss of the 7 [The King's Court](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/LoR:The_King%27s_Court "LoR:The King's Court")
- Crime Boss
- Champion Boxer

structure.name: Finn
structure.background:
### Early Life

Although not much is known about Finn's early life, it is heavily implied that he started his criminal career as a teenager, given that he already saw  [Vander](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Warwick "Universe:Warwick") as a threat at the time. After  [Silco](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Silco "Universe:Silco") killed Vander, Finn came to believe that the former was the perfect man to run  [Zaun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zaun "Universe:Zaun") and was more than happy to work for him.

At some point after Silco took control of the undercity, Finn made a name for himself as the boss of the Slickjaws, an illicit enterprise that specializes in assassinations, and became affiliated with several other crime lords who were also loyal to Silco, creating the first generation of  [Chem-Barons](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Chem-Barons "Universe:Chem-Barons").[[1]](#cite_note-107boy-1)

### Border Crisis

After the actions of  [Jinx](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jinx "Universe:Jinx"), Silco's adopted daughter, led  [Jayce](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jayce "Universe:Jayce") to shut down the border between Zaun and  [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover"), trade between the two cities came to a sudden halt, causing Finn to lose massive profits. Frustrated by the fact that Silco was doing nothing to keep Jinx under control, Finn started to lose faith in the former's leadership and even attempted to convince the other chem-barons to join him in a coup against Silco. However, before they could give him an answer, Silco arrived on the scene and unleashed a toxic gas in the air to remind them of the oppressive life that he had saved them from.[[1]](#cite_note-107boy-1)

Although this move convinced the other chem-barons to fall back in line, Finn was not swayed and his disdain towards Silco only increased, eventually leading him to arrive at the Last Drop and have a talk with  [Sevika](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sevika "Universe:Sevika"), offering her a deal if she agreed to turn on Silco.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

### Death

After Jayce led a raid on one of  [Renni's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Renni "Universe:Renni") factories and accidentally killed her son in the process, Finn secretly allied himself with Renni and finally attempted to overthrow Silco with her support. However, his coup attempt failed due to Sevika, who tricked him into thinking she was on his side, and slit his throat with her sword, killing him on the spot.[[3]](#cite_note-3)
structure.appearance: Finn was a tall and muscular young man of  [Ionian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia") descent with olive skin, teal eyes, and straight black hair that was fashioned in an undercut that fell to his right side. His skin was extensively decorated with intricate black tattoos, most notably the word "kill" written in gothic calligraphy across his chest. He also had an ostentatious, gold-colored prosthetic jaw and was almost always seen wearing a bright yellow overcoat draped over his shoulders.
structure.personality:
Finn was an arrogant, self-centered, and greedy individual who was deeply invested in his own money and power. As a result, he showed little interest in Silco's goals and only cared about doing business, leading him to eventually lose faith in Silco's leadership when the latter was willing to sacrifice profits in exchange for a shot at forcing Piltover to grant the undercity its independence.

Finn was also sly and underhand, having no qualms about employing manipulation and violence in order to secure his interests. He also had a tendency to speak his mind freely without care of the consequences and fidget with a fancy, gold-colored cigarette lighter engraved with the letter "F".
structure.abilities: - **Leader:** As a chembaron and leader of the  [Slickjaws](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Slickjaws "Universe:Slickjaws"), Finn was able to dramatically expand his influence as a crime lord under  [Silco's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Silco "Universe:Silco") leadership of the undercity.

relations.relationship_description: Finn and Silco used to have a friendly business relationship, with Finn trusting that Silco knew how to "run an enterprise" after he got rid of  [Vander](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Warwick "Universe:Warwick"). Finn served as a lieutenant in Silco's criminal empire for a number of years until  [Jinx's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jinx "Universe:Jinx") bombing of the Academy Square froze merchandise at the border, causing profits to plummet. After this, Finn convened an assembly of the other  [Chem-Barons](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Chem-Barons "Universe:Chem-Barons"), stating that Silco's control over his henchmen and his empire was slipping. Unlike Silco, Finn was not set on an all-out rebellion against Piltover and believed they should cut a deal with topside to give back the [hextech](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Hextech "Universe:Hextech") gemstone, as that would reopen trade. Silco later referred to Finn as a "parasite" when he attempted a coup against his leadership, looking down on him for being young and naive to the harsh conditions Zaunites used to live in. Finn, on the other hand, believed Silco was old, washed-up, and spineless when it came to his daughter, Jinx, boldly claiming to Silco's face that he would die that day.

Finn referred to Sevika as a "scary lady," recognizing her importance as  [Silco's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Silco "Universe:Silco") right-hand woman and the one responsible for controlling all his henchmen. Finn attempted to bargain with Sevika as he was organizing his coup, playing at her ego and planting seeds of doubt about Silco's faltering leadership and favoritism towards  [Jinx](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jinx "Universe:Jinx"). Sevika considered Finn's offer and later pretended to join him in his coup, before abruptly slicing his throat in front of Silco and  [Renni](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Renni "Universe:Renni"), surprising everyone else in the room. After Finn's death, Sevika called him a "worm," reaffirming her loyalty to Silco.

Renni and Finn were allies who had both become dissatisfied with  [Silco's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Silco "Universe:Silco") mishandling of the crisis with Piltover. After  [Jayce's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jayce "Universe:Jayce") attack on the [shimmer](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shimmer "Universe:Shimmer") refinery killed Renni's son, she blamed Silco for his death and joined Finn in his coup, and they both confronted Silco in his office to have him killed. After Finn's death, Renni was terrified and successfully brought back in line, fleeing the office as Silco spared her life.
