structure.name: Hwei
structure.quote: *"Calm and chaos—leave everything on the canvas."*
structure.background:
### Early life in [Koyehn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Koyehn "Koyehn")

Born into a legacy, Hwei was destined to inherit the Temple of [Koyehn](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Koyehn "Koyehn"). He spent his childhood immersed in the vibrant surroundings, translating his wild daydreams onto canvas. From a young age, it was evident that his visions were not mere reflections of reality; instead, they were fantastical interpretations that turned life itself into art.

Hwei's unique connection with the world manifested not only in his paintings but also in the shifting hues of his eyes, mirroring the ebb and flow of his mind and mood. The temple's art form, paint magic, became Hwei's chosen medium, a medium that influenced the emotions of its audience. However, strict control and discipline were necessary to prevent the art from overpowering mental perceptions and bodily sensations, as those who failed to control it were banished from Koyehn.

Despite the strict precepts, Hwei, driven by an insatiable curiosity and a desire to explore the depths of his power, indulged his imagination. In a pivotal moment, during a demonstration for the temple masters, Hwei's control wavered as he painted Koyehn's sea. Emotions crashed over him, and he surrendered to the beauty of his creation. This awakening infuriated the temple masters who, while unwilling to exile the heir, stressed the weight of his responsibilities. Hwei, haunted yet fascinated by the depths of his power, continued to push the boundaries in secret at night.

### Encounter with [Jhin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jhin "Universe:Jhin")

The tranquil existence of Koyehn was disrupted when  [Khada Jhin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jhin "Universe:Jhin") visited the temple. A bond formed between Hwei and Jhin, as they exchanged creative perspectives. However, the night before Jhin departed, he challenged Hwei, sensing the façade in the pieces he presented to the world. Reluctantly, Hwei unleashed his true art, revealing decades of suppressed emotions and imagination. Jhin, witnessing the forbidden visions, departed with an ominous farewell, stating he would move on tomorrow "to watch the lotuses bloom."

At dawn, Hwei awoke to a series of tragedies. Four historic paintings lay destroyed, the four masters who berated Hwei in his youth lay dead, and the temple itself erupted in flames. In the chaos, Hwei recognized the dark potential of his art for destruction and torment, realizing the horror and fascination that had gripped him in his youth.

As the temple collapsed into ruins, Hwei emerged as the sole survivor, haunted by guilt and the overwhelming power of his own imagination. By day, he mourned with the villagers, but by night, he revisited the wreckage, using his paintbrush and palette to create scenes that captured the essence of Koyehn's crest—the same crest worn over his heart.

Discovering a  [lotus-shaped trap](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Jhin#Captive_Audience "Jhin") amid the rubble, Hwei pieced together the perpetrator was none other than the artist he grew so close to. The thought unleashed a cascade of emotions—fear, sorrow, betrayal, and awe. Faced with a choice between staying with his people or pursuing the answers to the tragedy, Hwei, bearing only his paintbrush and palette, left Koyehn behind.

In the time since, Hwei has embarked on a journey of self-discovery and redemption. He seeks answers by revealing the full extent of his art, tracking down nefarious individuals in the darkest corners of  [Ionia](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ionia "Universe:Ionia"). As he spirals deeper into the shadows, Hwei lights a path, his mind brimming with possibility.
structure.appearance: Hwei is a slender man with pale olive skin and wavy, dark teal hair, usually parted to the left. His eyes change color based on his mood.[[2]](#cite_note-2) He wears a shade of dark aqua eyeshadow.[[3]](#cite_note-eyeshadow-3) He tends to wear simple, comfortable clothes, such as calf-length pants, a loose-fitting tunic, and slip-on shoes. This outfit contrasts dark, muted tones of teal with splashes of bright orange. At least his right ear is pierced in two places (his left ear is obscured by his hair). He is often seen carrying a massive paintbrush, comparable in size to a staff, and with a trail of paints levitating behind him.
structure.personality: Hwei is in conflict with his own duality. Beneath his kind and compassionate nature lies an insatiable curiosity, driving an imagination that blurs reality and fantasy. The internal conflict within him, torn between the light of redemption and the shadows of guilt, shapes his interactions. Hwei's emotional palette, unpredictable and intense, defines not only his art but also the complex relationships he navigates. In his journey through Ionia's darkest corners, he seeks answers and redemption, wielding his magical paintbrush to bring solace and reflection to others and himself.
structure.abilities:
- **[Paint Magic](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Magic "Universe:Magic")**: Hwei possesses an exceptional mastery of paint magic, a unique art form that allows him to shape and manipulate emotions through his paintings. The magical paint he wields responds to his emotions, creating vivid and enchanting scenes that influence those who witness them likewise, he can make his creations come to life.
  - **Red Paint**: When Hwei uses his magical red paint he has the ability to draw and give life to fireballs, lightning bolts and magma fissures.
  - **Blue Paint**: When Hwei uses his magical blue paint he can create and bring to life rivers, water spheres and even amplify his abilities.
  - **Purple Paint**: When Hwei uses his magical purple paint he has the ability to manipulate the emotions of others, he can instill fear, anxiety or even create constructions like claws.

- **Magic Brush**: Hwei carries a brush with him which he uses as a magic wand which he uses as a conduit for his magical powers, with it in addition to painting he can also cast spells with his brush.

relations.relationship_description: Hwei's encounter with Khada Jhin was a pivotal turning point in his life. During Jhin's visit to Koyehn, the two exchanged creative perspectives, with Hwei guiding Jhin through the beauty of his home. There was a mutual respect for their differences, as Hwei recognized Jhin's virtuosity. However, the night before Jhin's departure, the dynamic shifted. Jhin, sensing the façade in Hwei's presented art, challenged him to reveal a genuine performance. Reluctantly, Hwei unleashed the true power of his art, revealing decades of suppressed emotions. Jhin, witnessing the forbidden visions, left with an inscrutable farewell. The consequences of that night echoed through Koyehn, leaving Hwei to grapple with the aftermath of tragedy. The encounter with Jhin left an indelible mark on Hwei's path, influencing the conflicting hues within him.

structure.trivia:
- Hwei is in his early 30s.[[1]](#cite_note-age-1)
- Hwei has no connections with [Demons](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Demon "Demon").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
- Hwei's height is 178 centimeters (or 5 feet and 10 inches) while standing and between 173 to 175 centimeters (or 5 feet and 8 inches) while slouching.[[5]](#cite_note-5)
- Hwei's eyeshadow shade coincides with the hexcode *#146971*.[[3]](#cite_note-eyeshadow-3) This shade has the most similarities with the color "Dark Aqua", which has the hexcode *#05696B*.
- Hwei's name has many different linguistical layers to it: [[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7)
  - It's monosyllabic, which means it is easy to say and put next to names like  [Shen](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shen "Universe:Shen"),  [Zed](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Zed "Universe:Zed"), and  [Jhin](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jhin "Universe:Jhin").
  - It's a name without hard consonants, so that softer sound speaks more to his kinder nature.
  - It has four letters, which furthers the foil/parallel with Jhin.
  - His full name **Lukai Hwei** has a three-beat cadence that refers to the [rule of thirds](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_of_thirds) that surrounds his character.
  - His full name has a contradicting [aptronym](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/aptronym). Lukai Hwei sounds like "look away," when the last thing he wants you to do is look away from his art.
  - Both Hwei and Jhin obtained their full names in a similar fashion. "Lukai" was a top contender for Hwei's first name, but it became his family name instead. Similarly, "Khada" was considered for Jhin's first name, leading to its incorporation into his full name as Khada Jhin.
  - Hwei's last name, Lukai, possibly derives from Hindi लूक lūka [lu:ka:]"a meteor, falling or shooting star" or लूका lūkā [lu:ka:]"flash, flare, blaze or burning wood"[[8]](#cite_note-8).
  - The pinyin transcription of Hwei is hui, which can be written by many Chinese characters. The following are some characters possibly related to Hwei's concept[[9]](#cite_note-9):
    - 辉 hui [xweɪ55] "brightness; lustre; brilliance; radiance; splendour"
    - 灰 hui [xweɪ55] "ash; dust; lime; grey; disheartened"
    - 毁 hui [xweɪ214] "to destroy; to ruin; to slander"
    - 悔 hui [xweɪ214] "to repent; to regret"
    - 晦 hui [xweɪ51] "dark, unclear, obscure; night"
    - 彗 hui [xweɪ51] "comet"
    - 绘 hui [xweɪ51] "to paint; to portray; to depict"
      - Based on Hwei's biography, it seems natural to associate his family name with 绘 "to paint", which represents his (and his family's) expertise. However, in Chinese localization,  彗 "comet" has been chosen to translate 'Hwei'. Considering his first name, the translation is unlikely to be arbitrary and serves a narrative purpose. In both Eastern and Western cultures[[10]](#cite_note-10), the comet is associated with disasters. Furthermore, when examining the character form of 彗 "comet", it composes of 3 vertical strokes and 9 (3x3) horizontal storkes ,alluding to Hwei's preference for the number 3.
  - Hwei's name could be combined with  [Jhin's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Jhin "Universe:Jhin") name to form the Mandarin word 灰烬 huijin [xweɪ55 tɕɪn51] "remaining ashes after burning", 金辉 jinhui [tɕɪn55, xweɪ55] "golden brilliance" or 尽绘 jinhui [tɕɪn51, xweɪ51] "to fully portray".
- Hwei wants  [Sett](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Sett "Universe:Sett") to let him in to his circle in order to look for more information about Jhin, but more broadly about Ionia's underworld.[[11]](#cite_note-eyecolors-11)
- The emotions associated with his eye color can be contradictory, in true Hwei fashion. These are some of the emotions his eye colors could reflect: [[11]](#cite_note-eyecolors-11)
  - **Red:** pain, anger, malicious intent, but also passion
  - **Blue:** pensiveness, sadness, reflection, but also peacefulness and sympathy
  - **Purple:** shock, dread, panic, fear, but also imaginativeness and wisdom
  - **Gold**: despair, but also for emotional overwhelm in general, positive or negative.

structure.name: Mordekaiser
structure.quote: *"Destiny. Domination. Deceit."*
structure.background:
### Distant Past

[Sahn-Uzal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser/Cosmetics "Mordekaiser/Cosmetics") was one of the most feared warlords in the northern wildlands, conquering countless tribes and settlements so that he would one day earn a seat at the gods' table, the Hall of Bones.[[7]](#cite_note-MordeBio-7) Sahn-Uzal's conquests led to much bloodshed and sacrifice, and he was soon pursued by the demon  [Atakhan](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Atakhan "Universe:Atakhan"), who was drawn to the scent of death the warlord left in his wake. Sahn-Uzal managed to defeat the demon, but not before losing his most loyal general, Khatash-Li. Unwilling to let his best warrior die, Sahn-Uzal tasked his sorcerers to bind Khatash-Li's helmet with Atakhan, in a dark ritual that combined their souls into one tortured body and enslaved the demon to his will. Atakhan brought ever more victories to Sahn-Uzal, and his empire grew substantially.[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer-2)

Sahn-Uzal's conquests would one day end, however, and after his countless victories, Sahn-Uzal believed he had certainly earned a place in the Hall of Bones. But when he passed into the afterlife, he was furious to find there was no eternal glory like he had been promised as a follower of the First Truth;[[3]](#cite_note-Origins_of_Noxus-3) only an [empty gray wasteland](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Spirit_Realm "Universe:Spirit Realm") where souls would go to wander and eventually fade away. Vowing to forge the kingdom he was denied, Sahn-Uzal refused to fade, fueling himself with his hatred as he learned Ochnun, the language of the dead. Eventually, he formed a plan to return to the realm of the living and began to whisper temptations to any mortal foolish enough to think they could control him.

### Return from Death

Centuries later, Sahn-Uzal was summoned and bound into a massive suit of armor by a cult of sorcerers who sought to use the conqueror's prowess for their own ends. When they tried to bind him to their will, however, the spell failed, as Sahn-Uzal had given up his former name. His name was now only spoken in the language of the dead:  **Mordekaiser**. After slaying the foolish sorcerers, Mordekaiser forged a new mace from their souls— [Nightfall](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser#Obliterate "Mordekaiser")—and began his second conquest as the Iron Revenant.

Empowered by new necromantic sorcery, Mordekaiser raised the fallen soldiers from his past as shadows bound to his will, among them his old demonic servant, Atakhan.[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer-2) At some point, Mordekaiser also bound a fire demon,  [Tybaulk](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tybaulk "Universe:Tybaulk"), to his service,[[8]](#cite_note-Embers-8) and amassed a circle of acolytes who would do his bidding. Mordekaiser also captured a [yordle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Yordle "Yordle"),  [Veigar](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Veigar "Universe:Veigar"), and enslaved him to his service by torturing him until his mind eventually broke.[[9]](#cite_note-VeigarBio-9) With an army of dark forces at his command, Mordekaiser forged an empire that lasted for generations, bringing with it untold death and destruction. At the center of his empire, Mordekaiser raised the [Immortal Bastion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Immortal_Bastion "Universe:The Immortal Bastion"), which was both a symbol of his power and also held a darker, secret purpose.

After many years, Mordekaiser's reign of terror would finally come to an end when he was betrayed by one of the acolytes from his inner circle,  [LeBlanc](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:LeBlanc "Universe:LeBlanc"), who joined forces with the hemomancer  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir") and conspired with the Noxii tribes to seal Mordekaiser away, seizing his fortress and demonic servants for herself. Unbeknownst to LeBlanc, her betrayal had always been a part of Mordekaiser's plan, and after his second death he found himself surrounded not by an empty wasteland but by a grand and eternal  [Afterworld](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser#Realm_of_Death "Mordekaiser"), which he had constructed of blocks and mortar molded from the very souls he had slain on his second conquest. Mordekaiser called his Afterworld *"[Mitna Rachnun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mitna_Rachnun "Universe:Mitna Rachnun")"* and went to rule over the unfading souls as lord and master for all eternity.[[7]](#cite_note-MordeBio-7)[[6]](#cite_note-Final_Reign-6)

### Recent History

Mordekaiser remains in Mitna Rachnun, biding his time so that he may return once more to begin his final reign over Runeterra. LeBlanc continues to watch his armor to prevent the seal from breaking, and continuously seeks out more power to do battle against the Iron Revenant should he return one day.[[10]](#cite_note-Thorns-10) Mordekaiser still has some acolytes in Runeterra, such as Januk[[1]](#cite_note-Curator's_Gambit-1) and  [Lord Mallat](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mallat "Universe:Mallat"). His fortress, the Immortal Bastion, remains a symbol of power across the continent, eventually serving as the seat of power for the empire of  [Noxus](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus").
structure.appearance:
Mordekaiser appears to be a massive suit of animated armor with no visible trace of humanity save for two spectral teal eyes. Rigid and angular, the black metal plates that comprise his form are enormous, featuring three large spikes on each shoulder and two "horns" from the helmet. The armor seems to pulse and glow with the bright teal color of necromantic magic. He also wears a dark red loin cloth and a tri-pointed cape, faded and tattered.

His oversized mace,  [Nightfall](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser#Obliterate "Mordekaiser"), is colored identically to his armor and is spiked outward in four directions.
structure.personality: Mordekaiser is a brutal warlord that desires to conquer everything and destroy all those that stands in his way. Having died twice before, he does not fear death, as that would merely send him back to his own hellish dominion.
structure.abilities:
- **[Necromancy](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser#Death's_Grasp "Mordekaiser"):** After dying, Sahn-Uzal was placed inside a foggy plane of the Spirit World. There he learned Ochnun, the language of the dead, permitting him to pass through the veil. Now with the new name of  **Mordekaiser**, the Iron Revenant can control spectral energy to his desires.
  - **Self-Resurrection:** Mordekaiser is able to bind his own soul in his suit of armor, allowing him to continue in the physical world.
  - **Soul-Bidding:** When someone is slain by Mordekaiser or one under his control, their spirits are bound to his will, becoming servants in his army, regardless of their previous alliances.
  - **Soul Constructs:** Mordekaiser can collect the soul of his victims and twist them in to whatever shape he desires. Many of his belongings, such as his armor and his mace, are made from the souls of the dead.
- **Metallic Armor:** Mordekaiser often posses a enchanted armor that allows him to exist in the physical plane, and destroy his foes with overwhelming force.
- **[Mitna Rachnun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser#Realm_of_Death "Mordekaiser"):** By sheer force of will, Mordekaiser has been able to create his own [realm of the dead](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mitna_Rachnun "Universe:Mitna Rachnun") where he and those he controls go after leaving the physical plane. This allows him a home base that no army can reach.

relations.relationship_description: Atakhan was a demon who was drawn by  [Sahn-Uzal's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser/Cosmetics "Mordekaiser/Cosmetics") bloody conquests, hoping to feed on the misery, terror, and death that followed in his wake. Atakhan eventually attacked Sahn-Uzal, but was defeated and later bound to his service when Sahn-Uzal forcibly melded the demon with his most loyal general, Khatash-Li. Atakhan served Sahn-Uzal dutifully and violently, and became known as the warlord's "Bringer of Ruin." When Sahn-Uzal eventually died, Atakhan was free to roam Runeterra once again. When Sahn-Uzal returned as  **Mordekaiser**, he summoned Atakhan as a shadow from his past, gifting the demon a new form to do his bidding. However, Atakhan had grown used to its freedom and refused to serve him, so it was once again bound to its master's will by brutal force. After Mordekaiser was defeated by  [LeBlanc](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:LeBlanc "Universe:LeBlanc") and  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir"), they acquired Atakhan's helm and used magic to bind the demon to the service of the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose").[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer-2)

LeBlanc was one of Mordekaiser's acolytes during his reign as the Iron Revenant, who bore witness to his second enslavement of  [Atakhan](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Atakhan "Universe:Atakhan") and his brutal conquests across Valoran. LeBlanc would eventually conspire against her master and was instrumental to his downfall, which she accomplished together with  [Vladimir](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Vladimir "Universe:Vladimir"). Unbeknownst to LeBlanc, Mordekaiser had planned on her betrayal, suggesting he never fully trusted her to begin with. She is preparing to banish him when he returns to keep the [Immortal Bastion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Immortal_Bastion "Universe:The Immortal Bastion") for herself.

Mordekaiser tortured Veigar and forced the [yordle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Yordle "Universe:Yordle") to serve him until his defeat. Mordekaiser's reign had a lasting influence on Veigar, who would continue to mimic the revenant's behavior long after his downfall.

Vladimir was considered a god among the barbarian tribes in eastern Valoran, until he was approached by  [LeBlanc](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:LeBlanc "Universe:LeBlanc") and recruited to her conspiracy to end Mordekaiser's dark reign. Their plan to seal Mordekaiser succeeded, and they stole the [Immortal Bastion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Immortal_Bastion "Universe:The Immortal Bastion") and Mordekaiser's demonic servants for themselves. Currently, Vladimir owns a defaced statue of Mordekaiser, which is displayed prominently in his home.[[11]](#cite_note-Art-11) Mordekaiser, in turn, does not think highly of Vladimir, referring to him as a "stain splattered on the pages of history."

Prior to Mordekaiser's defeat, Tybaulk was one of his demonic servants who wreaked havoc on everything that stood in his master's way.[[8]](#cite_note-Embers-8) More recently, Tybaulk has been tamed by the will of  [Annie Hastur](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Annie "Universe:Annie"), so it is unknown if he still remains loyal to Mordekaiser.

Though his feats as Sahn-Uzal have largely faded into myth, Mordekaiser's second reign as the Iron Revenant made him a well-known and dreaded figure across Noxus, with Noxians learning about him in history books and defacing his many statues in the old city, while many fear the very mention of his name.[[10]](#cite_note-Thorns-10)[[12]](#cite_note-LeBlancBio-12) Mordekaiser's fortress, the [Immortal Bastion](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Immortal_Bastion "Universe:The Immortal Bastion"), serves as the Noxian seat of power, with both the  [Trifarix](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Trifarix "Universe:Trifarix") and the  [Black Rose](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Black_Rose "Universe:Black Rose") operating within the fortress walls.
Given Sahn-Uzal's faith in the Hall of Bones, it's safe to say his culture did not have a Kindred myth; which would explain why he was never claimed by them.

Januk [tasked](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Curator%27s_Gambit "Universe:The Curator's Gambit")  [Ezreal](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Ezreal "Universe:Ezreal") to obtain the [Elixir of Uloa](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Elixir_of_Uloa "Universe:The Elixir of Uloa") with which he would be able to resurrect Mordekaiser. However, Ezreal intentionally gave him a fake vial and left Januk while stealing an old Ochnun bell.

While it's not directly confirmed, it has been implied Mordekaiser may have a certain level of awareness about Viego's actions and is waiting to benefit from them once he decides to return.[[13]](#cite_note-13) It has been confirmed if they were to directly fight, Mordekaiser would likely win.

structure.trivia:
- Mordekaiser is at least 1500 years old, but due to the unknown period of time between Sahn-Uzal's death and his resurrection, Mordekaiser's actual age is unknown.
  - Mordekaiser was resurrected around 400 BN.[[14]](#cite_note-Realms-14) This event is stated to have occurred "centuries" after Sahn-Uzal's first reign and death,[[2]](#cite_note-Bringer-2) which places his origin some time before 600 BN.
  - According to his writer and ex-Rioter [Michael Yichao](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Michael_Yichao "Michael Yichao") on Mordekaiser Mains discord, Mordekaiser may have been living during the ancient  [Shuriman](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shurima "Universe:Shurima") Empire.
- Mordekaiser defied death by sheer force of will because he refused to accept the reality around him. He gained necromantic powers by teaching himself Ochnun in the death realm, which allowed him to speak beyond the veil of death to deceive mortals into resurrecting him.
- Mordekaiser's quote  *"Destiny. Domination. Deceit."* would subconsciously inspire Noxus' [Principles of Strength](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus#Law_of_the_Empire "Universe:Noxus"): Vision, Might, and Guile.
- Sahn-Uzal's ancient one-on-one duels influenced  [Noxian](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Noxus "Universe:Noxus") culture and formed the basis for the sport known as  [Reckoning](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Reckoners "Universe:Reckoners").[[15]](#cite_note-Sahn-Uzal_Reckoning-15)[[16]](#cite_note-The_Reckoners-16)
- [Mitna Rachnun](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Mitna_Rachnun "Universe:Mitna Rachnun"), also known as Mordekaiser's  [Realm of Death](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser#Realm_of_Death "Mordekaiser"), is a portion of the Spirit Realm that Mordekaiser has corrupted for his own uses.[[17]](#cite_note-17)
- Mordekaiser's story references [Dracula](https://Castlevania.fandom.com/wiki/Dracula) from *[Castlevania](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castlevania)* and [Sigma](https://megamanwiki.com/wiki/Sigma) from *[Megaman X](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megaman_X)*.
- Mordekaiser's mace being called  [Nightfall](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Mordekaiser#Obliterate "Mordekaiser") references [the eponymous band](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightfall_(band)) as well as [the eponymous song](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IoyToHOWSV8) by [Blind Guardian](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blind_Guardian).
  - Both it and a child's drawing of old Mordekaiser (standing next to a burning house with 'I ♥ My Daddy' written at the top) can be seen in [the game's Mac Version trailer](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qbPuz48CFnw).
- The Hall of Bones in Mordekaiser's [biography](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Iron_Revenant "Universe:The Iron Revenant") may be a reference to [Valhalla](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valhalla) ("Hall of the Slain") in [Norse mythology](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norse_mythology).
  - Another name for the Hall of Bones is "Osrachnun." The ancient Noxii tribes believed a seat at the gods' table was promised to followers of the First Truth: *"The strong eat, and the weak have nothing to offer their gods."*[[5]](#cite_note-The_Demon's_Hand-5)[[18]](#cite_note-Sahn-Uzal_Mordekaiser-18)
  - The empty gray wasteland Mordekaiser ended up in instead of the Hall of Bones likely references [Sheol](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheol), a dark realm where both the righteous and the wicked will go to after death, in [Hebrew mythology](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_mythology). It is also similar to the Underworld in [Mesopotamian mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Mesopotamian_underworld).
- [The Elixir of Uloa](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:The_Elixir_of_Uloa "Universe:The Elixir of Uloa") has the properties to resurrect Mordekaiser.
- His armor has two layers of metal, a black iron skeletal under-layer and the tarnished proto-Noxian armour on top of that.[[19]](#cite_note-19)
- As revealed in  [Rell's](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Rell "Rell") lore [live Q&A](https://youtu.be/ukA99Hx9EJw), Mordekaiser's armor is made from souls and iron.
- Mordekaiser's design is similar to [Eredin](https://thewitcher3.wiki.fextralife.com/Eredin) from *[The Witcher](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Witcher)* and [Sauron](https://tolkiengateway.net/wiki/Sauron) from *[The Lord of the Rings](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series))*.

structure.name: Rumble
structure.quote: *"Ugh, it's gonna take forever to scrape your face off my suit!"*
structure.background:
### Early Life

Born in  [Bandle City](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Bandle_City "Universe:Bandle City"), Rumble was bullied by his fellow yordles when he was younger, making him irritable and scrappy. He found solace in tinkering using discarded junk in the junkyard.

Rumble's teachers recommended him to go to  [Heimerdinger](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Heimerdinger "Universe:Heimerdinger")'s Yordle Academy of Science and Progress in  [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Piltover "Universe:Piltover"), but Rumble rejected it, seeing Heimerdinger and his staff as sellouts for wasting the potential of yordle technology for humans. However, this did not stop him from trying to greet Heimerdinger's human students whom had travelled to Bandle City. Unfortunately for him, the interaction culminated in him getting beaten up and hearing how much of an embarrassment he was to "enlightened" yordles like Heimerdinger. The next day, Rumble left Bandle City for several months. He returned with his mech Tristy, that he had constructed from scavenged junk, eager to show what yordle technology was capable of.

### Shuriman Trash

:   *Main article: [Shuriman Trash](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Shuriman_Trash "Shuriman Trash")*

Disguising himself as an elderly merchant, Rumble visited [Nashramae](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Nashramae "Nashramae"),  [Shurima](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Shurima "Universe:Shurima") to purchase wares from the other merchants. His cart was bumped into by a Shuriman cripple named Anaktu, whom was being bullied by the governor's stepson Kesu Rance and his friends. Initially indifferent towards Anaktu, Rumble took offense when Kesu began insulting him as well. He walked to his stall to activate Tristy in order to intimidate the bullies, but the mech began to malfunction, causing the bullies to attack the mech and taunt Rumble. Anaktu grabbed a mace from Rumble's stall to defend him, before swinging it at the bullies. As Kesu was about to attack him, Rumble came to Anaktu's defense with an  [electrified harpoon](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Rumble#Electro_Harpoon "Rumble"). Warming up to Anaktu, Rumble invited him to ride on his mech, letting him activate the  [flamespitter](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Rumble#Flamespitter "Rumble") and inviting him to watch his  [Equalizer](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Rumble#The_Equalizer "Rumble") fire its rockets, barring off Kesu's escape route. Anaktu asked Kesu why he was bullying him, with the latter confessing he wanted to impress his Noxian father. With Rumble's glamour expiring, the yordle threatened Kesu with a harpoon, demanding him to apologize to him. Kesu tried to apologise for his bullying, but Rumble told him that he disrespected junk and how it had so much potential. After Kesu dumbfoundedly apologized, Rumble decided to return to Bandle City. Anaktu offered to return his mace, but Rumble let him keep it out of respect towards his appreciation of junk.
structure.appearance: Rumble disguises himself as a travelling merchant. He wears a cape and vest with short sleeves. He wears very large boots which disappear beneath his vest. Like most male [Yordles](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Yordle "Yordle"), he is covered in fur.
structure.personality: Because he was bullied by others, it made him irritable, resourceful and scrappy, and make him build a mech so that no one would look down on him again.
structure.abilities:
- **Yordle Physiology:** Rumble is a Yordle, a being coming from the [Spirit Realm](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Spirit_Realm "Spirit Realm") and possesses several abilities natural of his species.
  - **Immortality:** Being spiritual beings, Yordles don't age the same way as normal humans, and they can't normally die.
  - **Yordle Magic:** Just like any [Yordle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Yordle "Yordle"), Rumble is capable of performing yordle magic, which he utilizes in tandem with his skills as an inventor.

relations.relationship_description: Rumble is a resourceful [yordle](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Yordle "Yordle") mechanic who is convinced [Bandle City](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Bandle_City "Bandle City") can be (if not is already) more technologically advanced than human nations (especially [Piltover](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Piltover "Piltover"), where  [Heimerdinger](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Heimerdinger "Universe:Heimerdinger") 'sold out')

To prove that he is more technologically advanced than human nations, he built himself a mechanized suit from junkyard scrap (named  [Tristy](https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Universe:Tristana "Universe:Tristana") after the one he has a crush on).
